Entry: IX = window frame; HL = cursor position.
Exit: Fc = 0, line cleared; HL unchanged.
Error: Fc = 1 when HL is outside the window (nothing written).
Changes: AF, BC, E.

15314.synopsis:
Entry inside ClearEOL: fills the line from the cursor to the window's last column with the
character and attribute in BC. When the window's grey or ungrey open flag is set (during +G
or -G) it rewrites the existing characters with their attribute greyed or ungreyed instead;
open-flag bits 6 and 5 select the pattern fill that ClearEOWm uses.
Entry: IX = window frame; HL = cursor position; C = character; B = attribute.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1; HL unchanged.
Error: Fc = 1 when HL is outside the window (nothing written).
Changes: AF, BC, E.

15418.synopsis:
Scrolls the window up one line: copies each line from the second to the last one line up
(su_2), clears the last line (ClearEOL), then moves the cursor up one line unless that would
leave the window.
Entry: IX = window frame; HL = cursor position.
Exit: Fc = 0; H = the cursor's line, one less when still inside the window; L unchanged.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, H.

15444.synopsis:
Step of ScrollUp: copies line H of the window onto line H-1 (from the first column, the
window's width plus one character, attributes included) when both lines are inside it.
Entry: IX = window frame; H = source line.
Exit: Fc = 0, line copied; Fc = 1, line H or H-1 is outside the window (nothing copied); H
unchanged.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, L.

15472.synopsis:
Scrolls the window down one line: copies each line from the last but one to the first one
line down (sd_2), clears the first line (ClearEOL), then moves the cursor down one line
unless that would leave the window.
Entry: IX = window frame; HL = cursor position.
Exit: Fc = 0; H = the cursor's line, one more when still inside the window; L unchanged.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, H.

15498.synopsis:
Step of ScrollDown: copies line H of the window onto line H+1 (from the first column, the
window's width plus one character, attributes included) when both lines are inside it.
Entry: IX = window frame; H = source line.
Exit: Fc = 0, line copied; Fc = 1, line H or H+1 is outside the window (nothing copied); H
unchanged.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, L.

15526.synopsis:
Returns the window's bottom-right position.
Entry: IX = window frame.
Exit: H = last line (wdf_endy); L = last column (wdf_endx).
Changes: HL.

15533.synopsis:
Returns the fill used to clear the window: character 0 with the window's reverse, flash,
grey and underline attributes.
Entry: IX = window frame.
Exit: B = attribute (wdf_flagsLo masked); C = 0.
Changes: AF, BC.

15542.synopsis:
Draws the window's side borders: a vertical bar (character $18A) one character left and one
character right of every line. When the brackets flag is set, the first line gets the shelf
brackets ($1BE on the left, $1BF on the right) instead of the bars.
Entry: IX = window frame; C = the window's open flags (wdf_OpenFlags).
Changes: AF, B, HL.

15603.synopsis:
Checks that the cursor position is inside the window: tests the line (NewYValid) and then
falls into NewXValid for the column.
Entry: IX = window frame; H = line; L = column byte offset.
Exit: Fc = 0 when both are inside the window; Fc = 1 otherwise.
Changes: AF.

15661.synopsis:
Sounds two bleeps (OS_Blp with A = 2, B = 5, C = 10).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC.

15670.synopsis:
Bell (BEL) of the screen driver: sounds one bleep (OS_Blp with A = 1, B = 0, C = 20).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC.

15695.synopsis:
Restores the screen from a file: sets E = 0 (read) and falls into SrScreen, which binds the
screen in, reads 8 blocks of type $A3 of 228 bytes each (the 114 characters of a line after
the first 10) into the screen lines with RdHeaderedData, redraws the OZ window (DrawOZwd)
and restores the S1 binding.
Entry: the filing-system stream that RdHeaderedData reads is set up by the caller.
Exit: Fc = 0, screen restored.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Type when a block has the wrong type).

15699.synopsis:
Saves the screen to a file: sets E = $FF (write) and falls into SrScreen, which binds the
screen in and writes the 8 lines as blocks of type $A3 of 228 bytes each (the 114 characters
after the first 10) with WrHeaderedData, redraws the OZ window and restores the S1 binding.
Entry: the filing-system stream that WrHeaderedData writes is set up by the caller.
Exit: Fc = 0, screen saved.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

15737.synopsis:
Reads or writes one headered block for SrScreen: WrHeaderedData when E = $FF, RdHeaderedData
when E = 0.
Entry: E = $FF (write) or 0 (read); A = block type; BC = length; HL = local address.
Exit: Fc = 0, block transferred.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Keeps: DE.

10.synopsis:
OS_Sci: alters the screen information, the base addresses of LORES0, LORES1, HIRES0, HIRES1
and the screen base file. The address in BHL is reduced to the Blink register value by the
reason's granularity (OSSciTable), the old value is read from the soft copies at $046x and
$047x and returned, and the new one is written when B is not 0. Setting the screen base also
reinitialises the screen: windows 7 and 8, the application window and the OZ window are set
up again.
Entry: A = reason (SC_LR0, SC_LR1, SC_HR0, SC_HR1 or SC_SBR); B = 0 to read, otherwise BHL =
new address.
Exit: Fc = 0; BHL = old address (in the caller's OS frame).
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (reason not 1-5).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

206.synopsis:
Key2MetaTable's character list for the special keys: a mask byte (7) and the 8 meta letters
" ETX?MIH" (Enter, Tab, Del, Esc, Menu, Index, Help per the source). Key2Meta masks the key
code with the mask byte and picks the letter.

215.synopsis:
Key2MetaTable's character list for control characters: a mask byte ($1F) and 32 meta
characters, "=", "A"-"Z", "[", "\", "]", the pound sign ($A3) and "-". Key2Meta masks the
key code with the mask byte and picks the character.

248.synopsis: Key2MetaTable's character list for the CTRL key itself: a mask byte (0) and "C".

250.synopsis: Key2MetaTable's character list for the ALT key itself: a mask byte (0) and "A".

252.synopsis:
End of Key2MetaTable (the source checks that the table stays in one page). The same address
starts CLI2KeyTable, used by CLIchar2key: a length byte (24) and 12 pairs of a letter after
"~" in a CLI string and its key code (D down, E enter, H help, I index, L left, M menu, R
right, T tab, U up, X del, C ctrl, A alt).

407.synopsis:
Common exit of the OS_Epr calls (entry inside ozFleEprFindFile): returns BHL to the caller
through PutOSFrame_BHL and, when Fz = 1, sets Fz in the caller's frame (ret_fz).
Entry: BHL = value to return; Fz = 1 to return Fz = 1; IY = OS frame.
Exit: frame B, H, L set; frame Fz set when Fz = 1 (it is 0 by default).

1239.synopsis:
Clears bits in the Blink COM register: complements the mask, ANDs it into the soft copy
BLSC_COM with interrupts disabled (chgcom_1), writes the soft copy and BL_COM, and enables
interrupts again.
Entry: A = bits to clear.
Exit: A = new COM value; interrupts enabled.
Changes: AF.

1253.synopsis:
Shared step of OrCom and AndCom: disables interrupts (so that slot polling cannot run while
a byte is blown) and reads the COM soft copy.
Entry: A = new bits.
Exit: B = new bits; A = BLSC_COM; interrupts disabled.
Changes: A, B.

1259.synopsis:
Makes a caller's local pointer reachable in segment 1: a pointer in segment 2 or 3 has the
caller's S2 or S3 bank (from the OS frame) bound into S1 and is moved into S1; a pointer
below $8000 is taken to be in S1 already and the S1 binding is only read (OZ_MGB).
Entry: HL = caller's local pointer; IY = OS frame.
Exit: HL = the pointer in segment 1; B = previous S1 bank (to restore with OZ_MPB); C =
MS_S1.
Changes: B, C, HL.

1325.synopsis:
Entry inside SetBlinkScreen, called when Fz = 1: sets the LCD-on bit (BB_COMLCDON) in A.
Entry: A = COM register value.
Exit: A with the LCD-on bit set.
Changes: A.

1328.synopsis:
Switches the LCD on: calls SetBlinkScreen with Fz = 1, which sets the LCD-on bit in the COM
soft copy and the Blink COM register. Used after blowing or erasing flash.
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

1723.synopsis:
Step of FleEprXfrBlkSize when the rest of the file fits in the current bank: the whole
remaining size becomes the block size.
Entry: DE' = remaining file size (at most 16K; C' is not changed).
Exit: HL' = block size (the remaining size); DE' = 0.
Changes: DE', HL'.

1730.synopsis:
Step of FleEprXfrBlkSize when the rest of the file crosses the bank boundary: the block is
DE bytes, and the remaining size CDE' is reduced by it.
Entry: DE = block size; CDE' = remaining file size; Fc = 0.
Exit: HL' = block size; CDE' = CDE' - DE.
Changes: C', DE', HL'.
Keeps: AF, DE.

1905.synopsis:
Step of DefHdrPos: looks for a file area header in the bank below the given one. The bank is
moved into the upper 512K when the card has 32 banks, and ChkFileEprHdr checks it.
Entry: A = bank above the file area (slot relative); E = card size in 16K banks; C = slot
number.
Exit: Fc = 0; Fz = 1, header found: A = sub type, B = absolute bank of the header, C = size
of the file area in banks; Fz = 0, no header: B = absolute bank where a new header would go,
C = potential size of the file area in banks.
Changes: AF, BC, E.

1933.synopsis:
Returns the no-room error for DefHdrPos when the application area leaves no 64K block for a
file area (called with CALL Z and CALL C).
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_ROOM.
Changes: AF.

1980.synopsis:
ValidateOzWaterMark: checks for an "oz" watermark at the top of a bank. It reads the size
byte, the sub type and the "oz" word, then writes 0 over the word and reads it again: only a
word that is still "oz" (ROM or flash, not RAM) counts. A changed word is written back.
Entry: BHL = absolute pointer to the size byte ($3FFC, or $3FEC in an application header).
Exit: Fz = 1, watermark found: C = sub type, D = size of the area in banks; Fz = 0, not
found.
Changes: AF, C, DE.
Keeps: B, HL.

2739.synopsis:
Stores one character of a file name for FetchFilename and advances the buffer pointer.
Entry: A = character; CDE = buffer pointer (C = bank).
Exit: (CDE) = A; DE + 1.
Changes: DE.
Keeps: BC, HL.

2858.synopsis:
Adds a file entry's size to the sum of active file space for CalcFileSpace.
Entry: CDE = size of the entry (header and image); BHL' = sum so far.
Exit: BHL' = BHL' + CDE.
Changes: B', HL', IX (CalcFileSpace saves IX).
Keeps: AF.

2878.synopsis:
Adds a file entry's size to the sum of deleted file space for CalcFileSpace.
Entry: CDE = size of the entry (header and image); CDE' = sum so far.
Exit: CDE' = CDE' + CDE.
Changes: C', DE', IX (CalcFileSpace saves IX).
Keeps: AF.

3014.synopsis:
Counts a deleted file entry for FileEprCntFiles, which calls it with the register sets
exchanged: the deleted-file counter DE is incremented unless the entry's file length (CDE in
the other set) is 0, the null file of Intel flash cards. Fz is kept, so the following CALL
NZ, ActiveFile is skipped.
Entry: DE = deleted-file count; CDE' = file length; Fz = 1.
Exit: DE = DE + 1 for a real file.
Changes: DE, AF'.

3025.synopsis:
Counts an active file entry for FileEprCntFiles.
Entry: HL = active-file count (in the exchanged register set).
Exit: HL = HL + 1.
Changes: HL.

3390.synopsis:
Error exit of BuildFileEntHdr when no file area is found: drops the two words of the entry
size and the File Entry pointer from the stack, the last of which restores HL.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Onf; HL = HL on entry to BuildFileEntHdr.
Changes: AF, HL.

3790.synopsis:
Error return of the flash erase routines.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_BER (block or sector erase failed).
Changes: AF.

3794.synopsis:
Error return of the flash write routines.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_BWR (byte not written).
Changes: AF.

4069.synopsis:
Table of the known flash chips, read by FlashEprCardId: a count byte (7), then 7 entries of
6 bytes: device code, manufacturer code, size in 16K banks, chip generation (FE_28F or
FE_29F) and a word pointing to the chip's name string (mnem_i004 and the following).

4112.synopsis: Name string of the Intel I28F004S5 flash chip, "I28F004S5 (512K)", null-terminated.

4129.synopsis:
Name string "I28F008S5 (1Mb)", null-terminated, shared by the Intel I28F008SA and I28F008S5
entries of DeviceCodeTable.

4145.synopsis: Name string of the AMD AM29F010B flash chip, "AM29F010B (128K)", null-terminated.

4162.synopsis: Name string of the AMD AM29F040B flash chip, "AM29F040B (512K)", null-terminated.

4179.synopsis: Name string of the AMD AM29F080B flash chip, "AM29F080B (1Mb)", null-terminated.

4195.synopsis: Name string of the AMIC29F040B flash chip, "AMIC29F040B (512K)", null-terminated.

4496.synopsis:
Copies a file entry to the file area of a flash card for FlshEprCpyFleEnt: gets a new entry
pointer (FleEprNewFileEnt), then blows the entry block by block, each block ending at a bank
boundary (FleEprXfrBlkSize, FlashEprCopyBlock). If a block fails, the new entry is marked as
deleted.
Entry: C = slot number; IY = work buffer with SrcFileEntry, SrcFileSize and FepType set.
Exit: Fc = 0, entry copied.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (no file area, or the write error of FlashEprCopyBlock).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, BC', DE', HL'.

4792.synopsis:
The null file that SaveNullFile blows at the bottom of an Intel flash card after formatting:
6 bytes, a file entry with a 1-character name ($00) and a file length of 0.

5070.synopsis:
Returns the flash chip generation of the card that holds a bank, for FlshEprStdFleHdr: the
slot comes from the bank (GetSlotNo) and the type from FlashEprCardId.
Entry: B = absolute bank.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = FE_28F or FE_29F.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_NFE (no known flash chip).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

5081.synopsis:
The last 6 bytes of a new "oz" file area header, copied by FlshEprStdFleHdr to $3FFA: the
high word of the random id ($01, $80), a size placeholder ($40), a sub type placeholder
($FF), both overwritten afterwards, and "oz".

5472.synopsis:
Body of OS_Fn (OSFn calls it inside the OS frame): exchanges A and B and dispatches on the
reason: FN_AH allocates a handle (AllocHandle), FN_VH verifies one (VerifyHandle), FN_FH
frees one (FreeHandle), FN_GH finds one by type and dynamic id (FindHandle), and FN_NH finds
the next handle of the same type.
Entry: A = reason (FN_AH to FN_NH); B = handle type; C = dynamic id (FN_GH); IX = handle.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = handle (FN_AH, FN_GH, FN_NH).
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Unk for an unknown reason, RC_Eof after the last handle).

5525.synopsis:
Initialises a device handle: FindHandleDOR takes the first device in DevTable whose id is at
least A + 1 and that is present (RAM fitted, ROM or file area found). The device id, the
application slot of a ROM device, the DOR's address and the handle flags are stored, then
the DOR's bank is bound into S2 and its type returned (GetDORType).
Entry: A = device id - 1; IX = handle.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = DOR type (Fz = 1 when it is 0); the DOR's bank bound into S2.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (no such device left in DevTable).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

5757.synopsis:
DOR of the SCR.0 (screen) device, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (parent, brother, son, 3
bytes each), type Dm_Chd, the length, the name record "SCR.0" and $FF. The parent field
holds its handle for OS_Nq ($8606, NQ_Shn).

5777.synopsis:
DOR of the PRT.0 (printer) device, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (parent, brother, son,
3 bytes each), type Dm_Chd, the length, the name record "PRT.0" and $FF. The parent field
holds its handle for OS_Nq ($8609, NQ_Phn).

5797.synopsis:
DOR of the COM.0 (serial port) device, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (parent, brother,
son, 3 bytes each), type Dm_Chd, the length, the name record "COM.0" and $FF. The parent
field holds its handle for OS_Nq ($8C1E, NQ_Chn).

5817.synopsis:
DOR of the NUL.0 (null) device, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (parent, brother, son, 3
bytes each), type Dm_Chd, the length, the name record "NUL.0" and $FF. The parent field
holds its handle for OS_Nq ($860C, NQ_Nhn).

5837.synopsis:
DOR of the INP.0 (input) device, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (parent, brother, son, 3
bytes each), type Dm_Chd, the length, the name record "INP.0" and $FF. The parent field
holds its handle for OS_Nq ($8615, NQ_Ihn).

5857.synopsis:
DOR of the OUT.0 (output) device, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (parent, brother, son, 3
bytes each), type Dm_Chd, the length, the name record "OUT.0" and $FF. The parent field
holds its handle for OS_Nq ($8618, NQ_Ohn).

5897.synopsis:
DOR of the ROM.1 device, 20 bytes: the parent and brother pointers (0), the son pointer to
the ROM Front DOR at the top of slot 1 (ROM_DOR in S2, bank RO1_BNK), type DM_ROM, the
length, the name record "ROM.1" and $FF.

5917.synopsis:
DOR of the ROM.2 device, 20 bytes: the parent and brother pointers (0), the son pointer to
the ROM Front DOR at the top of slot 2 (ROM_DOR in S2, bank RO2_BNK), type DM_ROM, the
length, the name record "ROM.2" and $FF.

5937.synopsis:
DOR of the ROM.3 device, 20 bytes: the parent and brother pointers (0), the son pointer to
the ROM Front DOR at the top of slot 3 (ROM_DOR in S2, bank RO3_BNK), type DM_ROM, the
length, the name record "ROM.3" and $FF.

5957.synopsis:
DOR of the APP.- device, 20 bytes: the parent and brother pointers (0), the son pointer to
the Front DOR of the installed applications (APX_DOR in S2, bank APX_BNK), type DM_ROM, the
length, the name record "APP.-" and $FF.

5977.synopsis:
DOR of the EPR.0 device of the Eprom filing system, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (all
0), type Dm_Epr, the length, the name record "EPR.0" and $FF.

5997.synopsis:
DOR of the EPR.1 device of the Eprom filing system, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (all
0), type Dm_Epr, the length, the name record "EPR.1" and $FF.

6017.synopsis:
DOR of the EPR.2 device of the Eprom filing system, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (all
0), type Dm_Epr, the length, the name record "EPR.2" and $FF.

6037.synopsis:
DOR of the EPR.3 device of the Eprom filing system, 20 bytes: the three link pointers (all
0), type Dm_Epr, the length, the name record "EPR.3" and $FF.

6057.synopsis:
Resets the machine, entered from Boot_reset with kernel bank 1 in S2; it never returns.
1. A hard reset (the flap was open, or bank $21 does not start with the RAM tag) fills banks
$21 and $20 with 0; a soft reset clears bank $20 except the preserved system variables. The
type ($00 hard, $FF soft) goes to ubResetType.
2. Writes InitData to the Blink and its soft copies, copies the low-RAM code into bank $20,
maps it at $0000 (COM), sets SP = $2000 and the kernel bank soft copies.
3. Resets the handles, sets the screen addresses with OS_Sci, clears the buffers
(InitBuffers) and prints "HARD RESET ..." or "SOFT RESET ...".
4. Allocates the filing-system memory pool, initialises RAM, marks the system and swap pages
and expands the machine when a 128K card is present (ExpandMachine).
5. After a soft reset restores the panel (PreserveSysPanel); sets the time (TimeReset), the
random seed and the RAM devices, moves the screen base file to bank $21 and resets the
serial interface.
6. Sets the default device to the expanded RAM card (defDev), installs the panel defaults,
enables interrupts and enters the Index (OS_Ent) in an endless loop.
Entry: A' = interrupt status (its flap-open bit is tested).

6430.synopsis:
The default device name ":RAM.0" (6 bytes, no terminator). Reset copies it to $1800, and
when an expanded RAM card is found replaces the digit with its slot and sets it with OS_Sp
PA_Dev.

6475.synopsis:
PreserveSystemPanel: gives the panel values kept over a soft reset back to the panel,
calling OS_Sp with a length of 1 for PA_Loc down to $8001 with cCountry, ubBadSize, cSound,
cKeyclick, ubRepeat and ubTimeout.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, HL.
Keeps: BC.

6492.synopsis:
Sets the clock at reset. After a soft reset the elapsed time from the hardware clock copy
(ubTIM1_A, or ubTIM1_B when bit 0 of ubTimeBufferSelect is set) updates the base time
(GN_Msc MT_UBT); after a hard reset SetInitialTime sets the date and time of the build
(GN_Dei, GN_Pmd, GN_Pmt). Both end in IntSecond.
Entry: ubResetType ($00 hard, $FF soft).

6551.synopsis:
Blink initialisation table read by Reset: pairs of port and value, ended by 0. SR2 gets
kernel bank 1, the timer interrupt mask and acknowledge get tick, second and minute, INT
enables flap, battery low, time and global interrupts, ACK acknowledges A19, flap, battery
low and keyboard, and EPR gets 0. Each value also goes to the port's soft copy.

6596.synopsis:
Zeroes BC bytes from HL: clears the first byte and copies it forward with LDIR. InitBuffers
calls it for the serial receive buffer and the keyboard buffer, then sets HL = KbdData and
BC = kbd_SIZEOF and falls into it for the keyboard variables.
Entry: HL = the area; BC = its length (at least 2: BC is decremented before the LDIR); HL
not at a $xxFF address (DE is made with INC E).
Exit: the area is zero; BC = 0; HL = its last byte; DE = the byte after it.
Changes: BC, DE, HL; F (P/V).
Keeps: A, IX, IY.

6989.synopsis:
OS_Cli: the CLI interface (internal). Reason 0 (undocumented) returns at once through
OZCallReturn2 with A = ubCLIActiveCnt and IX = KbdData. Any other reason builds the OS frame
(OSFramePush), exchanges A and B so that B holds the reason, runs OSCliMain and returns
through OSFramePop.
Entry: A = reason: 0, or CL_RIM, CL_MBC, CL_CMB, CL_INC, CL_DEC, CL_RES, CL_ACK (1-7); the
other registers as the reason needs them (see OSCliMain).
Exit: reason 0: A = the CLI use count; IX = KbdData. Others: as OSCliMain.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Unk for a reason above 7; others as OSCliMain.

7016.synopsis:
The body of OS_Cli: counts B down with DJNZ to pick the reason, with HL = ubCLIActiveCnt and
Fc = 0. Results go into the OS frame (IY). CL_RIM: reads raw input from the keyboard buffer
(RdKbBuffer) with BC as the timeout; returns BC = the time left, D = 0, E = the character.
CL_MBC: E = a character, D = its qualifiers; translates it (CLIchar2key for a control code
or a special key, then ApplyQualifiers) and returns E = the result, D = 0. CL_CMB: E = a key
code; returns E = the base character and D = its qualifiers (Key2Meta). CL_INC: increments
the CLI use count; when it was 0, first clears IST_B_CLISHIFT and IST_B_CLIDMND in
ubIntStatus. CL_DEC decrements it, CL_RES sets it to 0. These three then request an OZ
window redraw (SetPendingOZwd). CL_ACK: D = the keys to acknowledge (QUAL_B_CTRL clears
IST_B_CLIDMND, QUAL_B_SHIFT clears IST_B_CLISHIFT); returns D = the remaining IST_CLISHIFT
and IST_CLIDMND bits and Fz = 1 when neither is set.
Entry: B = reason (1-7); A = the caller's B; C, DE as the reason needs; IY = the OS frame.
Exit: Fc = 0; the results in the OS frame as above.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from RdKbBuffer, or RC_Unk for an unknown reason).

7190.synopsis:
Finds the application after the one in C: asks GetAppDOR for application C + 1 and returns
its number in BC. OS_Poll calls it with BC = the caller's IX.
Entry: C = the current application number (0 for the start of the list).
Exit: Fc = 0; BC = the next application's number (B = 0).
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Eof when there is no further application.
Changes: AF, BC, and what GetAppDOR changes.

7264.synopsis:
Checks that DE lies between BC and HL. ChkStkLimits uses it for the application stack
pointer and the unsafe area start, with HL = $1FFE and BC = $1820, and freezes when either
is outside.
Entry: DE = the value; HL = the upper limit; BC = the lower limit.
Exit: Fc = 0 when BC <= DE <= HL; Fc = 1 when DE is above HL or below BC.
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL, IX, IY.

7312.synopsis:
OS_Nq for the process enquiries ($86xx: NQ_Ain to NQ_Btl), entered from OSNqMain with the
reason's low byte in A and C. Rejects a low byte of $27 or more, else jumps into
OSNqPrcssTable, a table of 13 JP instructions (NQAin, NQKhn, NQShn, NQPhn, NQNhn, NQWai,
NQCom, NQIhn, NQOhn, NQRhn, NQVoz, NQRoz, NqBtl).
Entry: A = C = the reason's low byte (a multiple of 3); B = 0; IY = the OS frame.
Exit: as the handler.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Unk for a reason out of range.

7655.synopsis:
Waits for ESC or Q: reads raw keys with OS_Cli CL_RIM and no timeout until one arrives that
is ESC or Q (either case), with no qualifier byte. An escape condition (RC_Esc) is
acknowledged with OS_Esc and ends the wait too; RC_Susp and other errors read again. NQVoz's
error box uses it.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fz = 1 always; A = ESC or 'Q' for a key, or OS_Esc's result after an escape.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.

7691.synopsis:
GN_Win window definition for NQVoz's error box (7 bytes): $D1 (window 1, bars, banner and
bottom line, a grey pop-up, 7-pixel banner), X = 20, Y = 0, width 45, height 8, and the
banner pointer errbanner.

7698.synopsis: The error box's banner text: "ERROR" and a 0. ErrWinDef points to it.

7704.synopsis:
Reads the running OZ version: OS_Frm with A = FA_PTR, IX = -1 and DE = 0, which returns it
in DEBC. NQVoz compares C with the version an application asks for.
Entry: none.
Exit: DEBC = OS_Frm's result; C = the OZ version (e.g. $47).
Changes: AF, BC, DE.
Keeps: IX.

7734.synopsis:
The OZ revision number, a 32-bit value (ozrev) stored low word first; $0603C979 in this ROM.
NQRoz returns it in DEBC.

8026.synopsis:
Sets up the slot loop shared by StoreCardIDs and ChkCardChange: D = 3 slots to visit (slot 3
down to 1), E = $3F (the source calls it the maximum card size), and HL' = the end of slot
3's 4-byte card ID (ulSlot3ID + 4); the IDs are stored downwards from there.
Entry: none.
Exit: D = 3; E = $3F; HL' = ulSlot3ID + 4.
Changes: DE, HL'.

8047.synopsis:
OS_Op with OP_MEM: opens a memory file. Allocates a file handle (AllocHandle, HND_FILE),
initialises it as a memory file (InitMemHandle), copies C bytes from BHL into it (MvToFile),
marks it readable, writable and memory, and rewinds it (RewindFile). If the copy fails, the
handle is freed (FreeMemHandle).
Entry: BHL = the data; C = its length.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = the new handle, positioned at the start.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

8106.synopsis:
Writes a file DOR's name and dates. With Fz = 1 it first copies the 17-byte name at the
caller's HL (the OS frame) into a stack buffer and writes it as the 'N' record (OS_Dor
DR_WR; a failure hangs in a loop). Then it reads the machine date and time (GN_Gmd, GN_Gmt,
again while they are inconsistent) and writes them as the 'U' (update) record, and also as
the 'C' (create) record when Fc = 1.
Entry: IX = the DOR handle; Fz = 1 to rename (the name at the caller's HL); Fc = 1 to set
the creation date too; IY = the OS frame.
Exit: the records written; the 17-byte stack buffer released.

8180.synopsis:
OS_Map: map control, the graphics area that PipeDream's map uses. Runs OSMapMain with IX
kept.
Entry: C = reason (MP_WR, MP_DEF, MP_GRA, MP_DEL, MP_MEM); the other registers as OSMapMain.
Exit: as OSMapMain.
Keeps: IX.

8188.synopsis:
The body of OS_Map: picks the reason in C with DJNZ. MP_WR writes one pixel line: E = the
row (masked to 0-63), HL = the line's data in the caller's space; the line is the window's
map width (GetMapWidth) / 8 bytes, poked 8 bytes apart into the HIRES0 bank (the bank and
address come from BLSC_PB2L/PB2H). MP_DEF and MP_GRA define the map (_mp_def). MP_DEL does
nothing and returns Fc = 0. MP_MEM: B = an MS_Sx segment specifier; defines the map, then
returns DE = the widths from _mp_def, B = the map's bank, C = the segment specifier, and HL
= the map's base (OS_Sci SC_HR0) addressed in that segment.
Entry: C = reason; A = the window; as above; IY = the OS frame.
Exit: as above.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Unk for a reason above MP_MEM; Fc = 1 when the window is not found.

8268.synopsis:
Defines a map (MP_DEF; also MP_GRA and MP_MEM). Opens the screen data, finds the window
(GetWindowFrame) and gets the map size (sub_9EBC). When there is a map, it defines the
window (SOH 7 #) at X = 94 - C characters, Y = 0, C characters wide, 8 lines high, selects
and clears it with the active window kept (GetCurrentWdInfo, RestoreActiveWd), and sets the
window's right margin to D, the pixel width. Returns BC to the caller through the OS frame.
Entry: A = the window; C = the reason (MP_GRA and MP_MEM take the width from the caller's L,
MP_DEF from the Panel); IY = the OS frame.
Exit: Fc = 0; BC (and the frame's BC) = B the pixel width, C the width in characters; BC = 0
when there is no map (PA_Map not 'Y', or size 0).
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Hand when the window is not found.

8392.synopsis:
Works out the map's size for _mp_def. Asks whether there is a map (sub_9F0C, 'Y' for MP_GRA
and MP_MEM) and its width in pixels (sub_9EF6). A width above 96 is cut to 96 unless 128K of
RAM was found (Chk128KB).
Entry: IY = the OS frame (its C is the reason, its L the width for MP_GRA and MP_MEM).
Exit: Fc = 0; B = the width in pixels; D = the width rounded up to a multiple of 8 ($FF
above 248); C = the width in 6-pixel characters, (D - 1) / 6 + 1.
Error: Fc = 1, BC = 0 when there is no map, the width is 0 or OS_Nq fails.

8450.synopsis:
Gets the map's width in pixels: the caller's L for MP_GRA and MP_MEM, else the Panel setting
PA_Msz (sub_9F17); a value above 255 gives $FF.
Entry: IY = the OS frame.
Exit: Fc = 0; L = the width.
Error: Fc = 1 from OS_Nq.

8475.synopsis:
Gets whether the map is on: L = 'Y' for MP_GRA and MP_MEM; otherwise sets BC = PA_Map and
falls into sub_9F17 to read the Panel setting ('Y' or 'N').
Entry: IY = the OS frame.
Exit: L = 'Y' or 'N'.
Error: Fc = 1 from OS_Nq.

8489.synopsis:
Reads a 2-byte Panel setting with OS_Nq (A = 2, the buffer on the stack).
Entry: BC = the parameter (PA_xxx).
Exit: HL = the value.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from OS_Nq.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

8678.synopsis:
Copies the active application's MTH pointers (eAppDOR_2 to eAppTokens_2: five 3-byte
pointers, DOR, topics, commands, help and tokens) over the help pointers (eHlpAppDOR to
eHlpTokens). Falls into the copy shared with CopyMTHHelp_App.
Entry: none.
Exit: the 15 bytes copied; BC = 0.
Changes: BC, DE, HL; F (P/V, H, N).
Keeps: A, Fc, IX, IY.

8686.synopsis:
Copies the help MTH pointers (eHlpAppDOR to eHlpTokens, 15 bytes) back over the active
application's (eAppDOR_2 to eAppTokens_2).
Entry: none.
Exit: the 15 bytes copied; BC = 0.
Changes: BC, DE, HL; F (P/V, H, N).
Keeps: A, Fc, IX, IY.

8698.synopsis:
Calls OS_Sr and stores the IX it returns in pMTHScreenSave: the help system saves, restores
and frees the user screen through it.
Entry: A = the OS_Sr reason (SR_SUS, SR_RUS, SR_FUS); IX as OS_Sr needs.
Exit: as OS_Sr; pMTHScreenSave = IX.

8705.synopsis:
Draws the key legend beside the command menu (DrawMenuWd calls it), centred in tiny type,
four lines: MENU "ADVANCE" (HELP "BROWSE" when the active topic is an information topic),
the arrows "SELECT", ENTER "ACTION" ("DETAIL"), and ESC "RESUME". When no user screen was
saved (pMTHScreenSave high byte 0) the select and action lines become "MEMORY LOW".
Entry: none (reads ubHlpActiveTpc).

8778.synopsis:
Entry inside DrawMenuWd2: prints the symbol of key A (MTHPrintKeycode), then the string that
starts at HL + 1 (OS_Bout, which leaves HL after its terminator). DrawMenuWd2 calls it for
the first line and falls into it for the third.
Entry: A = the key code; HL = the byte before the string.
Exit: HL = the byte after the string's 0.

8800.synopsis:
The legend for an ordinary topic: SD_MNU (the MENU key), then "\nADVANCE" and "\nACTION",
each ended by a 0. DrawMenuWd2 prints them through dmwd_2.

8818.synopsis:
The legend for an information topic: SD_HLP (the HELP key), then "\nBROWSE" and "\nDETAIL",
each ended by a 0. DrawMenuWd2 prints them through dmwd_2.

8835.synopsis:
MENU in the menu: moves to the next page of topics. Checks there are two command topics
(mnu_m2), increments ubHlpActiveHelp, finds the next non-information topic after the active
one and falls into SetHlpActiveTpc.
Entry: none.
Exit: as SetHlpActiveTpc; Fc = 1 when there is no further topic.

8845.synopsis:
Makes topic A the active one. When Fc = 1, or the topic window's line (ubHlpActiveHelp) is 8
or more, it resets the line to 1 and moves to the first non-information topic from A
(GetNonInfoTopicByNum).
Entry: A = the topic number; Fc = 1 to reset the line.
Exit: Fc = 0; ubHlpActiveTpc (and maybe ubHlpActiveHelp) set.

8873.synopsis:
SHIFT MENU in the menu: moves to the previous topic. Checks there are two command topics
(mnu_m2), decrements ubHlpActiveHelp, finds the previous non-information topic and goes to
SetHlpActiveTpc.
Entry: none.
Exit: as SetHlpActiveTpc.

8885.synopsis:
Checks that the application has at least two non-information (command) topics; if so,
selects the first command (ubHlpActiveCmd = 1).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = ubHlpActiveHelp.
Error: Fc = 1 when there are fewer than two such topics.

8900.synopsis:
UP in the menu: A = the active command (ubHlpActiveCmd), and falls into loc_A0C8 to find the
one before it.

8903.synopsis:
Entry inside mnu_up2: finds the command before command A. Looks up A - 1, A - 2, ...
(GetCmdAttrByNum) until the position it reports is not A.
Entry: A = the command number.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0; A = the previous command's position.
Error: Fc = 1, Fz = 1 when A is 1 and the lookup gives 1 back.
Changes: AF, BC, and what GetCmdAttrByNum changes.

8963.synopsis:
Fills the first 3 bytes of the help state saved on entry to help (the 20-byte copy that
ExitHelp restores): with the current command, topic and line (ubHlpActiveCmd to
ubHlpActiveHelp) when help shows the suspended application (GetHlp_sub) and its active topic
exists and is not an information topic, else with 1, 1, 1 (dummy).
Entry: IY = DoHelp's frame, whose first word points at the saved state.
Exit: Fz = 1 when the help values were kept, Fz = 0 when they were reset; DE = the saved
ubHlpActiveApp byte.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

9002.synopsis:
Three 1 bytes: the command, topic and line that MayRstAppHlpData stores when it resets the
saved help state.

9005.synopsis:
Waits for a key in the help pages and jumps to its handler. The return address points at a
table: entries of a key code byte and a handler word, ended by a 0; the entry for code 1 is
the page's own redraw. Never returns to the table.
1. Examines the input (OS_Xin). When there is none but ubSysFlags1 has SF1_B_INPUTPENDING,
takes code 1.
2. Reads a key (RdStdinNoTO). RC_Susp reads again; ESC is acknowledged (OS_Esc SC_ACK) and
passed as IN_ESC; another error leaves help with Fc = 1.
3. INDEX becomes $89. That, the [] key and codes $80-$9F leave help with Fc = 1, A = the
code. ESC and DEL leave help with A = RC_Susp, Fc = 1.
4. Otherwise looks the key up in the table and jumps to its handler with A = the key and Fc
= 0. A key not in the table goes to RetryKeyJump, which handles OZ's own command keys
(beeping when memory is low) and waits again.
Entry: (SP) = the key table; IY = DoHelp's frame.
Exit: to the key's handler, or out of help through ExitKeyJump.

9091.synopsis:
The copyright page: prints CopyrightMsg (in mth/systoken.asm) as a full page (MTHFullPage)
and falls into cr_waitkey.

9097.synopsis:
Waits for a key on the copyright page (MTH_KeyJump, its table follows the call): HELP goes
to the first application's help (cr_hlp), LEFT to MTH_HallOfFame, RIGHT to MTH_Help; MENU,
UP, DOWN and ENTER wait again.

9125.synopsis:
The hall of fame page: prints HallOfFameMsg (in mth/systoken.asm) as a full page
(MTHFullPage) and falls into hf_waitkey.

9159.synopsis:
Prints a tokenized page across the screen: defines window 6 (X = 1, Y = 0, 92 wide, 8 high,
type $81), selects and clears it, centres the text, and prints the text from the MTH bank
(MTHPrintTokenized) with the system tokens (SF1_B_SYSTOKENS set, then ubSysFlags1 restored).
Entry: HL = the tokenized text in the MTH bank (MTH_BNK).
Changes: AF, B, HL, and what MTHPrintTokenized changes.

9203.synopsis:
The application help page: returns to the application whose help was shown
(SetHlpAppChgFile), sets the line, topic and command to 1, draws the page (DrawHelpWd) and
falls into hlp_waitkey.

9212.synopsis:
Waits for a key on the application help page (MTH_KeyJump, its table follows the call): HELP
to help_help, MENU to topic_menu, UP to help_up, DOWN to help_down, LEFT to MTH_Copyright,
RIGHT to help_right; ENTER waits again.

9240.synopsis:
UP on the help page: moves to the previous application (PrevAppDOR) and shows its help
(MTH_Help).

9245.synopsis:
HELP on the help page: when the application has a topic with help (GetFirstTopicHelp), goes
to MTH_Topic; otherwise falls into help_down.

9250.synopsis:
DOWN on the help page: moves to the next application (NextAppDOR) and shows its help
(MTH_Help).

9255.synopsis:
RIGHT on the help page: when the application has a topic with help (GetFirstTopicHelp),
falls into MTH_Topic; otherwise waits again (hlp_waitkey).

9260.synopsis:
The topic help page: selects the first command (ubHlpActiveCmd = 1), draws the active
topic's help (DrawTopicHelpWd) and falls into topic_waitkey.

9266.synopsis:
Waits for a key on the topic help page (MTH_KeyJump, its table follows the call): HELP to
topic_help, MENU to topic_menu, UP to topic_up, DOWN to topic_down, LEFT to MTH_Help, RIGHT
to topic_right; ENTER waits again.

9294.synopsis:
DOWN on the topic page: B = 1, and goes on at topic_up's search for the next topic with
help.

9298.synopsis:
UP on the topic page: B = -1. When at least two topics have help (Get2ndTopicHelp), steps
from the active topic by B, wrapping, to the next one with help, makes it active
(SetHlpActiveTpc, Fc = 0) and shows it (MTH_Topic); otherwise waits again.

9328.synopsis:
HELP on the topic page: shows the topic's first command with help (MTH_Command); without
one, the next topic with help (MTH_Topic), and after the last topic the next application's
help (help_down).

9344.synopsis:
RIGHT on the topic page: when the topic has a command with help (GetFirstCmdHelp), makes it
active and falls into MTH_Command; otherwise waits again.

9353.synopsis:
The command help page: draws the active command's help (DrawCmdHelpWd) and falls into
cmd_waitkey.

9356.synopsis:
Waits for a key on the command help page (MTH_KeyJump, its table follows the call): HELP to
cmd_help, MENU to topic_menu, UP to cmd_up, DOWN to cmd_down, LEFT to MTH_Topic; RIGHT and
ENTER wait again.

9384.synopsis:
UP on the command page: D = -1, and goes on at cmd_down's search for the previous command
with help.

9388.synopsis:
DOWN on the command page: D = 1. Steps from the active command by D, wrapping, to the next
command whose attributes have CMDF_B_HELP, makes it active and shows it (MTH_Command); after
a full round the active command stays.

9417.synopsis:
HELP on the command page: shows the next command with help (MTH_Command); without one, goes
on at topic_nxhelp (the next topic with help, or the next application).

9428.synopsis:
MENU from the help pages: updates the saved help state (MayRstAppHlpData), resets the line,
topic and command to 1 when it was reset, makes the suspended application active again
(SetActiveAppDOR, ChgHelpFile) and falls into menu_entry.

9441.synopsis:
The command menu. Finds the first command topic, makes the active topic at least that one
with its line in the topic window (ubHlpActiveHelp) at most 7, and moves it to a command
topic (GetNonInfoTopicByNum). Then (loc_A2AD, also reached from DoHelp for an information
topic) draws the topic window (DrawTopicWd) and, when no input is waiting, marks the active
topic on its line in window 7; draws the menu (DrawMenuWd), selects window 6 (X = 1, Y = 0,
92 wide, 8 high), highlights the active command (sub_A3EC, MTHHighlight) and waits
(MTH_KeyJump): HELP to mnu_help, MENU to mnu_menu, SHIFT MENU to mnu_smenu, UP, DOWN, LEFT,
RIGHT and ENTER to mnu_up, mnu_down, mnu_left, mnu_right and mnu_enter.

9627.synopsis:
MENU in the menu: next topic page (mnu_menu2); redraws the menu (menu_entry), or waits again
when there is none.

9635.synopsis:
SHIFT MENU in the menu: previous topic page (mnu_smenu2); redraws the menu (menu_entry), or
waits again when there is none.

9640.synopsis:
UP in the menu: finds the previous command (mnu_up2) and moves the highlight to it
(loc_A2C4).

9645.synopsis: DOWN in the menu: moves the highlight to the command after the active one (loc_A2C4).

9651.synopsis:
ENTER in the menu: runs the active command. A command marked CMDF_B_SAFE beeps (Beep_X). A
command with code 0 shows its help (DrawTopicWd, MTH_Command). Otherwise, when memory is not
low, help ends with A = the command code, Fc = 0, Fz = 1 (ExitKeyJump); when it is low, it
beeps.

9689.synopsis:
RIGHT in the menu: when the menu has one column (GetCmdAttrByNum for command 0 gives D = 1),
acts as DOWN. Otherwise searches forward from the active command (GetNextCmdAttr) for the
command in the next column on the same row, D being the column and E the row, and moves the
highlight to it (loc_A2C4).

9753.synopsis:
LEFT in the menu: when the menu has one column (GetCmdAttrByNum for command 0 gives D = 1),
acts as UP. Otherwise searches backward from the active command (loc_A0C8) for the command
in the previous column on the same row and moves the highlight to it (loc_A2C4).

9837.synopsis:
HELP in the menu: redraws the topic window (DrawTopicWd), then shows the application help
(MTH_Help) for an information topic, else the active command's help (MTH_Command), else the
topic's (MTH_Topic), else the application's.

9872.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to command A's place in the menu window: column 28 * (D - 1) and row E from
GetCmdAttrByNum.
Entry: A = the command number.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = the command's position; C = its row; B = 0; the cursor at its place.
Error: Fc = 1 when the command does not exist, its column starts at 66 or beyond, or no user
screen was saved (pMTHScreenSave high byte 0).

9916.synopsis:
Opens an application's help: builds ":ROM.*/HELP/" and the 17-byte application name in a
29-byte stack buffer, opens its DOR (FilenameDOR), reads the 12-byte 'H' record (the topics,
commands, help and tokens pointers) into eHlpTopics and fixes their slot (CopyAppPointers).
The DOR handle is freed if the read fails.
Entry: HL = the application name.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = the help DOR handle; eHlpTopics to eHlpTokens set.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

9968.synopsis:
Toggles reverse video over the 27 characters from the cursor (SOH R, SOH 2 E 27, SOH R): the
highlight bar of a menu command.
Entry: the cursor at the command.
Changes: F.

9980.synopsis:
Starts the right-hand box of a help page, when no input is waiting (MayMTHPrint): defines
window 6 (X = 63, Y = 0, 30 wide, 8 high, type $81), selects and clears it and prints "FOR
MORE INFORMATION:" centred in tiny type.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when input was waiting (nothing printed).

10026.synopsis:
Ends the right-hand box of a help page, when no input is waiting (MayMTHPrint): two lines of
key legends, MENU "topic entries", HELP "browse", INDEX "the manager" and ESC "resume".
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when input was waiting (nothing printed).

10091.synopsis:
Saves the active window for RestoreActiveWd: asks OS_Nq NQ_Wcur for the current window and
leaves two words on the caller's stack, HL with H = the window number, then IX. The caller
must call RestoreActiveWd before it returns.
Entry: none.
Exit: the two words pushed.
Changes: AF, HL (the return address), and what OS_Nq NQ_Wcur returns.

10103.synopsis:
Undoes GetCurrentWdInfo: takes the two words from the stack, restores IX and selects the
saved window again with SOH 2 H and its number.
Entry: the two words GetCurrentWdInfo left on the stack.
Exit: IX restored; the saved window active; H = its number.
Changes: HL, IX.
Keeps: AF.

10121.synopsis:
Draws the topic window (window 7): the application name (InitTopicWd), then seven lines of
command topic names (PrintTopic between MTH_ToggleLT calls), from topic 1, or from the
active topic minus 6 when it is beyond 7. The active window is kept.
Entry: none (reads ubHlpActiveTpc).

10190.synopsis:
Sends SOH L and SOH T, which toggle the caps (L) and tiny (T) attributes.
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF.

10200.synopsis:
Clears the topic window's top line: selects window 7, resets underline, clears line 0 and
prints the application name in tiny, caps and underline without reverse and grey, then
toggles underline and grey. The active window is kept.
Entry: none.

10245.synopsis:
Draws the application help page: the window (InitHelpWd), the application name and its help
text (GetHlpHelp, MTHPrintTokenized), then the right-hand box (Help2Wd_Top) with "other
programs" and the up and down arrows, " about <name> topics" and the right arrow when a
topic has help, and the key legends (Help2Wd_bottom).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1 when input was waiting and drawing stopped.

10338.synopsis:
Defines the help window (window 6 at column 1, row 0, 61 by 8, flags $81), selects and
clears it and sets centred justification, through MayMTHPrint. Nothing is drawn when a key
is waiting: MayMTHPrint then returns straight to this routine's caller.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, window 6 drawn and selected.
Error: Fc = 1 when input is pending (nothing drawn).

10358.synopsis:
Finds the second command of the active topic that has a help page: calls GetFirstCmdHelp,
then falls into GetNextCmdHelp.
Entry: ubHlpActiveTpc = active topic.
Exit: as GetNextCmdHelp.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10361.synopsis:
Finds the next command of the active topic after command A that has a help page (the
CMDF_B_HELP attribute bit), going on through GetCmdAttrByNum.
Entry: A = command number to start after; ubHlpActiveTpc = active topic.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = number of the command found; B = its attributes; C = its command code; HL
= its definition; DE = as GetCmdAttrByNum.
Error: Fc = 1 when no further command has help.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10364.synopsis:
Finds the first command of the active topic that has a help page: starts with command 1 and
calls GetCmdAttrByNum until a command has the CMDF_B_HELP attribute bit set.
Entry: ubHlpActiveTpc = active topic.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = number of the command found; B = its attributes; C = its command code; HL
= its definition; DE = as GetCmdAttrByNum.
Error: Fc = 1 when no command of the topic has help.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10376.synopsis:
Steps to the next command: increments A and falls into GetCmdAttrByNum.
Entry: A = current command number; ubHlpActiveTpc = active topic.
Exit: as GetCmdAttrByNum for command A+1.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10377.synopsis:
Looks up command A of the active help topic and returns its attributes. Binds in the help
command list (GetHlpCommands, OSBixS1), skips to topic ubHlpActiveTpc (GetCmdTopicByNum),
turns the count into a real position past hidden commands (GetRealCmdPosition), reads the
command code and the attribute byte (GetAttr), then restores segment 1 (OSBoxS1).
Entry: A = command number within the active topic; ubHlpActiveTpc = active topic.
Exit: A = command position; B = attribute byte (CMDF_xxx); C = command code; HL = command
definition (in the list's bank, which is no longer bound); DE = the column and row
GetRealCmdPosition left in DE.
Error: Fc = 1, A = 0 when the topic does not exist (B, C, HL not set); Fc = 1 also comes
from GetRealCmdPosition at the start or end of the topic, with B, C and HL still set.
Callers rely on A = 0 at the end of the list to wrap round.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

10421.synopsis:
Finds the second help topic that has a help page: calls GetFirstTpcHelp, then falls into
GetNextTopicHelp.
Entry: none.
Exit: as GetNextTopicHelp.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL.

10424.synopsis:
Finds the next topic after topic A that has a help page (the help bit, bit 4, of its
attribute byte), going on through GetTpcAttrByNum.
Entry: A = topic number to start after.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = number of the topic found; D = its attributes (TPCF_xxx); HL = its
definition.
Error: Fc = 1 when no further topic has help.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL.

10427.synopsis:
Finds the first help topic that has a help page: starts with topic 1 and calls
GetTpcAttrByNum until a topic has the help bit (bit 4) of its attributes set.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = number of the topic found; D = its attributes (TPCF_xxx); HL = its
definition.
Error: Fc = 1 when no topic has help.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL.

10439.synopsis:
Finds the first topic that is not an INFO topic: sets A = 1 and falls into GtNnInfoTpcByNum.
Entry: none.
Exit: as GtNnInfoTpcByNum.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL.

10441.synopsis:
Finds the first topic, from topic A upwards, that is not an INFO topic (TPCF_B_INFO clear in
its attributes), calling GetTpcAttrByNum for each.
Entry: A = topic number to start with.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = number of the topic found; D = its attributes; HL = its definition.
Error: Fc = 1 when the list ends first.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL.

10448.synopsis:
Entry inside GtNnInfoTpcByNum: increments A and goes on searching from the next topic for
one that is not an INFO topic.
Entry: A = current topic number.
Exit: as GtNnInfoTpcByNum.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL.

10451.synopsis:
Decrements A and searches from there with GtNnInfoTpcByNum. The search runs upwards, so when
topic A-1 is an INFO topic the result is the next non-INFO topic after it.
Entry: A = current topic number.
Exit: as GtNnInfoTpcByNum.
Changes: AF, BC, D, HL.

10478.synopsis:
Prints the key legend of an internal key code: looks A up in CmdKeycodeTbl (3-byte entries:
key code, modifier symbol, key symbol, ended by 0) and prints SOH and the modifier symbol
when there is one, then SOH and the key symbol, through ScrDrv_SOH_A (OS_Out). Prints
nothing for a code not in the table.
Entry: A = internal key code (IN_xxx).
Exit: legend printed.
Changes: AF, BC.
Keeps: DE, HL.

10601.synopsis:
Starts help for an application: stores A as the active help application (ubHlpActiveApp) and
falls into InitHlpActHelp, which sets help page, topic and command to 1.
Entry: A = application number.
Exit: ubHlpActiveApp = A; ubHlpActiveHelp, ubHlpActiveTpc, ubHlpActiveCmd = 1; A = 1.
Changes: AF.

10604.synopsis:
Sets the active help page, topic and command to 1: loads A = 1 and falls into
SetHlpActiveHelp.
Entry: none.
Exit: ubHlpActiveHelp, ubHlpActiveTpc, ubHlpActiveCmd = 1; A = 1.
Changes: AF.

10606.synopsis:
Stores A as the active help page (ubHlpActiveHelp), sets the active topic to 1 and falls
into InitHlpActiveCmd.
Entry: A = help page number.
Exit: ubHlpActiveHelp = A; ubHlpActiveTpc, ubHlpActiveCmd = 1; A = 1.
Changes: AF.

10614.synopsis:
Selects the first command of the active topic: sets ubHlpActiveCmd to 1.
Entry: none.
Exit: ubHlpActiveCmd = 1; A = 1.
Changes: AF.

10795.synopsis:
OS_Sp main part, called by OSSp in kernel 0 after OSFramePush. Checks the reason's high byte
($80-$8E), pushes NqSp_ret as the return address and jumps through OSSpTable (one JP per 3
in the high byte): $80xx SpPanel (Panel and PrinterEd settings), $83xx, $86xx and $89xx do
nothing, $8Cxx hands the frame to DC_Sp (Director and CLI settings).
Entry: B = reason high byte; IY = OS frame (C, A, HL of the call are read from it).
Exit: as the handler; the handler gets A = C = reason low byte, B = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Unk when B is outside $80-$8E.

10846.synopsis:
OS_Nq main part, called by OSNq in kernel 0 after OSFramePush. Checks the reason's high byte
($80-$8E), pushes NqSp_ret as the return address and jumps through OSNqTable (one JP per 3
in the high byte): $80xx NqPanel, $83xx OSNqWindow, $86xx OSNqProcess, $89xx OSNqMemory,
$8Cxx OSNqDirector (DC_Nq).
Entry: B = reason high byte; IY = OS frame (C, A, DE of the call are read from it).
Exit: as the handler; the handler gets A = C = reason low byte, B = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Unk when B is outside $80-$8E.

11008.synopsis:
Copies the default value of a Panel or ISO-translation setting into a buffer and falls into
NqGetDest. The reason's low byte (OSFrame_C) indexes PrefTbl1 (panel, bit 7 clear) or
PrefTbl2 (ISO, bit 7 set) in the MTH bank, which hold byte offsets: the data starts at the
entry's offset and its length is the next offset minus this one.
Entry: IX = temporary buffer (NqPanel makes 256 bytes on the stack); IY = OS frame.
Exit: DE = IX (the default value); C = its length; HL = caller's destination buffer; A =
caller's buffer size (see NqGetDest).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

11057.synopsis:
Finds where OS_Nq returns its data: the caller's buffer from the frame's DE, and its size
from the frame's A. When the caller passed DE = 2, the value is returned in DE itself: the
frame's DE is cleared and HL points to OSFrame_E, with A = 2.
Entry: DE = source data; C = data length; IY = OS frame.
Exit: HL = destination; A = buffer size (2 when DE = 2 was passed).
Changes: AF, HL.
Keeps: BC, DE.

11272.synopsis:
Skips one attribute of the saved preferences data: reads its length byte from the memory
file with RdFileByte and reads past that many bytes.
Entry: memory file positioned on an attribute's length byte.
Exit: Fc = 0, positioned on the next attribute; A = 0 when the length was 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from RdFileByte.
Changes: AF, B.

11286.synopsis:
Checks the length given to OS_Sp for a Panel or ISO setting against the default length in
PrefTbl1/PrefTbl2 (MTH bank). The length is the frame's A, or 2 when the frame's DE is 2.
Entry: IY = OS frame (C = reason low byte, A = length, DE = data or 2).
Exit: C = the default length; Fz = 1 when the given length is 255 (A = 0) or when it and the
default length are both 0; Fz = 0 otherwise (SpPanel then writes the attribute).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

11340.synopsis:
Copies one byte from the old preferences data to the new memory file: reads it with
PanelFsRdByte and falls into MemFsWrByte.
Entry: both file states set up by SpPanel.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = the byte copied.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

11344.synopsis:
Writes A to the new preferences memory file: switches the file position to it (UseMemFs) and
jumps to WrFileByte.
Entry: A = byte.
Exit: Fc = 0, byte written.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

11350.synopsis:
Reads a byte of the old preferences data: switches the file position to it (UsePanelFs) and
jumps to RdFileByte.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = byte read.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (end of file included).
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

11356.synopsis:
Switches the kernel memory file position to the old preferences data: saves the 4-byte
eFsMemFilePos in pMTHScreenSave and loads it from lFsPanelArea. UseMemFs switches back.
Entry: none.
Exit: eFsMemFilePos = the panel data's position.
Changes: DE, HL.
Keeps: AF, BC.

11381.synopsis:
Switches the kernel memory file position to the new preferences memory file: saves the
4-byte eFsMemFilePos in lFsPanelArea and loads it from pMTHScreenSave. UsePanelFs switches
back.
Entry: none.
Exit: eFsMemFilePos = the new file's position.
Changes: DE, HL.
Keeps: AF, BC.

11630.synopsis:
Makes pPrefs1 the current preferences data: stores DE in pPrefs1, clears IST_B_2 at (HL) and
returns the other pointer, pPrefs2.
Entry: DE = new preferences data; HL = ubIntStatus.
Exit: DE = pPrefs2 (the previous data).
Changes: DE.
Keeps: AF.

11641.synopsis:
Makes pPrefs2 the current preferences data: stores DE in pPrefs2, sets IST_B_2 at (HL) and
returns the other pointer, pPrefs1.
Entry: DE = new preferences data; HL = ubIntStatus.
Exit: DE = pPrefs1 (the previous data).
Changes: DE.
Keeps: AF.

11744.synopsis:
Table of country settings read by RstRdPanelAttrs: a count byte ($0E), then 14 entries of 6
bytes: the PA_Loc country letter, the date filter table (word), two country-ID letters with
bit 7 set (for the OZ window) and the keymap's page in the keymap bank. The first entry (UK)
is the default when the country is not found.

11850.synopsis:
OS_Out to the screen: opens the screen, takes the active window (sbf_ActiveWd) in IX, hides
the cursor, puts the byte through OSOut_Put, stores the cursor position, shows the cursor
again and closes the screen.
Entry: A = byte to write.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Keeps: IX.

11880.synopsis:
Puts one byte through the screen driver. While a prefix sequence is open (sbf_CtrlPrefix not
0) the byte goes to OsOut_Prefixed. Otherwise a control code cancels the prefix: CR, BEL,
BS, HT, LF, VT and FF run their handlers, ESC is ignored, and any other code below $20
starts a prefix sequence (stored in sbf_CtrlPrefix, buffer cleared by OSIsq). A printable
byte is upper-cased when the window has caps (WDFH_B_CAPS) and falls into ScrD_PutChar.
Entry: A = byte; IX = active window; HL = cursor position.
Exit: HL = new cursor position.

12006.synopsis:
Gives the character code of the user-defined character numbered in sbf_VDU1: the number is
taken modulo 64 with 128K or more RAM (codes $C0-$FF) and modulo 32 otherwise ($E0-$FF),
checked with Chk128KB, and complemented.
Entry: sbf_VDU1 = character number.
Exit: A = complement of the number ($C0-$FF).
Changes: AF.

12056.synopsis:
Searches a column of the 4-byte-per-entry key/character/LORES table (Key2Chr_tbl,
Chr2VDU_tbl or VDU2Chr_tbl) for A. The search ends at an entry whose byte in this column and
the next are both 0. VDU2ChrCode loads HL = VDU2Chr_tbl and falls in here.
Entry: A = byte to find; HL = the column's label.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1, HL = the matching entry's byte in the next column.
Error: Fc = 1 when not found (HL near the table's end).
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: A, DE.

12135.synopsis:
Tells whether a character has bold and tiny variants in the LORES font: codes $08-$7F do.
Entry: A = character code.
Exit: Fc = 0 when A is $08-$7F; Fc = 1 otherwise.
Changes: F.

12162.synopsis:
Stores one byte of a prefix (SOH) sequence in its buffer: +0 the count of bytes still
expected, +1 the low byte of the write pointer, then the bytes. The first byte sets the
length: $80-$94 gives length 0-20, a digit gives its value, and any other byte is stored as
a one-byte sequence. A length of 0 cancels the sequence (falls into Zero_ctrlprefix). When
the last byte arrives, +0 is set to the sequence length.
Entry: A = byte; HL = sequence buffer (sbf_PrefixSeq).
Exit: Fc = 0, A = 0 when the sequence is complete; Fc = 1 while bytes are still expected (A
= -1, or the length that was set).

12190.synopsis:
Ends the open prefix sequence: clears sbf_CtrlPrefix. StorePrefixed falls in here when a
sequence length of 0 is given.
Entry: none.
Exit: sbf_CtrlPrefix = 0.
Keeps: all registers and flags.

12314.synopsis:
Shows the cursor of window IX when the window has a cursor (WDFH_B_CURSOR) and it is not on
already: saves the attribute byte at the cursor cell in wdf_crsrattr and sets it to flash
(LORES cells also get the LORES cursor bits), then sets WDFH_B_CURSORON.
Entry: IX = window frame.
Exit: HL = cursor cell's attribute byte when shown.
Changes: AF, HL.

12347.synopsis:
Hides the cursor of window IX: when WDFH_B_CURSORON is set, puts the saved attribute byte
(wdf_crsrattr) back at the cursor cell and clears the flag.
Entry: IX = window frame.
Exit: HL = cursor position (L = wdf_crsrx, H = wdf_crsry).
Changes: AF, HL.

12369.synopsis:
Turns window coordinates into a screen position: L = 2*C + wdf_startx (two bytes per
character cell), H = B + wdf_starty.
Entry: B = row; C = column; IX = window frame.
Exit: HL = screen position.
Changes: AF, HL.

12382.synopsis:
Turns a screen position into window coordinates, the inverse of ScrD_GetNewXY: C = (L -
wdf_startx) / 2, B = H - wdf_starty.
Entry: HL = screen position; IX = window frame.
Exit: B = row; C = column.
Changes: AF, BC.

12395.synopsis:
Screen driver command "JC": sets centred justification (3) by counting E up through
SetLeftJustify and SetRightJustify into SetNormalJustify.
Entry: E = 0 (set by CallFuncDE); IX = window frame.
Exit: justification bits of wdf_flagsHi = 3.
Changes: AF, E.

12396.synopsis:
Screen driver command "JL": sets left justification (2); falls through SetRightJustify into
SetNormalJustify.
Entry: E = 0 (set by CallFuncDE); IX = window frame.
Exit: justification bits of wdf_flagsHi = 2.
Changes: AF, E.

12397.synopsis:
Screen driver command "JR": sets right justification (1); falls into SetNormalJustify.
Entry: E = 0 (set by CallFuncDE); IX = window frame.
Exit: justification bits of wdf_flagsHi = 1.
Changes: AF, E.

12398.synopsis:
Screen driver command "JN": writes E into the justification bits (WDFH_JUSTIFICATION) of
wdf_flagsHi; E = 0 means normal justification.
Entry: E = justification (0 normal, 1 right, 2 left, 3 centre); IX = window frame.
Exit: wdf_flagsHi updated.
Changes: AF.

12414.synopsis:
Makes room for the next character under the window's justification. With normal
justification it does nothing. Otherwise it finds the edges of the text on the cursor's row
(a null cell or the window edge, from the right margin, the left margin or the middle of the
margins) and, unless the target cell is already null, moves the characters between the edges
one cell (two bytes) to the left.
Entry: HL = cursor position; IX = window frame.
Exit: HL = the cell the next character goes to.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, AF'.

12609.synopsis:
Checks a new row against window IX: builds the position with row C and the cursor's column
(ScrD_GetNewXY) and tests it with NewYValid.
Entry: C = new row; HL = cursor position; IX = window frame.
Exit: Fc = 0, D = the new row's screen line, E = cursor column byte.
Error: Fc = 1 when the row is outside the window.
Changes: AF, B, DE.
Keeps: HL.

12799.synopsis:
Resets the attributes of window IX: clears wdf_flagsHi, wdf_f2, wdf_f6 and wdf_flagsLo.
InitWindowFrame falls in here; it is also the $7F function of ScrDrvAttrTable (reset all
toggles).
Entry: IX = window frame.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1; BC = 0.
Changes: F, BC.

12827.synopsis:
Entry inside SelClearWd: resets the window's attributes (ResetWdAttrs), marks it initialised
(WDF2_B_INITIALIZED) and jumps to ClearScr. SelInitWd calls it when a window is selected for
the first time.
Entry: IX = window frame.
Exit: as ClearScr.

12867.synopsis:
Reads the cursor position of window IX. SelHoldWd falls in here after selecting a window.
Entry: IX = window frame.
Exit: L = wdf_crsrx; H = wdf_crsry.
Changes: HL.

12874.synopsis:
Stores HL as the cursor position of window IX.
Entry: HL = cursor position; IX = window frame.
Exit: wdf_crsrx = L; wdf_crsry = H.
Keeps: all registers.

12910.synopsis:
Checks a window number argument: the screen driver passes it less $20, so A + $20 must be
the digit '1'-'8'.
Entry: A = window digit - $20.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = window index 0-7.
Error: Fc = 1 when it is not '1'-'8'.
Changes: AF.

13014.synopsis:
Screen driver command ".": passes the rest of the sequence to DC_Gen, with BHL = sbf_VDU1 in
the screen base bank (ubScreenBase) and C = the sequence length less 1.
Entry: sbf_PrefixSeq = sequence length.
Exit: as DC_Gen.
Keeps: HL.

13032.synopsis:
Table of the screen driver's SOH commands, read by FindSDCmd: 27 entries of 4 bytes (the
command letter, a second byte that must match sbf_VDU1 or 0 for any, the handler's address),
ended by 0. CallFuncDE calls the handler with A, B, C = the next three sequence bytes less
$20 and E = 0.

13141.synopsis:
Table of the screen driver's one-letter SOH sequences, read by ScrDrvGetAttrBits. Three
kinds of 3-byte entries, ended by 0: 12 attribute toggles (letter, wdf_flagsLo bits,
wdf_flagsHi bits); three functions ($FF scroll up, $FE scroll down, $7F ResetWdAttrs) with
the handler's address; 27 special characters (code, LORES code, control byte: bit 0 selects
LORES $100-$1FF, bits 1-2 make it 2 or 3 cells wide).

13398.synopsis:
Frees a handle and its memory: FreeMemData0 releases the data, FreeHandle releases the
handle by its type (hnd_Type). Entry inside OSSr_FUS after its handle check; file and
filesystem code jump here too.
Entry: IX = handle.
Exit: handle and memory freed.
Keeps: AF.

13537.synopsis:
Key-to-character table, one table seen through three labels a byte apart: 90 entries of 4
bytes (internal key code, ISO Latin-1 code, LORES font code low byte, high byte), bold and
tiny variants included, followed by zero bytes that end the search. OS_In searches this
column with Chr2ScreenCode to turn a foreign key code into its ISO character.

13538.synopsis:
Second column of the key-to-character table (see Key2Chr_tbl): the ISO Latin-1 code of each
entry. Char2VDU searches it with Chr2ScreenCode to find a character's LORES code, read from
the next two bytes.

13539.synopsis:
Third column of the key-to-character table (see Key2Chr_tbl): the low byte of each entry's
LORES font code, followed by the high byte. VDU2ChrCode searches it with Chr2ScreenCode.

14094.synopsis:
OS_Si SI_FTX (flush transmit buffer), kernel 1 part: not available.
Entry: none.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Na always.
Changes: AF.

14104.synopsis:
Reads a Panel parameter into DE: calls OS_Nq with DE = 2, which returns the value in DE.
Entry: BC = parameter (PA_xxx).
Exit: DE = value.
Changes: AF, DE.

14110.synopsis:
Turns a baud rate into its register code: looks DE up in BaudRates and returns its index. A
rate not in the table gives BR_9600.
Entry: DE = baud rate.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = code 0-7.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, AF'.

14143.synopsis:
Table of the baud rates the serial port supports, read by BaudToReg: 8 words (75, 300, 600,
1200, 2400, 9600, 19200, 38400) in register code order, ended by a zero word.

14387.synopsis:
Printer filter, one character. FF, LF and CR go to PrntFF, PrntLF and PrntCR. Any other
character first sends pending attribute changes (ApplyAttrs); a space is only counted in
PendingSpaces. Otherwise pending spaces are printed, then:
1. When an attribute that is on uses a placeholder, its 'on' string is printed with the
placeholder replaced by the character.
2. Otherwise the character is looked up in Translations; a match prints its translation
string (OS_Nq), and anything else goes to PutChar as it is.
Entry: A = character, also in prtInChar; StackBufPtr = 33-byte stack buffer.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 from the serial output.

14548.synopsis:
Sends a byte to the printer: when output is enabled (PRT_B_ENABLED in Flags) writes it to
the serial port with OSSiPbt and the default timeout (BC = -1).
Entry: A = byte.
Exit: Fc = 0 (also when output is disabled).
Error: as OSSiPbt.
Keeps: BC, HL.

14700.synopsis:
Table of 6 words: the handlers of the printer filter's control sequences after the 8
attribute letters of CtrlChars, in its order: FilterOn ('['), FilterOff (']'), Microspace
('h'), ResetAttrs ('s'), SetPageLen ('p'), SendHex ('$'). OSPrtPrntCtrlSeq reads it.

14712.synopsis:
The printer filter's control sequence letters, ended by 0, searched by OSPrtPrntCtrlSeq
after OR $20: "ubxilrae" (attributes 0-7, toggled in AttrUnderline to AttrUserdef), then
'{', '}', 'h', 's', 'p', '$' (handlers in CtrlSeqFuncs; '{' and '}' match '[' and ']').

14757.synopsis:
Converts an ASCII hex digit ('0'-'9', 'A'-'F' or 'a'-'f') to its value.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = value 0-15.
Error: Fc = 0 when A is not a hex digit.
Changes: AF.

14919.synopsis:
Sends the pending attribute changes: for each of the 8 printer attributes, from AttrUserdef
down to AttrUnderline, with PRA_B_PENDING set, prints pending spaces and toggles it with
ToggleAttr (C = the new state).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 from the serial output.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14947.synopsis:
Toggles a printer attribute: flips PRA_B_ON at (HL), clears PRA_B_PENDING and, unless the
attribute uses a placeholder, prints its 'on' or 'off' string (GetPAtoggle,
PrntStackBuffer).
Entry: HL = attribute byte; B = attribute number 1-8; C = 1 for on, 0 for off.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 from the serial output.
Changes: AF, DE.
Keeps: BC, HL.

14988.synopsis:
Prints the spaces counted in PendingSpaces with PutChar and clears the count.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = $20 after printing, A = 0 when there were none.
Error: Fc = 1 from the serial output (count kept).
Keeps: BC.

15013.synopsis:
Reads a Panel or PrinterEd parameter into DE: OS_Nq with DE = 2, then tests the length.
Entry: BC = parameter.
Exit: DE = value; A = returned length; Fz = 1 when it is 0 (parameter not set); Fc = 0.
Changes: AF, DE.

15020.synopsis:
Gives the OS_Nq reason of a printer translation's character: B = $80, C = $48 + 2*A for
Tr1-Tr9 (A = 0-8) and $6E + 2*A for Tr10 upwards. The translation string is the next reason
(BC + 1).
Entry: A = translation index from 0.
Exit: BC = reason.
Changes: AF, BC.

15033.synopsis:
Resets the printer filter's state: clears the on and pending bits of the 8 attributes,
keeping their reset-at-CR and placeholder bits, sets PendingSpaces and Rows to 0 and PageLen
to 66.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = 66.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

64.synopsis:
Shift table of the British keymap (KeyMap_UK, used for the UK, US, IS, JP and TR country
settings), at offset $40 of the keymap's page, after the 64-byte key matrix. A count byte,
then that many pairs (key code, code with Shift held) in ascending key-code order, for the
keys outside A-Z that are not in the Caps table. This keymap has 23 pairs. The Caps,
Diamond, Square and dead-key tables follow it; at reset the country setup (os/spnq1.asm)
records where each starts, and the keyboard driver (os/kbd.asm) searches them.

111.synopsis:
Caps table of the British keymap: a count byte, then that many pairs (lower case, upper
case) of keys outside A-Z that CAPS LOCK and Shift switch between. The table is empty here
(count 0).

112.synopsis:
Diamond table of the British keymap: a count byte, then that many pairs (key code, code with

135.synopsis:

1980.synopsis:

2048.synopsis:
Start of the LOWRAM code (rst.asm, low_int.asm, memfunc.asm, flash.asm), which the reset
code (os/reset.asm) copies from this bank into RAM bank $20 and runs at $0000, up to
LowRAMcode_end. It holds the RST vectors, the interrupt entries, the OZ call dispatch and
return, the fast bank binding (RST 30H, EXTCALL) and the flash chip routines. At $0000
itself is the RST 00 reset entry: it disables interrupts and writes 0 to BL_COM, which binds
ROM bank 0 into the lower 8K of segment 0, so execution continues in bank 0's boot code.
Entry: none.

2104.synopsis:
Maskable interrupt entry (RST 38H, interrupt mode 1): a JP to LOWRAM_INT. The jump's address
is patched: nmi_halt points it at kernel 0's HW_INT before the machine enters coma, and
NMIWakeup restores LOWRAM_INT.
Entry: none.

2125.synopsis:
Default application error handler, installed by OS_Erh when HL = 0 and at process start
(DefErrHandler + 1 when the application DOR sets AT2_Ie, ignore errors). CallErrorHandler
calls it through JpAHL with the error in AF. When Fz = 1 (a fatal error) it returns AF
unchanged, so CallErrorHandler shows the error with GN_Err. Otherwise, and always from the
second byte, CP A gives Fc = 0, Fz = 1, which returns the error to the program.
Entry: A = error code; Fc = 1; Fz = 1 for a fatal error.
Exit: Fz = 1 on entry: AF unchanged; else Fc = 0, Fz = 1.
Changes: F.

2138.synopsis:
Second half of the dispatch of a two-byte OZ call (os/oz2call.asm jumps here): pops the code
bank into A and binds it into segment 3 (MS3BankA), pops the caller's AF and returns, which
goes to the function address the dispatcher pushed under them. Its last two instructions
(noEI: POP AF, RET) are also LOWRAM_NMI's exit when interrupts stay disabled.
Entry: stack: code bank in A of the top word, then the caller's AF, then the function
address.
Exit: S3 = code bank; AF = caller's AF.

2150.synopsis:
Non-maskable interrupt entry (NMI at $0066): a JP to LOWRAM_NMI. The jump's address is
patched like OZ_INT's: nmi_halt points it at kernel 0's HW_NMI before coma and NMIWakeup
restores it; the OZ update code (dc/ozupdate.asm) replaces the JP with RET while it
reprograms the flash.
Entry: none.

2153.synopsis:
Handles a non-maskable interrupt from the Blink. If SP is in page $00xx the machine is still
in its start-up code and it restarts at RST 00. Otherwise it saves I and the interrupt state
(IFF2, read through LD A,I), disables interrupts, binds kernel 0 into segment 3, calls
NMIEntry there, restores segment 3 and returns, enabling interrupts only when they were
enabled before. It returns with RET, not RETN, because NMIEntry uses EI and DI around HALT.
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2189.synopsis:
Return path of an OZ call that never calls the application's error handler: the caller gets
the handler's AF, BC, DE and HL. It pops the stacked S2/S3 word, clears the carry of that
copy so OZErrorHandler is skipped, restores segment 3 from the stacked S2/S3 word (only
BLSC_SR3 and BL_SR3 are written), decrements ubAppCallLevel and returns to the caller of the
OZ call.
Entry: AF, BC, DE, HL = results; stack: S2/S3 word, then the return address.
Exit: AF, BC, DE, HL as on entry; S3 restored.

2194.synopsis:
Return path of an OZ call that gives the caller the handler's AF, BC, DE and HL (EXX here
and again in OZCallReturn3, so the main set is kept); falls into OZCallReturn2. Like the
other return entries it restores segment 3 from the stacked S2/S3 word (only BLSC_SR3 and
BL_SR3 are written), decrements ubAppCallLevel and returns to the caller of the OZ call;
unlike OZCallReturn0, when the result has Fc = 1 and the call level reaches 0 (the
application's outermost call) it calls OZErrorHandler.
Entry: AF, BC, DE, HL = results; stack: S2/S3 word, then the return address.
Exit: AF, BC, DE, HL as on entry; S3 restored.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code; the application's error handler may run first.

2195.synopsis:
Return path of an OZ call that gives the caller the handler's AF but its own BC, DE and HL
from the alternate set (EX AF,AF' here, EXX in OZCallReturn3); falls into OZCallReturn3. The
tail is OZCallReturn1's, error handler call included.
Entry: AF = result; BC', DE', HL' = the caller's values; stack: S2/S3 word, then the return
address.
Exit: AF = result; BC, DE, HL = the caller's values; S3 restored.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code; the application's error handler may run first.

2196.synopsis:
Return path of an OZ call that gives the caller back its own AF, BC, DE and HL from the
alternate sets (EXX here; AF' is swapped in by the common tail); falls into OZCallReturnFP.
The error handler check uses the caller's own carry.
Entry: AF', BC', DE', HL' = the caller's values; stack: S2/S3 word, then the return address.
Exit: AF, BC, DE, HL = the caller's values; S3 restored.

2197.synopsis:
Return path of an FPP call (fp/fpp.asm): the caller gets its own AF from the alternate set
and the handler's BC, DE and HL. It pops the stacked S2/S3 word, sets its carry, restores
segment 3 from the stacked S2/S3 word (only BLSC_SR3 and BL_SR3 are written), decrements
ubAppCallLevel and returns to the caller of the OZ call; when AF' has Fc = 1 and the call
level reaches 0 it calls OZErrorHandler.
Entry: BC, DE, HL = results; AF' = AF to return; stack: S2/S3 word, then the return address.
Exit: AF = AF' on entry; BC, DE, HL as on entry; S3 restored.

2218.synopsis:
Calls the application's error handler for an OZ call that returned an error. Returns at once
when Fc = 0. Otherwise binds kernel 0 into segment 3, calls CallErrorHandler (os/error.asm)
with A = the bank to bind for the handler and the error in AF', then rebinds that bank into
segment 3 through MS3BankA.
Entry: A = bank of segment 3 to restore; Fc = 1 to call the handler; AF' = error result.
Exit: segment 3 = the bank in A.

2231.synopsis:
Calls the routine at HL in the bank in A bound into segment 3: binds A through MS3BankA,
swaps AF so the routine gets AF', calls it through JpHL, swaps its returned AF into AF',
then falls into MS3Kernel0, which binds kernel 0 back into segment 3. Used to call an
application's error handler and entry points (error.asm, process0.asm).
Entry: A = bank; HL = address in segment 3; AF' = AF for the routine.
Exit: AF' = AF returned by the routine; A = KN0_BNK; segment 3 = kernel 0.
Changes: AF, AF', and what the routine changes.

2239.synopsis:
Binds kernel bank 0 into segment 3: loads A = KN0_BNK and falls into MS3BankA.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = KN0_BNK; segment 3 = kernel 0.
Changes: A.

2241.synopsis:
Binds the bank in A into segment 3: writes it to the soft copy BLSC_SR3 and to port BL_SR3.
Entry: A = bank.
Exit: segment 3 = bank in A.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

2273.synopsis:
Jumps to the address in HL (JP (HL)); CALL JpHL calls it. It is also the end of CallOZMain,
which reaches it with HL = $FFnn, the entry for call byte nn in OS_TBL of kernel 0, bound in
segment 3. Called from JpAHL, ExtCallK0 and pfilter0.asm.
Entry: HL = address.

2445.synopsis:
Calls kernel 0's BothShifts through ExtCallK0 (on the system stack, with kernel 0 bound into
segment 3) and returns its result. Used by the interrupt handler while the keyboard is
locked, to see whether both Shift keys are down.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0 when only both Shift keys (and maybe Shift Lock) are down, A bit 4 = Shift
Lock; Fc = 1, Fz = 1 when one Shift key is down; Fc = 1, Fz = 0 when other keys are down.
Changes: AF, BC.
Keeps: DE, HL.

2608.synopsis:
Disables the UART interrupt (clears BM_INTUART in BLSC_INT and writes it to BL_INT) until
the serial receive buffer is emptied. Called by the RDRF interrupt code when the buffer is
full.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

2634.synopsis:
Reloads the automatic switch-off counter ubTimeoutCnt from the Panel's time-out ubTimeout
(minutes). A non-zero value is stored plus one, so the counter is not 30 seconds shorter
than set; 0 (no time-out) is stored as it is. Called on each key press and while the small
timer runs.
Entry: none.
Keeps: all registers.

2664.synopsis:
Drives the beeper on each TICK interrupt (unless ITSK_B_PREEMPTION is set).
1. With no sound running (ubSoundCount = 0): a pending keyclick (KBF_B_BEEP) is cleared and
turns the speaker on; otherwise the speaker is silenced if it runs.
2. Otherwise it sets the speaker for the current phase (intb_beep4: odd ubSoundCount = mark,
sounding; even = space) and decrements ubSoundActive.
3. When that reaches 0 it decrements ubSoundCount and loads ubSoundActive with the next
space or mark count, skipping zero counts; at count 0 the speaker is silenced. The speaker
is set by bit BB_COMSRUN of BLSC_COM, written to BL_COM.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, HL.

2724.synopsis:
Sets the speaker for a beep phase: clears BB_COMSRUN in BLSC_COM, sets it again when Fc = 1
and the sound setting cSound is 'Y' (the 3K2 tone drives the speaker), and writes BLSC_COM
to BL_COM.
Entry: Fc = 1 for a mark (sounding) phase, Fc = 0 for a space.
Changes: AF, HL.

2908.synopsis:
Finds the slot of the code that made an EXTCALL with a slot-relative bank ($00-$3F): reads
the soft copy of the bank bound in the segment that H addresses and returns its slot bits.
ExtCall ORs them with the relative bank number.
Entry: H = high byte of an address in the calling code.
Exit: A = slot mask (bits 7-6 of the bound bank); BC = address of the segment's soft copy.
Changes: AF, BC.

3019.synopsis:
End of the LOWRAM code: the first address after the block that the reset code copies to RAM.
The assembly fails if it reaches SV_PRESERVED_RAM ($0400).

13056.synopsis:
Date filter table of the UK, run at $7300 in segment 1, also used for the US, IS, JP and TR
country settings. The country setup (os/spnq1.asm) stores the address of the selected
country's table in uwGnDateFilter; GN_Gdt and GN_Pdt (gn/gnaconv.asm) and GNLdm
(gn/gnldm.asm) open it with GN_Flo. It translates between the language's words and the
one-byte codes of the GN date routines (GN_Pdt uses reverse mode). Layout: a word, the
table's length; a byte of left-hand flags and one of right-hand flags (FL_ALPHA, FL_ISO,
...); then pairs of length-prefixed strings, the length byte counting itself: the word, then
