at IX with seconds and leading zeroes into a 9-byte stack buffer (GN_Ptm), edits it with
GN_Sip until a cursor key or Enter, converts it with GN_Gtm (an invalid time beeps and is
edited again) and stores it at IX. The cursor is on while editing.
Entry: IX = 3-byte internal time; B = column; C = row.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the input; (IX+0..2) = the new time.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from GN_Ptm or GN_Sip.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, AF'.
Keeps: BC, IX.

10688.synopsis:
Fetches the handle of the standard output (OS_Nq, NQ_Out). The Clock, Calendar and Alarm
copy; the Diary has its own.
Entry: none.
Exit: IX = standard output handle.
Keeps: BC.

10696.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to a column of the current row (SOH "2X").
Entry: B = column.
Changes: AF.

10708.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to a position in the current window (SOH "3@").
Entry: B = column; C = row.
Changes: AF.

10725.synopsis:
Applies the current hardware toggles (reverse, flash, grey, underline) to the next
characters from the cursor (SOH "2A").
Entry: A = 32 + number of characters.

10750.synopsis:
Toggles tiny type, then falls into ToggleRvrs to toggle reverse video.
Entry: none.

10753.synopsis:
Entry inside ToggleTR: toggles reverse video (SOH "R").
Entry: none.

10765.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to (0,0) and clears the current window.
Entry: none.

10784.synopsis:
Clears from the cursor to the end of the line.
Entry: none.

10792.synopsis:
The text "DATE", null-terminated: the name of the mailbox the Calendar reads and writes with
OS_Sr (SR_RPD, SR_WPD).

10797.synopsis:
The Clock popdown's entry, reached from the vector at the start of the code.
1. Enables escape detection and checks the OZ version (OS_Nq, NQ_Voz); leaves with OS_Bye on
an older OZ.
2. Opens window 5 with GN_Win (MainWindowDef) and reserves 7 bytes at IX: a time, a date and
the menu selector (IX+6).
3. Clears the window, prints the "ESC SET" menu on the bottom line and highlights it
(ClkHighlight1).
4. Reads the date (GN_Gmd), formats it in full (GN_Pdt) and prints the weekday, the day and
month, and the year on three centred lines.
5. Prints the time with seconds at (3,5) (DisplayTime); when GN_Gmt finds the time
inconsistent with the date read (Fz = 0), redraws from step 3.
6. Waits 25 centiseconds for a key (OS_Tin) and dispatches it through ClkKeyCmds_tbl;
success redraws from step 3, RC_Susp and RC_Time update the time, RC_Fail waits again,
anything else (RC_Esc acknowledged) leaves through Exit.

11054.synopsis:
The Clock's command table for KeyJump: Right (Clock_Right), Left (Clock_Left) and Enter
(Clock_Enter), ended by 0.

11075.synopsis:
Left in the Clock: toggles the menu selector (IX+6) between ESC and SET and redraws the
highlight. Clock_Right continues here.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail, so the clock waits for the next key without redrawing.
Keeps: BC.

11097.synopsis:
Right in the Clock: toggles the menu selector (IX+6) between ESC and SET; continues in
Clock_Left to redraw the highlight.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail.
Keeps: BC.

11111.synopsis:
Draws the Clock's menu highlight on row 6: removes the reverse from the 16-character bar,
then reverses the 7 characters of the selected entry (column 0 for ESC, 7 for SET, from bit
0 of IX+6); then toggles tiny and reverse back.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Changes: AF, BC.

11150.synopsis:
The Clock's SET command, reached through ClkCmds_tbl: clears the window, shows the "NEW
DATE" and "NEW TIME" titles, reads the time into (IX+0..2) (GN_Gmt) and the date into
(IX+3..5) (GN_Gmd), shows the time and runs the two fields of ClkSet_tbl with NavigateTable.
After Enter, sets the time (GN_Pmt) and the date (GN_Pmd) with alarm handling suspended
(OS_Alm AH_AINC, AH_ADEC). Selects ESC in the menu again.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from NavigateTable; the date and time are not set.

11255.synopsis:
The date field of the Clock's SET form: edits the date at IX+3 at (2,2) with AskDate.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame Exit, Error: as AskDate.
Keeps: IX.

11271.synopsis:
The time field of the Clock's SET form: edits the time at IX at (3,5) with AskTime.
Entry: IX = the Clock's 7-byte frame Exit, Error: as AskTime.

11277.synopsis:
Prints the time at IX with seconds and leading zeroes at (3,5); continues in DisplayTime.
Entry: IX = 3-byte internal time.

11288.synopsis:
The fields of the Clock's SET form for NavigateTable: a 0 start mark, SetDate, SetTime and
the $FFFF end mark.

11296.synopsis:
The Clock's menu commands for TableJump, indexed by the selector: Exit (ESC) and Cl_Set
(SET).

11300.synopsis:
The Clock's GN_Win window definition: window 5 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel
banner ($A5), at (78,0), 14 columns by 8 rows, banner clock_banner.

11313.synopsis:
The Calendar popdown's entry, reached from the vector at the start of the code and again
after RC_Draw.
1. Enables escape detection and checks the OZ version (OS_Nq, NQ_Voz); leaves with OS_Bye on
an older OZ.
2. Clears its 33 bytes of workspace and opens window 5 (CalWindow_txt).
3. Reads a date and a diary entry from the "DATE" mailbox (OS_Sr, SR_RPD); with one, follows
the diary's entry list from it. Without one, or when InitMonth rejects it, takes today's
date (GN_Gmd), and a fixed date when that is rejected too.
4. Writes the date into the mailbox (SR_WPD), draws its month (DrawMonth), highlights the
day and runs the keys of CalKeyCmds_tbl with KeyJump0.
5. Restarts after RC_Draw; leaves through Exit otherwise.

11460.synopsis:
The Calendar's command table for KeyJump0: Enter (Cal_Enter), Shift Up and Down (Cal_SUp,
Cal_SDown), Diamond Up and Down (Cal_DUp, Cal_DDown), Down, Left, Up and Right (Cal_Down,
Cal_Left, Cal_Up, Cal_Right), Square Right and Left (Cal_ARight, Cal_ALeft), ended by 0.

11530.synopsis:
Left in the Calendar: moves to the previous day; from the 1st, draws the previous month and
highlights its last day.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11564.synopsis:
Down in the Calendar: moves a week on; past the month's end, draws the next month and
highlights the same weekday in its first week.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11613.synopsis:
Up in the Calendar: moves a week back; in the first week, draws the previous month and
highlights the same weekday in its last week.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11651.synopsis:
Shift Down in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the next month (the month's last day if
it is shorter); continues in Cal_SUpDn.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11656.synopsis:
Shift Up in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the previous month (the month's last day
if it is shorter). Falls into Cal_SUpDn, which takes the 1st of the new month in ABC, draws
the month and highlights the day.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11693.synopsis:
Diamond Down in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the same month a year later; joins
Cal_DUp to make the date (GN_Dei) and continues in Cal_SUpDn.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11703.synopsis:
Diamond Up in the Calendar: moves to the same day of the same month a year earlier; makes
the 1st of that month (GN_Dei) and continues in Cal_SUpDn.
Entry: D = the highlighted day of the month.
Exit: Fc = 0; D = the new day.

11724.synopsis:
Enter in the Calendar: asks for a date after "Look for : " on row 7, starting from today's,
and moves to it (MoveToDay), redrawing the month when needed; asks again when MoveToDay
fails. Escape abandons the input (tj_2). Then clears the prompt line and highlights the day.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from AskDate other than RC_Esc.
Changes: IX (left pointing at the freed 3-byte buffer).

11798.synopsis:
Makes the 1st of the month before the one in ubMonth and swYear (December of the year before
for January); shares its end with NextMonth.
Entry: none (ubMonth, swYear).
Exit: ABC = internal date of the 1st of the month.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from GN_Dei.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

11819.synopsis:
Makes the 1st of the month after the one in ubMonth and swYear (January of the year after
for December) with GN_Dei.
Entry: none (ubMonth, swYear).
Exit: ABC = internal date of the 1st of the month.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from GN_Dei.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

11848.synopsis:
Fills the Calendar's month variables from a date: MonthStart (the 1st, internal format),
swYear, ubMonth, ubNMonthDays, ubDay (the date's day of the month) and ubWeekday (the
weekday of the 1st), using GN_Die and GN_Dei.
Entry: ABC = internal date.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 from GN_Die or GN_Dei.
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: A, BC, DE.

11908.synopsis:
Makes a date the Calendar's current day: fills the month variables (InitMonth), stores the
date in CurrentDay and redraws the month (DrawMonth) when the date is outside the month
drawn.
Entry: ABC = internal date.
Exit: Fc = 0; E = A.
Error: Fc = 1 from InitMonth; the month variables may be partly updated.

11971.synopsis:
Draws the month set up by InitMonth.
1. Clears the window; records the month's first day (DrawnMonthStart, SearchDay) and the
first day of the next month (NextMonthStart); positions the diary list before the month
(FindPrevDiaryEntry).
2. Prints the month name (GN_Ldm) and the year (GN_Pdn, at least 4 digits below 100, " BC"
for a negative year) centred on the first line, and reverses that line.
3. Prints the short weekday names, Monday first, in tiny underlined type.
4. Prints the day numbers from the weekday of the 1st, five columns each, with a bullet in
front of a day that has a diary entry (DrawMonthDay).
Entry: none (the month variables).
Keeps: DE.

12202.synopsis:
Square Right in the Calendar: moves to the next day after the current one that has a diary
entry (FindNextDiaryEntry, MoveToDay) and highlights it; continues in Cal_ALeft's tail.
Nothing moves when there is none.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.

12210.synopsis:
Square Left in the Calendar: moves to the previous day before the current one that has a
diary entry (FindPrevDiaryEntry, MoveToDay) and highlights it. Nothing moves when there is
none.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.

12236.synopsis:
Copies the current day (CurrentDay) to SearchDay, where a diary-entry search starts.
Entry: none.
Changes: A, HL.

12249.synopsis:
Finds the first diary entry dated after SearchDay. The Diary's entries form an XOR-linked
list walked with GN_Xnx (swapping BHL and CDE reverses the direction); the position is kept
in DiaryEntry (previous) and NextDiaryEntry (current). The search walks backward until an
entry dated before the search day, then forward until one dated after it. A walk stops at
the end of the list or back at OrigDiaryEntry, the entry the Diary passed with the date.
Entry: SearchDay = the day to search from; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = list position.
Exit: Fc = 0: found; NextDiaryDay = its date; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = position on it.
Error: Fc = 1 when no later entry exists (the position is stored all the same).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

12286.synopsis:
Finds the last diary entry dated before SearchDay: walks forward until an entry dated on or
after the search day, then backward until one dated before it, and turns the position to
face forward again. Called by DrawMonth (with SearchDay = first day of the drawn month) and
by Cal_ALeft. The list and its end tests are as in FindNextDiaryEnt.
Entry: SearchDay = the day to search from; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = list position.
Exit: Fc = 0: found; NextDiaryDay = its date; DiaryEntry, NextDiaryEntry = position on it.
Error: Fc = 1 when no earlier entry exists (the position is stored all the same).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE.

12332.synopsis:
Stores the diary list position: CDE (the previous entry) in DiaryEntry and BHL (the current
entry) in NextDiaryEntry.
Entry: CDE = previous entry; BHL = current entry.
Changes: A.

12388.synopsis:
Steps one entry along the diary list with GN_Xnx and tests for the end of the walk: Fz = 1
when the new entry is null or is OrigDiaryEntry (the test at loc_EDF7).
Entry: BHL = current entry; CDE = previous entry.
Exit: BHL = next entry; CDE = the entry left; Fz = 1 at the end of the walk.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

12425.synopsis:
Reads the date of the diary entry at BHL, its bytes 3 to 5 read with GN_Rbe, into
NextDiaryDay (a 3-byte internal date).
Entry: BHL = diary entry (extended address).
Exit: NextDiaryDay = the entry's date; A = its high byte; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: HL.

12463.synopsis:
Subtracts BC days from CurrentDay, a 3-byte internal date, and falls into SetCurDay, which
stores the result.
Entry: BC = number of days.
Exit: CurrentDay = AHL = the new date.
Changes: AF, HL.

12481.synopsis:
Records D as the selected day of the month (ubDay) and falls into HighlightDay.
Entry: D = day of the month.
Changes: AF, D.

12485.synopsis:
Shows the selected day (ubDay) in reverse: moves to its cell in the month grid, cell
ubWeekday - 1 + ubDay (MoveToDayXY), turns reverse on, applies it to the cell's 5 characters
and turns reverse off again.
Entry: ubDay = day of the month; ubWeekday = cell of the month's first day.
Changes: AF, D.

12508.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the selected day: moves to its cell, as HighlightDay does, and
applies the plain attributes (reverse off) to the cell's 5 characters.
Entry: ubDay = day of the month; ubWeekday = cell of the month's first day.
Changes: C.
Keeps: AF.

12528.synopsis:
Prints one day cell of the month grid at the cursor: a space, a bullet (BulletR_txt) when
the day has a diary entry or a space when not, then the day number in 2 digits with a
trailing space (GN_Pdn).
1. Works out the day's date, DrawnMonthStart + C - 1, and compares it with NextDiaryDay.
2. While the day is past NextDiaryDay, steps the diary list forward (GN_Xnx, PutDiaryList,
PutNxtDiaryDay) and compares again; at the end of the list the day gets no bullet.
Entry: C = day of the month (1 = first); NextDiaryDay and the list position from
FindPrevDiaryEnt or the previous cell.
Exit: B = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE.

12610.synopsis:
VDU string SOH, SD_BRGT, 0: the right-pointing bullet DrawMonthDay prints before the number
of a day that has a diary entry.

12613.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to cell A of the month grid (1 = the top left cell, seven cells a row): row
2 + (A - 1) div 7, column 5 * ((A - 1) mod 7), through MoveToXYbc.
Entry: A = cell number.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC.

12636.synopsis: Text " BC", zero-terminated: DrawMonth prints it after the year of a month before year 1.

12640.synopsis: Text "Look for : ", zero-terminated: the date prompt Cal_Enter prints on row 7.

12652.synopsis:
VDU sequence that sets up the Calendar's window: defines window 5 at column 42, row 0, 35
columns wide and 8 rows high (SOH 7 #), selects and clears it (SOH 2 C 5) and turns off
scrolling and the cursor (SOH 3 - S C). Printed by init_calendar with GN_Sop.

12671.synopsis:
Alarm popdown: entry point.
1. Checks the OZ version with OS_Nq (NQ_Voz) and leaves through Exit when it is not this
OZ's version.
2. Enables ESC detection (OS_Esc SC_ENA) and suspends alarms while the popdown runs (OS_Alm
AH_SUSP).
3. At alm_1: draws window 6 with the "ALARMS" title and the column header, and sets up
windows 4 and 5.
4. Clears MailDate and the list state; reads the "DATE" mail into MailDate (OS_Sr SR_RPD).
Without one it takes today's date (GN_Gmd) and reads a "NAME" mail into scratch1; with a
name it loads alarms from that file (AlmLoadMail, AlmLoad2).
5. AlmEntry: draws the list (RedrawAlarms) and runs the key loop (KeyJump0 with
AlmKeyCmds_tbl); RC_Draw starts again at alm_1, anything else falls into AlmExit.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

12892.synopsis:
Leaves the Alarm popdown: re-enables alarms (OS_Alm AH_REV) and jumps to Exit (OS_Bye).
Reached at the end of the key loop, from the ESC button and with command code $04.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

12917.synopsis:
Left arrow in the alarm list: moves the button highlight to the previous of ESC, SET ALARM,
CLEAR ALARM and VIEW ALARM (the low 2 bits of ubAlmActiveButton), from the first to the
last. CLEAR ALARM and VIEW ALARM are refused while no alarm is shown. The shared code at
almlr_2 stores the button and redraws the row (AlmHghlghtButton).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).
Changes: AF, BC.

12954.synopsis:
Right arrow in the alarm list: moves the button highlight to the next button, from the last
to the first, and joins Alm_Left's code at almlr_2.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).
Changes: AF, BC.

12968.synopsis:
Up arrow in the alarm list: moves the selection bar to the previous alarm.
1. Inside the window it moves the bar up a row (ubSelectedAlmPos).
2. On the top row with alarms above, it scrolls the window (SOH SD_UP), redraws the button
row, and prints the previous alarm on row 0 (ubTopVisibleAlarm - 1).
3. On the first alarm it goes to the last: counts the alarms and, with more than five, shows
the last five (DrawAlarms) and selects the last row. Does nothing while no alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).

13073.synopsis:
Down arrow in the alarm list: moves the selection bar to the next alarm. Inside the window
it moves the bar down a row; on the bottom row with an alarm below, it scrolls the window
(SOH SD_DWN), prints that alarm on row 4 and redraws the button row; on the last alarm it
goes to the first, redrawing the list when the first is not shown. Does nothing while no
alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1, A = RC_Fail (KeyJump0 then reads the next key).

13165.synopsis:
CLEAR ALARM: removes the selected alarm (number ubTopVisibleAlarm + ubSelectedAlmPos) from
the alarm chain with GN_Uab and frees its block with GN_Fab when GN_Uab took it out (Fc = 0,
Fz = 1), then redraws the list. Returns at once while no alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: AF as GN_Uab or GN_Fab left it; Fc = 0, A = 0 when no alarm is shown.

13200.synopsis:
VIEW ALARM: shows the selected alarm in full (ViewSingleAlarm) and falls into PressEsc_txt,
which waits for ESC. Returns at once while no alarm is shown.
Entry: none.
Exit: as PressEsc_txt; Fc = 0, A = 0 when no alarm is shown.

13219.synopsis:
Entry inside AlmView, also called after alarms are loaded or saved: prints "PRESS ESC WHEN
READY" on row 5 and reads keys (OS_In) until ESC, ignoring keys and RC_Susp. ESC is
acknowledged and the alarm list redrawn (RedrawAlarms). RC_Draw restarts AlmView, whoever
the caller was.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = 0 after ESC.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Quit and the like).

13291.synopsis:
SET ALARM: creates a new alarm and lets the user edit it.
1. Allocates an alarm block (GN_Aab), binds it in segment 1 and clears its 47 bytes.
2. Fills in the current time (GN_Gmt), the date from MailDate, ALMF_BELL and ALRF_NEVER.
3. Runs the edit form (AlmSetMain); on success links the block into the alarm chain
(GN_Lab). When GN_Lab fails with RC_Fail it beeps and returns to the form.
4. On another error or ESC it frees the block (GN_Fab). Errors other than ESC are reported
(GN_Err); RC_Quit returns at once, any other case redraws the alarm list.
Entry: MailDate = the date to start from.
Exit: Fc = 0: the alarm is set.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Esc when the user left with ESC).

13394.synopsis:
Redraws the alarm list (DrawAlarms) and the selection bar (DrawAlmHilight).
Entry: ubTopVisibleAlarm, ubSelectedAlmPos.

13400.synopsis:
Clears the list window and prints up to five alarms from number ubTopVisibleAlarm, one a
line (GetAlarmByNum, PrintAlarm, GN_Nln). When that alarm no longer exists it starts again
from the first, setting ubTopVisibleAlarm and ubSelectedAlmPos to 0. Stores the count in
ubNumVisibleAlarms, makes ESC the active button and falls into DrawAlmWdBottom.
Entry: ubTopVisibleAlarm = number of the alarm on the top row.
Exit: ubNumVisibleAlarms = alarms shown (0 to 5); IX = last alarm block read.

13457.synopsis:
Prints the button row on row 5 in tiny text ("ESC SET ALARM CLEAR ALARM VIEW ALARM") and
falls into AlmHghlghtButton.
Entry: ubAlmActiveButton = the active button.

13525.synopsis:
Highlights the active button of the button row: with tiny text on, applies the plain
attributes to the 54 characters of row 5, then reverse to the 12 characters of the active
button (low 2 bits of ubAlmActiveButton: 0 ESC at column 1, 1 SET ALARM at 14, 2 CLEAR ALARM
at 27, 3 VIEW ALARM at 40) and turns tiny and reverse off (ToggleTR).
Entry: ubAlmActiveButton = the active button.
Changes: AF, BC.

13562.synopsis:
Entry inside AlmHghlghtButton: moves to column B, row C, turns reverse on, applies the
attributes to 12 characters and turns tiny and reverse off (ToggleTR).
Entry: B = column; C = row (5); tiny text on.
Changes: AF.

13576.synopsis:
Finds alarm number A (0 = the first) in the alarm chain: starts at the list head pAlarmList
and steps with GetNextAlarm.
Entry: A = alarm number.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = the alarm block, bound in segment 1; B = its bank.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Eof when the chain has fewer alarms.
Changes: AF, B, E, IX.

13594.synopsis:
Follows the link of the alarm block at IX (alm_Next, 3 bytes) to the next alarm and binds
its bank in segment 1.
Entry: IX = alarm block or the list head pAlarmList.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = the next alarm block; B = its bank.
Error: Fc = 1 at the end of the chain (A = 0).
Changes: AF, B, IX.
Keeps: C, HL.

13621.synopsis:
Prints alarm IX on the current line: back to column 0 and clears the line, then the date at
column 0 (GN_Pdt, short form with century and '/'), the time with seconds at column 15
(DisplayTime), the reason or command at column 25 and, when ALMF_SHOWBELL is set, a bell
symbol (SD_BLL) at column 50.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: DE, HL.
Keeps: AF, BC, IX.

13712.synopsis:
The alarm edit form: shows the alarm (ViewSingleAlarm) and runs the fields of AlmSet_tbl
through NavigateTable (date, time, reason, bell, type, repeat, number of times); the arrow
keys move between fields, wrapping round, and ENTER ends the form.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fc = 0 after ENTER.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Esc after ESC).

13721.synopsis:
Shows one alarm in full: clears the window, prints the alarm on row 1 (PrintAlarm), the
header "BELL | ALARM TYPE | REPEAT EVERY | No.OF TIMES" on row 3 in tiny reverse, and on row
4 the bell, the type, the repeat interval (GetAlmRepeat, AlmShowRepeat) and the number of
times (AlmShowNTimes).
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.

13821.synopsis:
Date field of the alarm form: edits alm_Date at column 0, row 1 with AskDate.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: as AskDate: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Keeps: IX.

13837.synopsis:
Time field of the alarm form: edits alm_Time at column 15, row 1 with AskTime.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: as AskTime: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Keeps: IX.

13853.synopsis:
Reason field of the alarm form: edits alm_Reason at column 25, row 1 with GN_Sip (buffer of
23, returning on special keys) and the cursor shown, until an arrow key or ENTER (TestKeys).
RC_Susp edits again.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

13901.synopsis:
Bell field of the alarm form: highlights it (DrawBellHilight); up and down toggle ALMF_BELL
in alm_Flags and show it (AlmShowBell); an arrow key or ENTER (TestKeys) ends the edit and
removes the highlight. RC_Susp reads again.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

13954.synopsis:
Type field of the alarm form: as SetABell, with up and down toggling ALMF_EXECUTE (ALARM or
EXECUTE, AlmShowType).
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: Fz = 1; A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

14007.synopsis:
Repeat field of the alarm form: edits the repeat interval as a value and a unit.
1. Highlights the field and gets the value in the current unit (GetAlmRepeat).
2. Down decrements the value, moving to the previous unit at 0; up increments it, moving to
the next unit from NEVER or past 59 seconds or minutes. Shift-down and shift-up change the
unit (rotating alm_RepeatFlags) and reset the value to 1. Each change is shown
(AlmShowRepeat).
3. An arrow key or ENTER stores the value: days, months or years in alm_RepeatDays, weeks as
days (times 7), seconds, minutes or hours as centiseconds in alm_RepeatTime; NEVER stores
nothing. Then removes the highlight.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (nothing stored).

14217.synopsis:
Returns the alarm's repeat interval in the unit set in alm_RepeatFlags: 1 for NEVER;
alm_RepeatTime (centiseconds) divided by 100, 6000 or 360000 for seconds, minutes or hours
(GN_D24); alm_RepeatDays for days, months or years; alm_RepeatDays / 7 for weeks.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: BHL = the interval.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14309.synopsis:
Number of times field of the alarm form: edits alm_RepeatNum. Down and up change it by 1,
with shift by 10 and with diamond by 100, showing each value (AlmShowNTimes); an arrow key
or ENTER stores it and removes the highlight. RC_Susp reads again.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Exit: A = the key that ended the edit.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (nothing stored).

14407.synopsis:
Prints "ON" or "OFF" for ALMF_BELL at column 4, row 4, through the code it shares with
AlmShowType (almt_1).
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

14424.synopsis:
Prints "ALARM" or "EXECUTE" for ALMF_EXECUTE at column 10, row 4.
Entry: IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

14450.synopsis:
Prints the repeat interval at column 21, row 4: blanks the 13 characters, prints the value
in 5 characters (not for NEVER), the unit name from RepeatUnits_tbl for the lowest set bit
of alm_RepeatFlags, and an 'S' unless the value is 1.
Entry: HL = the value (16 bits are printed); IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, DE.
Keeps: BC, HL.

14540.synopsis:
Prints the number of times at column 35, row 4: "NEVER" for 0, "FOREVER" for $FFFF,
otherwise the number in 10 characters.
Entry: HL = number of times; IX = alarm block, bound in.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.
Keeps: HL.

14604.synopsis:
Highlights the type field of the alarm form (column 10, 10 characters) and jumps to
DrawHilight, which moves to row 4, toggles tiny and reverse (ToggleTR) and applies them to
the field. The toggles stay set while the field is edited; RmTypeHilight turns them back.
Changes: AF, BC.

14610.synopsis:
Highlights the repeat field of the alarm form (column 21, 13 characters) through
DrawHilight.
Changes: AF, BC.

14616.synopsis:
Highlights the number of times field of the alarm form (column 35, 11 characters) and falls
into DrawHilight.
Changes: AF, BC.

14633.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the bell field of the alarm form (column 4, 5 characters) and
jumps to RemoveHiligh, which moves to row 4, toggles tiny and reverse back (ToggleTR) and
applies tiny text alone to the field.
Changes: AF, BC.

14639.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the type field (column 10, 10 characters) through RemoveHiligh.
Changes: AF, BC.

14645.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the repeat field (column 21, 13 characters) through RemoveHiligh.
Changes: AF, BC.

14651.synopsis:
Removes the highlight from the number of times field (column 35, 11 characters) and falls
into RemoveHiligh.
Changes: AF, BC.

14674.synopsis:
Draws the selection bar on the selected alarm: turns reverse on, applies it to the row
(RemAlmHilight) and turns reverse off.
Entry: ubSelectedAlmPos, ubNumVisibleAlarms.
Keeps: AF, BC.

14686.synopsis:
Applies the current attributes to the selected alarm's row (49 characters at column 0),
which removes the selection bar with reverse off. ubSelectedAlmPos is first limited to the
last row shown. Does nothing while no alarm is shown.
Entry: ubSelectedAlmPos, ubNumVisibleAlarms.
Keeps: AF, BC.

14912.synopsis:
Asks for a file name: selects window 4, clears it, prints "Filename: " and reads up to 32
characters into scratch1 (GN_Sip), then selects window 5. RC_Susp asks again; ESC is
acknowledged; RC_Quit leaves the popdown (Exit); another error is reported by GN_Err
(do_error), which returns with Fc = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; scratch1 = the name.
Error: Fc = 1 after ESC.

15161.synopsis:
Field table of the alarm form for NavigateTable: a 0 start mark, the field routines
SetADate, SetATime, SetAReason, SetABell, SetAType, SetARepeat and SetATimes, and a -1 end
mark.

15179.synopsis:
Table of 8 words: the unit names of the repeat interval, one per bit of alm_RepeatFlags from
bit 0 (SEC, MIN, HOUR, DAY, WEEK, MONTH, YEAR, NEVER). Read by AlmShowRepeat.

15195.synopsis:
Table of 4 words: the handlers of the button row (AlmExit, AlmSet, AlmClear, AlmView),
indexed by the active button. Alm_Enter jumps through it with TableJump.

15203.synopsis: Text " ON ", zero-terminated: the bell field when the bell is on (AlmShowBell).

15209.synopsis: Text " OFF ", zero-terminated: the bell field when the bell is off (AlmShowBell).

15215.synopsis: Text " ALARM ", zero-terminated: the type field of an alarm (AlmShowType).

15226.synopsis: Text " EXECUTE ", zero-terminated: the type field of a command (AlmShowType).

15237.synopsis:
Text " NEVER ", zero-terminated: the number of times 0 (AlmShowNTimes) and the NEVER entry
of RepeatUnits_tbl.

15249.synopsis: Text " FOREVER ", zero-terminated: the number of times $FFFF (AlmShowNTimes).

15261.synopsis: Text "SEC", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15265.synopsis: Text "MIN", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15269.synopsis: Text "HOUR", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15274.synopsis: Text "DAY", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15278.synopsis: Text "WEEK", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15283.synopsis: Text "MONTH", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15289.synopsis: Text "YEAR", zero-terminated: a unit name of the repeat interval (RepeatUnits_tbl).

15294.synopsis:
Text "NAME", zero-terminated: the name of the mail AlarmEnt reads for a file of alarms to
load.

labels.name: init_crash
labels.synopsis: Hangs in a loop to itself: OS_Bye does not come back.

labels.name: Exit_crash
labels.synopsis: Hangs in a loop to itself: OS_Bye does not come back.

109.synopsis:
The main loop of the Panel and PrinterEd: edits the current entry and runs the command that
ends the edit.
1. Empties the buffer, then copies the entry's saved value into it (StrcpyIX_Buffer).
2. Moves to the field, blanks it and moves back.
3. Edits it: an option list through HandleComboBox, anything else through HandleInputLine,
which return a command code in C ($20-$2E; other codes go back to main_1, which reloads the
saved value).
4. Clears the message line and stores the input (ValidateInput). An error is printed and the
entry edited again (main_2), except for Escape ($20), Next option ($26) and New ($2C).
5. Jumps to the command's handler in CommandTable with MainLoop as its return address.
Entry: IY = the variables (p_ubEntryID); the setting pool and buffers allocated.
Exit: never returns; the commands leave through Exit.

124.synopsis:
Entry inside MainLoop: edits the current entry again without reloading the buffer, so the
text that failed validation stays in the field. MainLoop jumps here after printing the
error.

492.synopsis:
Table of 15 words: the handler of each command code $20-$2E, in order CmdEscape, CmdEnter,
CmdLeft, CmdRight, CmdUp, CmdDown, CmdNextOption, CmdChgPage (twice, $27 and $28), CmdLoad,
CmdSave, CmdName, CmdNew, CmdUpdate and CmdTranslations. MainLoop indexes it with (code -
$20) * 2.

522.synopsis:
The Enter command ($21). In the Panel it applies every setting (CmdUpdate) and leaves
through Exit; in PrinterEd it moves to the next entry like CmdDown.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: PrinterEd: p_ubEntryID = the next entry. Panel: does not return.

533.synopsis:
The Escape command ($20): acknowledges the escape (ClearEsc). The Panel then leaves through
Exit without applying anything; PrinterEd returns to the main loop.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: PrinterEd only: A = the page ID; Fz = 0.

542.synopsis:
Acknowledges a pending escape with OS_Esc (SC_ACK).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF.

549.synopsis:
The cursor-up command ($24): selects the previous entry of the page; from the first entry
($20) it wraps to the last one.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubEntryID = the new entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

576.synopsis:
The cursor-down command ($25): selects the next entry of the page; after the last one it
wraps to the first ($20). CmdEnter falls back on it in PrinterEd.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubEntryID = the new entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

592.synopsis:
The page commands ($27, $28): in PrinterEd switches between page 1 and page 2 (from the
translation page it goes to page 1), selects the first entry and redraws the screen through
DrawScreenLabels. The Panel has one page and returns at once.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubPageID and p_ubEntryID set; the screen redrawn.

614.synopsis:
The translations command ($2E): selects the first entry of PrinterEd's ISO translation page
(page $22) and redraws the screen through DrawScreenLabels.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubPageID = $22; p_ubEntryID = $20.

735.synopsis:
The cursor-left command ($22): selects the entry that comes before the current one in
reading order (the nearest one above it, or left of it on the same row), comparing the
fields' screen positions. With none before it, it wraps to the last entry of the page. Keeps
a 6-byte work area on the stack and leaves through CmdRight's ending.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: p_ubEntryID and p_ubPageID = the new entry.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

845.synopsis:
The next-option command ($26) for a number field with an option list (the baud rates): finds
the buffer's text in the list (MatchComboOption), takes the option after it, copies that
text into the buffer, stores it (ValidateInput) and prints an error if that fails. Does
nothing for a field without a list.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: the buffer and the setting hold the next option.

982.synopsis:
The New command ($2C): resets every parameter of every page to its default with OS_Sp (A =
255), and in PrinterEd the printer name (PA_Ptr) too, then reads the settings back
(StoreDefSettings) and redraws the screen through DrawScreenLabels.
Entry: IY = the variables.

1025.synopsis:
The Load command ($29): asks for a file name (AskFilename), starts a new setting list
(is_1), opens the file and reads it line by line: each line is the entry ID, the page ID and
the value text, stored through vi_4. The end of the file ends it. On an error the file name
is cleared and the settings are read back from OZ (StoreAllSettings). Then closes the file,
redraws the screen and prints any error (CmdSave's ending).
Entry: IY = the variables.
Error: printed; ERR_BadFile for a line without its two ID bytes or a last line without a CR.

1108.synopsis:
The Save command ($2A): asks for a file name (AskFilename), opens it for output and writes
one line for every entry of every page that has a saved value: the entry ID, the page ID,
the value text and a CR (SaveBuffer). Then closes the file, redraws the screen and prints
any error.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Error: printed (PrintError); 0 means the system error.

1215.synopsis:
The Name command ($2B): asks for a file name (AskFilename) and redraws the screen with it,
or prints the error. In PrinterEd the name is the printer's name (PA_Ptr), and its file part
names the application.
Entry: IY = the variables.

1227.synopsis:
Clears the file name and the flag that says the setting pool is bound in, then falls into
is_1: selects the first entry, frees the setting pool and opens a new one.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: Fc = 0; p_pSettingPool = the new pool; p_pSettings = 0 (no settings).
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from OS_Mop.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

1235.synopsis:
Entry inside InitSettings that keeps the file name: selects the first entry of the first
page (InitPagePtrs), closes the setting pool if one is open, opens a new one in segment 1
with OS_Mop and empties the setting list. CmdLoad uses it.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: Fc = 0; p_pSettingPool = the new pool; p_pSettings = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from OS_Mop.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, IX.

1279.synopsis:
Writes the buffer as one line of a saved file: replaces its 0 terminator with a CR and
writes the text and the CR to the open file with OS_Mv.
Entry: the buffer = a 0-terminated text; p_pPrinterFileHandle = the file.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = 0 (the system error; OS_Erc gives it).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

1414.synopsis:
Opens the file name window: defines window 2 (60 by 8 characters at column 10, with a
border), selects and clears it and prints "Filename" at row 1.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1443.synopsis:
Closes the file name window: selects window 1 again and sends 1,"2D2" for window 2.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1511.synopsis:
Leaves the Panel or PrinterEd: closes the setting pool and the memory pool with OS_Mcl and
calls OS_Bye with A = 0. Also reached from MayRedraw and ErrorHandler on RC_Quit.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

1569.synopsis:
Prints the last system error: falls into PrintError with A = 0, which sounds the bell and
prints OZ's text for the error (OS_Erc, GN_Esp), at most 16 characters, on row 2.
Entry: the error to print is OZ's last one.
Exit: Fc = 1.

1637.synopsis:
Table of 7 words: the texts of the program's own errors ERR_OutOfMemory (1) to ERR_BadName
(7), indexed by the code - 1. PrintError reads it.

1651.synopsis: Error text 1 (ERR_OutOfMemory): "Out of memory", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1664.synopsis: Error text 2 (ERR_BadFile): "Bad file", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1672.synopsis: Error text 3 (ERR_Escape): "Escape", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1678.synopsis: Error text 4 (ERR_BadCodeString): "Bad code string", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1693.synopsis: Error text 5 (ERR_StringTooLong): "String too long", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1708.synopsis: Error text 6 (ERR_BadValue): "Bad value", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1717.synopsis: Error text 7 (ERR_BadName): "Bad name", bit 7 set on the last letter.

1725.synopsis:
Sounds the bell: writes BEL with OS_Out.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1730.synopsis:
Hides the cursor: writes 1,"2-C" through CursorOn's ending (CursorOnOff).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

1735.synopsis:
Shows the cursor: writes 1,"2+C".
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

1757.synopsis:
Clears the message line: moves to row 2, column 0 and writes 15 spaces.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

1769.synopsis:
Prints the 0-terminated text that follows the CALL and returns past it. A byte $A0-$BF is a
move: with the next byte it makes a cursor position, row = byte - $A0, column = next byte -
$20 (KprintSpecial). Other bytes go out with OS_Out.
Entry: the text after the CALL.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

1785.synopsis:
KPrint's handler for a byte with bit 7 set. For $A0-$BF it writes 1,"3@", the next byte
(column + $20) and the byte with bit 7 cleared (row + $20), and returns the byte after the
pair for KPrint to print. Other bytes are returned unchanged.
Entry: A = the byte; HL = its address.
Exit: A = the byte to print; HL = its address.
Changes: AF, HL.

1840.synopsis:
Draws the whole screen: defines window 1 (92 by 8 characters), selects and clears it, prints
the current page's labels (ShowPanel, ShowPrEdPg1, ShowPrEdPg2 or ShowPrEdTrans) and every
entry's value. In PrinterEd with a printer name it also prints "PRINTER" and the name
centred under it, and names the application (DC_Nam) after the name's file part.
Entry: IY = the variables.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

1994.synopsis:
Toggles tiny and reverse text: writes 1,"T",1,"R".
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

2084.synopsis:
Copies the 0-terminated text at IX into the buffer (p_pMem_Buffer_100).
Entry: IX = the text.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2202.synopsis:
Says whether the Panel is running: reads the page ID and compares it with the Panel's page
($2A).
Entry: IY = the variables.
Exit: A = the page ID; Fz = 1 for the Panel, 0 for PrinterEd.
Changes: AF.

2208.synopsis:
Returns an entry's OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason: $80 and the entry record's fifth byte.
Entry: HL = the entry record (from GetEntryData).
Exit: BC = the reason; HL = HL + 4.
Changes: BC, HL.

2216.synopsis:
Checks the buffer's text for the current entry and stores it as its setting.
1. A number field with an option list (the baud rates) must match one option (ERR_BadValue).
2. In the Panel the default device and directory are parsed as names (CheckName,
ERR_BadName); in PrinterEd text is checked as a code string (EncodeTranslate).
3. Falls into vi_4 to store it. Option-list fields skip the checks.
Entry: IY = the variables; the buffer = the text.
Exit: Fc = 0, the setting stored.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (ERR_xxx); out of memory is printed here.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2262.synopsis:
Entry inside ValidateInput: stores a text as the setting of one entry, replacing the one it
had (StoreSetting), and copies the text into the new record. CmdLoad stores each line's
value through it.
Entry: HL = the 0-terminated text; B = the page ID; C = the entry ID.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; "Out of memory" printed (PrintError).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

2295.synopsis:
Returns the length of the 0-terminated text in the buffer; falls into StrLen.
Entry: the buffer = the text.
Exit: A = the length; HL = past the terminator; BC = - the length.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

2483.synopsis:
Applies every setting (the Panel's Enter): for every entry of every page sends its value to
OZ with OS_Sp. A Panel number is converted with FP_VAL, FP_ABS and FP_FIX and sent as a byte
or a word; a PrinterEd code string is encoded (EncodeTranslate), and for a field with a
placeholder (flags bit 5) a non-zero placeholder byte is sent to reason + 3 first; text goes
as it is; an entry without a value is sent with A = 255. PrinterEd also sends the printer
name (PA_Ptr). Ends with OS_Sp PA_Gfi, which installs the changed settings. Errors are
printed (PrintSysError).
Entry: IY = the variables.

2940.synopsis:
Entry inside StoreDefSettings, after InitSettings: reads every entry's current value from OZ
(OS_Nq) and stores it as a text setting. A Panel number becomes decimal text (FP_STR); a
PrinterEd code becomes a comma-separated list of decimal numbers (GN_Pdn, built on the
stack); text is kept. PrinterEd first reads the printer name (PA_Ptr) into the file name
buffer.
Entry: IY = the variables; a setting pool open.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when memory runs out.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3118.synopsis:
Table of control character names for PrinterEd's code strings: each record is the name in
capitals followed by its code ($00-$1F), from "NUL" to "US", with synonyms such as "BELL",
"TAB", "XON" and "XOFF"; -1 ends it. EncodeTranslate looks names up in it.

3378.synopsis:
Prints the labels of PrinterEd's page 1 (the printer codes 1-8 and their ON, OFF and Off at
CR fields) through KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

3611.synopsis:
Entry table of PrinterEd's page 2: 25 records (printer on and off, end of page, allow line
feed, the HMI prefix, suffix and offset, then the nine translations' characters and codes),
-1 ends it. Each record is 5 bytes: x + $20, y + $20, the field width, the flags (bit 7
number, bit 6 option list, bit 5 has a placeholder, bit 4 text (with bit 7, a list of
numbers), bits 3-0 the option list's offset in ComboBox_tbl) and the low byte of the
OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason ($80xx). GetEntryData reads it.

3737.synopsis:
Prints the labels of PrinterEd's page 2 (printer on/off, end of page, line feed, HMI and the
translations A to C) through KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

4008.synopsis:
Entry table of PrinterEd's ISO translation page: 64 records in 8 columns of 8, alternating a
character (a number, width 5) and what it changes to (a code string, width 8), for reasons
$80-$BF; $FF ends it. Each record is 5 bytes: x + $20, y + $20, the field width, the flags
(bit 7 number, bit 6 option list, bit 5 has a placeholder, bit 4 text (with bit 7, a list of
numbers), bits 3-0 the option list's offset in ComboBox_tbl) and the low byte of the
OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason ($80xx). GetEntryData reads it.

4329.synopsis:
Prints the labels of PrinterEd's ISO translation page (Ch and To on alternate rows) through
KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

4438.synopsis:
Entry table of the Panel: 15 records (auto repeat, keyclick, insert/overtype, default device
and directory, timeout, sound, map, map size, date format, the baud rates, parity, Xon/Xoff
and the keyboard), -1 ends it. Each record is 5 bytes: x + $20, y + $20, the field width,
the flags (bit 7 number, bit 6 option list, bit 5 has a placeholder, bit 4 text (with bit 7,
a list of numbers), bits 3-0 the option list's offset in ComboBox_tbl) and the low byte of
the OS_Sp/OS_Nq reason ($80xx). GetEntryData reads it.

4514.synopsis:
Prints the Panel's labels and its "PRESS ENTER TO UPDATE" note through KPrint.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

4763.synopsis:
Table of 6 words: the option lists YesNoTxt_tbl, CursorTxt_tbl, FormatTxt_tbl,
ParityTxt_tbl, BaudTxt_tbl and Keymap_tbl, indexed by bits 3-0 of an entry's flags (0, 2,
... 10). GetComboBox reads it.

4775.synopsis:
Option list "Yes" and "No": the texts separated by 0, -1 ends it. An option's key is its
first capital letter or digit.

4782.synopsis: Option list "Insert" and "Overtype", separated by 0, -1 ends it.

4798.synopsis: Option list of the date format, "European" and "American", separated by 0, -1 ends it.

4816.synopsis:
Option list of the parity: "None", "Space", "Mark", "Odd" and "Even", separated by 0, -1
ends it.

4841.synopsis:
Option list of the baud rates: 9600, 19200, 38400, 75, 300, 600, 1200 and 2400, separated by
0, -1 ends it. CmdNextOption steps through it.

4880.synopsis:
Option list of the keyboard layouts: "Uk", "France", "Denmark", "Sweden", "finLand",
"Germany", "usA", "sPain", "Italy" and "Norway", separated by 0, -1 ends it. The capital
letter is each option's key.

5132.synopsis: The Terminal's application name, "VT52" and a 0, given to DC_Nam.

5310.synopsis:
Table of 14 bytes: the control code the Terminal sends for menu commands 3 to 16: DEL, BS,
BEL, HT, LF, FF, CR, SO, SI, DC1, DC3, CAN, SUB and ESC.

5324.synopsis:
Sends a byte to the serial port with OS_SI (SI_PBT) and a 100 ms timeout. On a timeout it
sounds the bell.
Entry: A = the byte.
Exit: Fc = 0 when sent.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code for an error other than RC_Time.
Changes: AF, BC.
Keeps: DE, HL.

5455.synopsis:
The text 1,"3@" and a 0: the Terminal writes it before the column and row of a VT52 ESC Y
cursor move.

5556.synopsis:
Table of the VT52 escape sequences the Terminal turns into screen codes: each record is the
letter after ESC and the 0-terminated text written for it (A up, B down, C right, D left, H
home, I reverse line feed, J erase to the end of the screen, K erase to the end of the line,
L clear); a 0 ends it.

5819.synopsis:
The Calculator's Enter key: presses the highlighted button. Drops the return address that
IndirectJump left, takes the character of button row * 5 + column from Key2Button_tbl and
dispatches it as a typed key (main_5).
Entry: IY = the Calculator's variables (calc_ActiveRow, calc_ActiveCol).

5904.synopsis:
Table of the Calculator's keys, a 0 at the end: the 25 buttons row by row (C, DEL, S, R, +,
7, 8, 9, U, *, 4, 5, 6, Y, -, 1, 2, 3, I, /, 0, ., %, F, =), the convert keys P, T, X, M, D,
\ and E, then the cursor keys ($FF, $FE, $FC, $FD), Enter, Escape and $12. A key's place
gives the button's row and column and its handler in KeyTable.

5944.synopsis:
Table of 39 words: the handler of each key in Key2Button_tbl, in the same order. The main
loop calls it through IndirectJump with the key's number.

6022.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the digit keys (KeyTable). Clears a shown error (ClrError). With no
command pending the digit goes to the number being typed (PutNum); with StoM, RclM or Fix
waiting for its digit, it calls the command's handler in CmdTable (DoStoM, RclM, Fix)
through IndirectJump.
Entry: A = key, '0' to '9'; IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: to PutNum; or to the command's handler with A = digit (0-9); DE = IX = address of the
byte after the command code in calc_CmdBuffer.

6055.synopsis:
Calculator: the StoM command, reached from key_Num through CmdTable. Takes the shown value
(ldFH_F1NumBuf) into FReg1 and Float1, points IX at memory A (GetMemPtrA) and jumps through
StoM_tbl, indexed by the operator stored after StoM (none, +, -, x, /), to store, add,
subtract, multiply or divide the value into that memory. The memory's address is left on the
stack for StoM_plain.
Entry: A = memory number (0-9); DE = address of the operator byte in calc_CmdBuffer (0 for
none, 5-8 for + - x /); IY = calculator workspace.

6092.synopsis:
Calculator: table of 5 words, the StoM handlers: StoM_plain, StoM_add, StoM_sub, StoM_mul
and StoM_div. DoStoM indexes it with 0 for a plain StoM or the operator byte minus 4 (1-4).

6102.synopsis:
Calculator: StoM+. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), adds it to the value (FpAdd)
and goes on to StoM_plain to store the sum in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6110.synopsis:
Calculator: StoM-. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), computes memory - value (FpSub)
and goes on to StoM_plain to store the result in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6118.synopsis:
Calculator: StoMx. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), multiplies it by the value
(FpMul) and goes on to StoM_plain to store the product in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6126.synopsis:
Calculator: StoM/. Loads the memory into FReg2 (RclM_FReg2), computes memory / value (FpDiv)
and falls into StoM_plain to store the quotient in the memory.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value; IX = memory slot; the slot's address on the stack.

6132.synopsis:
Calculator: plain StoM, and the end of every StoM handler. Pops the memory slot's address
into IX, stores FReg1 in it (StoM_FReg1) and falls into ClearCommand.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value to store; the memory slot's address on the stack.

6137.synopsis:
Calculator: ends a command. Resets the command flag (CF_B_Command) and empties the command
buffer (calc_CmdBuffer).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: F, DE, HL.
Keeps: A, BC.

6151.synopsis:
Calculator: the RclM command, reached from key_Num through CmdTable. Drops the number being
typed, loads memory A into FReg1 and Float1 (the shown value) and goes to ClearCommand.
Entry: A = memory number (0-9); IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Float1 = memory A.

6166.synopsis:
Calculator: the Fix command, reached from key_Num through CmdTable. Stores 2 * A + 1 in
varFix (bit 0 marks a Fix as set; the display code, sub_FEBC, takes A back as the number of
decimals, 9 selecting a different FP_STR format) and goes to ClearCommand.
Entry: A = digit (0-9); IY = calculator workspace.

6173.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the '.' and 'E' keys (KeyTable). Ignores the key when the number
being typed already holds that character; otherwise falls into PutNum, which also starts a
new number with it.
Entry: A = '.' or 'E'; IY = calculator workspace.

6194.synopsis:
Calculator: adds a character to the number being typed (calc_NumBuffer, at most 17
characters). Ignored while a command is pending. Starts an empty buffer when no number is
being typed (sets CF_B_HasNumBuf), and a new character other than '.' replaces a leading '0'
that is not followed by '.'. A full buffer drops the character (NumBufferFull).
Entry: A = character; IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: calc_BufferPos advanced; buffer zero-terminated.
Changes: F, C, DE, HL.

6270.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the Clear key (KeyTable). Cancels a pending command (ClearCommand),
clears the number-entry, operator, error, constant and CF_B_3 flags, and falls into ZeroNums
to zero X and Y (Float1 and Float2).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: AF, B, DE, HL.

6311.synopsis:
Fills B bytes from HL with zero. Reached from ZeroNums, from key_DiamR (falls in, clearing
the memories and varFix) and from the start-up code (the workspace).
Entry: HL = start; B = byte count (1-256).
Exit: HL = byte after the block; A = 0; B = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

6317.synopsis:
Calculator: clears a shown error. When CF_B_Error is set, it resets it and the number-entry
and operator flags (CF_B_HasNumBuf, CF_B_Symbol).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: F.

6335.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the RclM key (KeyTable). A = CC_RCLM and on to PutCmd, which starts
the command; the memory number comes with the next digit (key_Num).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

6339.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the Fix key (KeyTable). A = CC_FIX and on to PutCmd, which starts the
command; the number of decimals comes with the next digit (key_Num).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

6343.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the StoM key (KeyTable). A = CC_STOM and falls into PutCmd, which
starts the command (ignored while an error is shown or a command is pending); an operator
and the memory number follow (loc_F9AB, key_Num).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

6359.synopsis:
Calculator: appends a byte to the zero-terminated command buffer (calc_CmdBuffer): a command
code (CC_xxx, 4 for Unit) or an operator byte (5-8 for + - x /) after StoM.
Entry: A = byte; IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: F, C, DE, HL.

6378.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the Unit key (KeyTable): the unit conversions. Ignored while an error
is shown or a command is pending.
1. Stores Unit (4) in the command buffer, shows it (sub_FBA0), sets CF_B_Convert, redraws
the calculator button and selects window 4, the convert window.
2. UnitLoop: redraws the convert buttons (UpdConvButton), reads a key (ReadKey, ToUpper),
looks it up in UnitKey_tbl, ignoring keys not there, and calls its handler from UnitCmd_tbl
with A = key; it loops while the handler returns Fc = 0.
3. Clears CF_B_Convert, redraws the convert button, selects window 5 again, redraws the
calculator button and ends with ClearCommand.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

6470.synopsis:
Calculator: the keys of the unit conversion, 20 bytes and a zero terminator: 'C', DEL ($7F),
Left ($FC), Right ($FD), Up ($FF), Down ($FE), '=', Enter ($0D), Esc ($1B), '0' to '9' and
'.'. key_Unit's loop uses the index of the key found to pick its handler in UnitCmd_tbl.

6491.synopsis:
Calculator: table of 20 words, the unit conversion's key handlers in UnitKey_tbl's order:
ckey_Clr, ckey_Del, ckey_Left, ckey_Right, ckey_Up, ckey_Down, ckey_EquEnter twice ('=' and
Enter), ckey_Esc, ckey_Num ten times and ckey_Dot. A handler returning Fc = 1 ends the
conversion.

6531.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: a digit key. Adds it to the number being typed (PutNum) and
goes on to ckey_numdot to show it.
Entry: A = '0' to '9'; IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0 when OS_Pout succeeds, so the conversion goes on.

6536.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the '.' key. Adds it to the number being typed (key_DotE), then
ckey_numdot selects window 5, redraws the value (PrintStatusRow), selects window 4 again and
returns.
Entry: A = '.'; IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0 when OS_Pout succeeds, so the conversion goes on.

6557.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the Clear key. Clears the calculator (key_Clr) and falls into
ckey_Del, which ends the conversion.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Fc = 1.

6560.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the DEL key, and the end of ckey_Clr. Ends the conversion
without converting.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1.
Changes: F.

6562.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the Up key. Moves the highlight up a row (cDecRow); from the
top row it wraps to the bottom row and falls into cDecCol to step back a column as well.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6566.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active convert column left, from column 0 wrapping to column 1. Also
the end of ckey_Up.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: A = old column; Fz = 1 when it wrapped; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6582.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the Left key. Moves the highlight a column left (cDecCol); from
column 0 it wraps to column 1 and falls into cDecRow to step up a row as well.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6586.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active convert row up, from row 0 wrapping to row 6. Also the end of
ckey_Left.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: A = old row; Fz = 1 when it wrapped; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6602.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the Right key. Moves the highlight a column right (cIncCol);
from column 1 it wraps to column 0 and falls into cIncRow to step down a row as well.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6606.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active convert row down, from row 6 wrapping to row 0. Also the end of
ckey_Right.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: A = new row; Fz = 1 when it wrapped; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6624.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the Down key. Moves the highlight down a row (cIncRow); from
row 6 it wraps to row 0 and falls into cIncCol to step right a column as well.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6628.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active convert column right, from column 1 wrapping to column 0. Also
the end of ckey_Down.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: A = new column; Fz = 1 when it wrapped; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

6646.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the '=' and Enter keys. Converts the shown value with the
active conversion and ends the conversion. Takes the value into Float1 (ldFH_F1NumBuf),
loads the active row's factor from ConvNumTable (GetNumC, FpVal) into FReg1 and jumps
through ConvertCmd_tbl, indexed by the row, with A = the active column (0 converts into the
left unit, 1 into the right one). The handler leaves the result in Float1.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Float1 = converted value; Fc = 1.

6675.synopsis:
Calculator: table of 7 words, the conversion of each convert row: loc_F71D (multiply by the
factor) for Gallons/Litres, Miles/km, Acres/Hectares, lb/kg and oz/g, loc_F72C for
MPG/l/100km and loc_F73A for DegF/DegC. ckey_EquEnter indexes it with the active row.

6689.synopsis:
Calculator: converts by a factor. Inverts the factor for column 1 (sub_F76F), multiplies the
value by it and falls into loc_F727, which stores the result in Float1 and sets Fc. Column 0
converts into the left unit (litres to gallons), column 1 into the right one.
Entry: A = active column; FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = factor; Float1 = value.
Exit: Float1 = result; Fc = 1.

6704.synopsis:
Calculator: converts between MPG and l/100km, the same in both directions: result = factor /
value, with factor 282.4691303. Ends at loc_F727, which stores the result in Float1 and sets
Fc.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = factor; Float1 = value.
Exit: Float1 = result; Fc = 1.

6718.synopsis:
Calculator: converts between degrees Fahrenheit and Celsius with the factor 1.8. Column 0
computes value * 1.8 + 32 (Celsius to Fahrenheit), column 1 (value - 32) / 1.8 (Fahrenheit
to Celsius). Ends at loc_F727, which stores the result in Float1 and sets Fc.
Entry: A = active column; FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = factor 1.8; Float1 = value.
Exit: Float1 = result; Fc = 1.

6769.synopsis:
Calculator, unit conversion: the Esc key. Ends the conversion without converting.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 1.
Changes: F.

6771.synopsis:
Calculator: replaces FReg1 with its reciprocal (OnePerFloat), unless it is zero (FpTst).
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = number.
Exit: FReg1 = 1 / number, or 0 unchanged.

6791.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the convert window's highlight. Redraws the previously active convert
button and the active one (PrintConvButton), and records the active one as the previous.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: C = active column; B = active row.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

6816.synopsis:
Calculator: draws one button of the convert window, at column 12 * C + 1 of line B + 1, in
small type: the 8-character unit name from CvtStrings_tbl (row B, column C), reversed when
the conversion is active (CF_B_Convert) and it is the active button. At column 10 of the
line it then writes "<-" (active column 0) or "->" (column 1) when B is the active row, else
two spaces.
Entry: B = row (0-6); C = column (0-1); IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.
Keeps: BC.

7037.synopsis:
Calculator: table of 7 zero-terminated decimal strings, one conversion factor per convert
row, read by GetNumC and FP_VAL. This first one is row 0's, ".219978442": gallons per litre.

7048.synopsis:
Calculator: conversion factor of row 1 (Miles/km), ".621371192" and a zero: miles per
kilometre. Part of ConvNumTable.

7059.synopsis:
Calculator: conversion constant of row 2 (MPG/l/100km), "282.4691303" and a zero: l/100km =
constant / MPG, and the other way round (loc_F72C). Part of ConvNumTable.

7071.synopsis:
Calculator: conversion factor of row 3 (Acres/Hectares), "2.47104395" and a zero: acres per
hectare. Part of ConvNumTable.

7082.synopsis:
Calculator: conversion factor of row 4 (lb/kg), "2.204622345" and a zero: pounds per
kilogram. Part of ConvNumTable.

7094.synopsis:
Calculator: conversion factor of row 5 (oz/g), ".03527399" and a zero: ounces per gram. Part
of ConvNumTable.

7104.synopsis:
Calculator: conversion factor of row 6 (DegF/DegC), "1.8" and a zero: Fahrenheit degrees per
Celsius degree; loc_F73A adds or removes the offset 32. The last of ConvNumTable.

7108.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the DEL key (KeyTable). Clears a shown error (ClrError), then cancels
a pending command (ClearCommand); or removes the last character of the number being typed,
ending number entry when the buffer becomes empty; or, with no number typed, sets X (Float1)
to zero.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7163.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the % key (KeyTable). Ignored while a command is pending or when no
operator is pending (CF_B_Symbol). Takes the shown value x into FReg1 and Float1, loads the
first operand y (Float2) into FReg2 and jumps through PercCmd_tbl, indexed by the pending
operation (calc_Operation).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7193.synopsis:
Calculator: table of 4 words, the % handlers by pending operation: PercAdd, PercSub, PercMul
and PercDiv (OP_ADD to OP_DIV). key_Perc jumps through it.

7201.synopsis:
Calculator: y + x %. Computes y / (1 - x / 100), then ends at loc_F963: the result goes to
Float1, the operator and the constant mode are cleared and Float2 is zeroed.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = x; FReg2 (DE, DE', B) = y.

7219.synopsis:
Calculator: y - x %. Computes 100 * (y - x) / x, the change from x to y in per cent, then
ends at loc_F963: the result goes to Float1, the operator and the constant mode are cleared
and Float2 is zeroed.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = x; Float1 = x; FReg2 (DE, DE', B) = y.

7239.synopsis:
Calculator: y x x %. Computes x * y / 100 into Float1 and sets CF_B_3, keeping the operator
and Float2: a following + or - then adds it to or takes it from y at once (loc_FA07 through
sub_FA1A); x and / clear CF_B_3.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = x; FReg2 (DE, DE', B) = y.

7258.synopsis:
Calculator: y / x %. Computes 100 * y / x, then falls into loc_F963: the result goes to
Float1, the operator and the constant mode are cleared and Float2 is zeroed.
Entry: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = x; FReg2 (DE, DE', B) = y.

7285.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the P key (KeyTable). Makes the + button (row 0, column 4) the active
one and falls into key_Add.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7293.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the + key (KeyTable). C = OP_ADD and on to the operator code
(loc_F9AB): after StoM it adds the operator to the command; after PercMul (CF_B_3) it
applies it to the first operand at once; otherwise it finishes a pending operation
(sub_FA1A), makes the shown value the first operand (Float2) and records the operator. The
same operator twice toggles the constant mode (CF_B_Constant).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7297.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the M key (KeyTable). Makes the - button (row 2, column 4) the active
one and falls into key_Sub.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7305.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the - key (KeyTable). C = OP_SUB and on to the operator code
(loc_F9AB), as key_Add.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7309.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the T and X keys (KeyTable). Makes the x button (row 1, column 4) the
active one and falls into key_Mul.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7317.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the * key (KeyTable). Clears CF_B_3, then C = OP_MUL and on to the
operator code (loc_F9AB), as key_Add.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7325.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the D and \ keys (KeyTable). Makes the / button (row 3, column 4) the
active one and falls into key_Div.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7333.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the / key (KeyTable). Clears CF_B_3, then C = OP_DIV and falls into
the operator code (loc_F9AB), as key_Add.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7436.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the = key (KeyTable). Clears CF_B_3; ignored while a command is
pending or when no operator is pending (CF_B_Symbol); otherwise falls into sub_FA1A to
compute the result.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7450.synopsis:
Calculator: carries out the pending operation. Computes y op x, y being the first operand
(Float2), x the shown value (the number being typed or Float1) and op the pending operation
(calc_Operation, through OpCmd_tbl: FpAdd, FpSub, FpMul, FpDiv), and stores the result in
Float1. Clears CF_B_3. Unless the constant mode is on, also clears the operator
(CF_B_Symbol) and zeroes Float2; in constant mode y and the operator stay for the next =.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: Float1 = result; FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = result, or 0 when Float2 was zeroed.

7497.synopsis:
Calculator: handler of the Y key, Y<>x (KeyTable). Ignored while a command is pending. Takes
the shown value into Float1 and swaps Float1 and Float2 (X and Y).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.

7520.synopsis:
Calculator: loads the shown value into FReg1: Float1, or, when a number is being typed
(CF_B_HasNumBuf), the value of calc_NumBuffer (FP_VAL), ending the number entry. Float1
itself is not written.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: FReg1 (HL, HL', C) = value.

7687.synopsis:
Calculator: tests whether the number being typed still has room. Measures the text in
calc_NumBuffer, from its start to the end pointer calc_BufferPos/calc_BufferPosH.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace; A = any (kept).
Exit: Fc = 1 when the text is shorter than 17 characters (room for one more); Fc = 0 when it
is full; HL = end pointer of the text; DE = start of calc_NumBuffer.
Changes: F, C, DE, HL.
Keeps: A, B.

7716.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active button one row up, wrapping from the top row to the bottom row
(4). key_Left falls into it after DecCol has wrapped, so moving left past the first column
goes to the row above.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: calc_ActiveRow updated; Fz = 1 when it wrapped to row 4, Fz = 0 otherwise; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

7736.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active button one column left, wrapping from the first column to the
last (4). key_Up falls into it after DecRow has wrapped.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: calc_ActiveCol updated; Fz = 1 when it wrapped to column 4, Fz = 0 otherwise; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

7756.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active button one row down, wrapping from the bottom row (4) to the
top. key_Right falls into it after IncCol has wrapped.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: calc_ActiveRow updated; Fc = 1 when it moved down, Fc = 0 when it wrapped to row 0.
Changes: AF.

7776.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the active button one column right, wrapping from the last column (4) to
the first. key_Down falls into it after IncRow has wrapped.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: calc_ActiveCol updated; Fc = 1 when it moved right, Fc = 0 when it wrapped to column
0.
Changes: AF.

7799.synopsis:
Calculator: leaves the popdown with OS_Bye (A = 0). key_Esc falls into it when no command is
pending; ReadKey and ErrorHandler jump here on RC_Quit. A loop on itself follows the call.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

7804.synopsis:
Calculator: points IX at memory A, one of the ten 5-byte floating-point memories in the
Memories array.
Entry: A = memory number (0-9).
Exit: IX = Memories + 5 * A; A = 5 * A.
Changes: AF, IX.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

7820.synopsis:
Calculator: jumps to entry C of a table of handler addresses. The caller executes EXX, loads
C (and IX) in the other register set and calls this; the routine switches back with EXX, so
the handler starts with the caller's original registers, except that IX takes the value of
DE. The handler returns to the instruction after the call.
Entry: IX = table of words; C = index (in the set active at the call); DE (other set) =
value for IX.
Exit: at the handler, with IX = DE; return address of the caller on the stack.
Changes: BC and IX of the set active at the call; IX.

7840.synopsis:
Calculator: prints the command line at column 2, row 2: the names of the commands queued in
calc_CmdBuffer (each from GetCmdNameA, followed by a space) and a "?", in tiny type, when
command mode is on. Then pads with spaces over what the previous line left and records the
new length in calc_StatusLineLen.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: calc_StatusLineLen = length of the line printed.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

7913.synopsis:
Calculator: finds the name of a command in the list at aStom by skipping A zero-terminated
names.
Entry: A = command number (0 = StoM, 1 = RclM, 2 = Fix, 3 = Unit, 4-7 = + - * /).
Exit: DE = the command's name.
Changes: AF, DE.
Keeps: BC, HL.

7931.synopsis:
Calculator: table of 3 words, the handlers of the commands that wait for a digit: DoStoM,
RclM and Fix, in the order CC_STOM, CC_RCLM, CC_FIX (index = command - 1). key_Num jumps
through it with IndirectJump when a digit completes a command.

7937.synopsis:
Calculator: the command names, each zero-terminated: StoM, RclM, Fix, Unit, +, -, *, /.
GetCmdNameA finds one by number; sub_FBA0 prints those of the pending command.

7964.synopsis:
Calculator: prints the status row. At column 8, row 1, shows right-justified in 17 columns
the text "Error" when the error flag is set, otherwise the number being typed
(calc_NumBuffer) or, when there is none, Float1 formatted by sub_FEBC. At column 28 it then
prints the symbol of the pending operation from Symbol_tbl (or a space), a space, and a tiny
"K" when the constant flag is set (otherwise a space).
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL; the FPP registers when Float1 is formatted.

8088.synopsis:
Calculator: four characters "+-x/", the symbol of each operation (calc_Operation: OP_ADD,
OP_SUB, OP_MUL, OP_DIV), printed by PrintStatusRow.

8092.synopsis:
Calculator: the text "Error",0, copied (6 bytes) into calc_StrBuffer by PrintStatusRow when
the error flag is set.

8098.synopsis:
Calculator: draws the calculator window's frame: the centred tiny title "CALCULATOR" on a
reverse, underlined bar 33 characters wide, then a vertical bar (PrntVBar) at columns 6 and
26 of row 1, either side of the number display.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, B.

8164.synopsis:
Calculator: prints the screen-driver sequence 1,$7C, the vertical bar between buttons and
around the display.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

8170.synopsis:
Calculator: redraws the previously active button as a plain button and the active one
highlighted (PrintCalcButton), then records the active column and row as the previous ones.
Entry: IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: C = calc_ActiveCol; B = calc_ActiveRow; calc_PrevActCol/calc_PrecActRow set to them.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

8195.synopsis:
Calculator: draws one keypad button at column 6 * C + 2, row B + 3: its five characters from
ButtonTxt_tbl (entry 5 * B + C), in tiny type except in the last column, in reverse when it
is the active button (not while the Convert window is active), underlined except on the
bottom row, followed by a vertical bar except in the last column.
Entry: C = column (0-4); B = row (0-4); IY = calculator workspace.
Changes: AF, HL.
Keeps: BC.

8301.synopsis:
Calculator: prints the sequence 1,"2+U", which sets underline on.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

8309.synopsis:
Calculator: prints the sequence 1,"U", which toggles underline.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

8315.synopsis:
Calculator: prints the sequence 1,"T", which toggles tiny type.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

8321.synopsis:
Calculator: the texts of the 25 keypad buttons, five characters each, row by row: "Clear", "
DEL ", "StoM ", "RclM ", " + "; 7, 8, 9, Unit, x; 4, 5, 6, Y<>x, -; 1, 2, 3, sIgn, /; 0, .,
%, Fix, =. PrintCalcButton prints entry 5 * row + column.

8446.synopsis:
Calculator: loads Float1 into FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL', HL, C = Float1; A = its exponent.
Changes: A, C, HL, HL'.

8459.synopsis:
Calculator: loads Float1 into FPP register 2 (DE' low word, DE high word, B exponent).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE', DE, B = Float1; A = its exponent.
Changes: A, B, DE, DE'.

8474.synopsis:
Calculator: loads Float2 into FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent).
Entry: none.
Exit: HL', HL, C = Float2; A = its exponent.
Changes: A, C, HL, HL'.

8487.synopsis:
Calculator: loads Float2 into FPP register 2 (DE' low word, DE high word, B exponent).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE', DE, B = Float2; A = its exponent.
Changes: A, B, DE, DE'.

8502.synopsis:
Calculator: stores FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent) in Float1.
Entry: HL', HL, C = number.
Exit: Float1 = the number; A = C.
Changes: A.

8515.synopsis:
Calculator: stores FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent) in Float2.
Entry: HL', HL, C = number.
Exit: Float2 = the number; A = C.
Changes: A.

8543.synopsis:
Calculator: loads the 5-byte number at IX (a memory, from GetMemPtrA) into FPP register 1
(HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent).
Entry: IX = number.
Exit: HL', HL, C = number.
Changes: C, HL, HL'.

8561.synopsis:
Calculator: stores FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent) in the 5 bytes at
IX (a memory, from GetMemPtrA).
Entry: IX = destination; HL', HL, C = number.
Exit: (IX) to (IX+4) = the number.
Changes: none.

8579.synopsis:
Calculator: loads the 5-byte number at IX (a memory, from GetMemPtrA) into FPP register 2
(DE' low word, DE high word, B exponent).
Entry: IX = number.
Exit: DE', DE, B = number.
Changes: B, DE, DE'.

8597.synopsis:
Calculator: sets FPP register 1 to zero with FP_ZER.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL', HL, C = 0.

8600.synopsis:
Calculator: loads the integer 32 into FPP register 2 (exponent byte B = 0 marks an integer),
for the Celsius and Fahrenheit conversion (loc_F73A).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE' = 32; DE = 0; B = 0.
Changes: B, DE, DE'.

8611.synopsis:
Calculator: loads the integer 100 into FPP register 2 (exponent byte B = 0 marks an
integer), for the percentage operations (PercAdd to PercDiv).
Entry: none.
Exit: DE' = 100; DE = 0; B = 0.
Changes: B, DE, DE'.

8622.synopsis:
Calculator: converts the text at HL to a number with FP_VAL.
Entry: HL = text.
Exit: HL', HL, C = the number.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP.

8625.synopsis:
Calculator: formats FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent) as text into
calc_StrBuffer with FP_STR (entry FpStr). The format goes in D' and E': D' = 2, E' = 2 when
no Fix is set (varFix = 0); after Fix n, E' = n, and D' = 0 when n is 9.
Entry: HL', HL, C = number; IY = calculator workspace.
Exit: the text in calc_StrBuffer.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP.

8657.synopsis:
Calculator: exchanges FPP register 1 (HL' HL C) and FPP register 2 (DE' DE B).
Entry: HL', HL, C and DE', DE, B = the two numbers.
Exit: the two numbers swapped; A = the old B.
Changes: A, BC, DE, HL, DE', HL'.

8665.synopsis:
Calculator: tests FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent) with FP_TST.
Entry: HL', HL, C = number.
Exit: Fz = 1 when it is zero; Fc = 1 when it is negative (A = $80 when it is not zero).
Changes: AF.

8669.synopsis:
Calculator: sets FPP register 1 to one with FP_ONE.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL', HL, C = 1.

8672.synopsis:
Calculator: adds the FPP registers with FP_ADD: register 1 = register 1 + register 2.
Entry: HL', HL, C and DE', DE, B = the operands.
Exit: HL', HL, C = the sum.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP.

8675.synopsis:
Calculator: negates FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent): swaps it into
register 2, sets register 1 to zero and falls into FpSub, which gives 0 - number.
Entry: HL', HL, C = number.
Exit: HL', HL, C = minus the number.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP.

8684.synopsis:
Calculator: subtracts with FP_SUB after exchanging the registers, so register 1 = register 2
- register 1 (the earlier operand or the memory minus the new value).
Entry: HL', HL, C = subtrahend; DE', DE, B = minuend.
Exit: HL', HL, C = the difference.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP.

8690.synopsis:
Calculator: multiplies the FPP registers with FP_MUL: register 1 = register 1 * register 2.
Entry: HL', HL, C and DE', DE, B = the operands.
Exit: HL', HL, C = the product.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP.

8693.synopsis:
Calculator: replaces FPP register 1 (HL' low word, HL high word, C exponent) by its
reciprocal: puts the number in register 2 and 1 in register 1, and falls into FpDiv, which
gives 1 / number.
Entry: HL', HL, C = number.
Exit: HL', HL, C = 1 / number.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP (RC_Dvz for zero).

8702.synopsis:
Calculator: divides with FP_DIV after exchanging the registers, so register 1 = register 2 /
register 1.
Entry: HL', HL, C = divisor; DE', DE, B = dividend.
Exit: HL', HL, C = the quotient.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from the FPP.

8708.synopsis:
Calculator: moves the cursor to column A, row B of the current window by printing
1,"3@",A+$20,B+$20.
Entry: A = column; B = row.
Exit: A = column + $20.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

8734.synopsis:
Calculator: purges the keyboard buffer (OS_Pur) and waits for a key with OS_In. An extended
key (0 followed by a code) returns the second code. RC_Quit leaves through Exit_calc; Escape
is acknowledged (OS_Esc, SC_ACK) and returned as $1B; any other error is ignored and the
read repeats.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = key, Fc = 0; or A = $1B, Fc = 1 after Escape.
Changes: AF.

8785.synopsis:
Calculator: converts a letter to upper case; other characters pass unchanged.
Entry: A = character.
