Exit: A = the character, upper case when it is a letter; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

8792.synopsis:
Calculator: tests whether A is a decimal digit.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: Fc = 1 when A is "0" to "9".
Changes: F.

8803.synopsis:
Calculator: tests whether A is a letter. The unused IsAlphaNum, before it, falls into it.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: Fc = 1 when A is "A" to "Z" or "a" to "z".
Changes: F.

8817.synopsis:
Calculator: prints character 12, which clears the current window.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.

8821.synopsis:
Calculator: prints character 7 (the bell).
Entry: none.
Exit: A = 7; Fc = 1.
Changes: F.

8827.synopsis:
Calculator: prints the sequence 1,"R", which toggles reverse video.
Entry: none.
Changes: none (AF is kept).

8857.synopsis:
Calculator: prints A spaces with the repeat sequence 1,"3N",A+$20," " (the space is
PrntSpace's, which it falls into). Prints nothing when A is 0.
Entry: A = count.
Exit: A = " " (A = 0 when nothing was printed).
Changes: AF.

8871.synopsis:
Calculator: prints one space.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = " ".
Changes: AF.

9216.synopsis:
Imp/Export: the popdown's entry point (IXP_ENT): jumps to app_main. The SCF and RET after
the jump are not reached from it.
Entry: IX = information block from the Index.

9221.synopsis:
Imp/Export: starts the popdown and runs its command loop. Never returns.
1. Checks that the Index gave it 5 pages of contiguous RAM ((IX+2) = $20 + IXP_BAD), else
leaves with OS_Bye (A = 7). Checks the OZ version (OS_Nq, NQ_Voz), else leaves with OS_Bye
(A = 0).
2. Sets IY = WorkSpace, enables Escape detection and installs ErrHandler (OS_Erh), then
draws the window (InitWd).
3. Loads the XY-modem settings, acknowledges Escape and asks for X, Y, B, E, R or S, reading
one character with GN_Sip (MayQuit, MayExit and Backspace_C handle its errors).
4. Finds the character in CmdChars_tbl and calls the matching CmdFuncs_tbl entry; a bad one
prints "Bad response". A command returning Fc = 1 redraws the window; then the loop repeats.
Entry: IX = information block from the Index.
Exit: does not return (OS_Bye).

9418.synopsis:
Imp/Export: table of 6 words, the command handlers in the reverse order of CmdChars_tbl:
Cmd_Xmodem, Cmd_Ymodem, Cmd_BatchRcv, Cmd_EndBatch, Cmd_Receive, cmd_Send. app_main indexes
it with the count CPIR leaves in BC.

9430.synopsis:
Imp/Export: the six command keys "SREBYX" (Send, Receive, End batch, Batch receive, Ymodem,
Xmodem), searched with CPIR by app_main.

9436.synopsis:
Imp/Export: X command: clears the ymodem bit of state_prg and jumps to xymodem_init for an
XMODEM transfer.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.

9443.synopsis:
Imp/Export: Y command: sets the ymodem bit of state_prg and jumps to xymodem_init for a
YMODEM transfer.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.

9450.synopsis:
Imp/Export: after a failed GN_Sip, leaves the popdown (Exit_impexp) when the error is
RC_Esc.
Entry: A = error code.
Exit: Fc = 1 (any other error).
Changes: F.

9456.synopsis:
Imp/Export: after a failed GN_Sip, falls into Exit_impexp when the error is RC_Quit.
Entry: A = error code.
Exit: Fc = 1, Fz = 0 (any other error).
Changes: F.

9460.synopsis:
Imp/Export: leaves the popdown with OS_Bye (A = 0), repeating the call if it returns.
MayQuit falls into it; MayExit and ErrHandler jump to it.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

9465.synopsis:
Imp/Export: the error handler installed with OS_Erh. Returns at once for a fatal error (Fz =
1); leaves the popdown (Exit_impexp) on RC_Quit; returns any other error to the failing call
with Fz = 1, Fc = 0.
Entry: A = error code; Fz = 1 when the error is fatal.
Changes: F.

9477.synopsis:
Imp/Export: B command, batch receive: receives files with Receive one after another,
starting a new line after each that ends with end of file, until a transfer ends any other
way (end of batch, an error or Escape). Its opening CALL C, PrntError does nothing from the
dispatcher, which enters with Fc = 0.
Entry: Fc = 0; IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = status code of the last transfer.

9492.synopsis:
Imp/Export: E command, end batch: sends ESC "Z" through the serial port (MaySendB_EscA) and
prints the error when that fails (Escape or a serial port error).
Entry: Fc = 0; IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: Fc = 0.

9515.synopsis:
Imp/Export: S command, send: asks for a file name and sends the file, or every file a
wildcard matches, through the serial port.
1. Asks for the name (AskFilename), again while it is empty, and expands it (GN_Fex). A
wildcard opens a handle (GN_Opw); each file match (GN_Wfn) is printed and sent.
2. Opens the file (GN_Opf), sends ESC "N", the name and ESC "F", then the file block by
block (loadbuffer, sendbuffer) and ESC "E". Bytes outside the printable characters, CR, LF
and TAB go as ESC "B" and two hex digits (SendChar).
3. Closes the file and takes the next wildcard match; when there is none it reports "All
sent". SndRcv_End closes the handles and prints any error.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: Fc = 1 when the name could not be read (an error other than Escape), which makes
app_main redraw the window; otherwise Fc = 0.

9675.synopsis:
Imp/Export: sends BC bytes from the buffer at HL through the serial port with SendChar,
printing the line number in DE at every CR or LF (PrntLineNum). On a failure it ends the
transfer with SndRcv_End (closing the file and printing the error).
Entry: HL = buffer; BC = byte count (not 0); DE = line number.
Exit: Fc = 0; HL = past the buffer; BC = 0; DE = next line number.
Error: Fc = 1, after SndRcv_End.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

9728.synopsis:
Sends the byte in A over the serial port in Imp/Export's encoding: a printable character
($20-$7E), CR, TAB or LF goes out as it is (MaySendB); any other byte goes out as ESC 'B'
followed by its two hex digits, upper case (ItoH, sent by calling itself).
Entry: A = byte to send.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = ERR_Esc (5) if Escape is pending, ERR_System (0) if OS_Si fails.
Changes: AF, BC.

9786.synopsis:
Converts the value 0-15 in A to its ASCII hex digit, '0'-'9' or 'A'-'F'.
Entry: A = value, 0 to 15.
Exit: A = hex digit.
Changes: AF.

9794.synopsis:
The R)eceive command: asks for a local file name with AskFname_impexp and returns if that
fails or is escaped; otherwise falls into Receive (an empty name means the remote name is
used).
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: as Receive.

9804.synopsis:
Receives one file in Imp/Export's own protocol over the serial port and ends through
SndRcv_End. The sender's stream is plain text with escape sequences: ESC 'N' name ESC 'F'
gives the remote name, ESC 'B' hh a binary byte, ESC 'E' the end of the file and ESC 'Z' the
end of the batch.
1. Clears FileHandle, WildHandle and RemoteName; tests Escape before every byte (RcvB).
2. An ESC goes to RcvFilename: a name sets RemoteName, a hex byte is stored as data, end of
file or batch leaves the loop.
3. Data before any name (local or remote) is ignored. The first data byte creates the file
with GN_Opf (OP_Out) under the local name if one was given, else the remote one (GetName),
and prints "Using supplied name:" or "Using remote name:" with the name.
4. Each byte shows the line number on CR/LF (PrntLineNum) and is written through the buffer
(byte2file); at end of file or batch the buffer is flushed (flushbuffer).
Entry: IY = WorkSpace; LocalName = local file name or empty.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = MSG_Eof (4) after a file, MSG_Eob (3) at the end of a batch, or the error
number that SndRcv_End has printed (ERR_Esc, ERR_Data, 0 for an OZ error).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

9979.synopsis:
Ends a send or a receive: closes the file (CloseFile), prints the message for A when Fc = 1
(PrntError), and closes the wildcard handler in WildHandle with GN_Wcl if there is one. If
the close fails and no error was pending, the OZ error is printed instead (A = 0).
Entry: A = message number (ERR_xxx or MSG_xxx; 0 = the last OZ error); Fc = 1 to print it.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = message number; Fz = 1 if it is 0.
Changes: AF, HL, IX; BC and DE when a message is printed.

10015.synopsis:
Returns the name to create a received file under: LocalName if the user gave one, else
RemoteName.
Exit: HL = LocalName, Fz = 0; or HL = RemoteName, Fz = 1 if LocalName is empty.
Changes: AF, HL.

10025.synopsis:
Handles an escape sequence of Receive, after its ESC: reads the command letter (upper cased)
and acts on it. 'N' reads the remote name (at most 50 characters, up to the next ESC) into
RemoteName, null-terminated, and expects 'F' after it; 'F' ends a name; 'B' reads two hex
digits (GetHexB); 'E' and 'Z' end the file and the batch.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: Fc = 0. After a name or 'F': F = P/V only (Fpe, ignore). After 'B': A = byte, F = 0
(Fpo, store A).
Error: Fc = 1, A = MSG_Eof (4) on 'E', MSG_Eob (3) on 'Z', ERR_Data (2) on a bad letter, a
bad hex digit or a name that is too long, ERR_System (0) if a byte does not arrive.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

10150.synopsis:
Closes the file in FileHandle with GN_Cl if one is open, and clears FileHandle.
Entry: FileHandle = file handle or 0.
Exit: A = 0; Fc = 0 (Fz = 1 if no file was open).
Error: Fc = 1 if GN_Cl fails (A = 0, so PrntError shows the OZ error).
Changes: AF; HL and IX when a file was open.

10209.synopsis:
Gets a byte from the serial port with OS_Si (SI_Gbt), timeout BC = 60000 (the source says 60
s), and clears its bit 7: data is 7-bit, binary bytes come as ESC 'B' hh.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = byte, $00-$7F.
Error: Fc = 1, A = ERR_System (0).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

10230.synopsis:
Sends ESC (27) and then the byte in A over the serial port, each through MaySendB.
Entry: A = byte to send after ESC.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = ERR_Esc (5) if Escape is pending, ERR_System (0) if OS_Si fails.
Changes: AF, BC.

10239.synopsis:
Sends the byte in A over the serial port with OS_Si (SI_Pbt, timeout BC = 60000) unless
Escape is pending (TestEsc).
Entry: A = byte to send.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = ERR_Esc (5) if Escape is pending, ERR_System (0) if OS_Si fails.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

10262.synopsis:
Tests for a pending Escape condition with OS_Esc (SC_BIT).
Exit: Fc = 1 if Escape is pending, else Fc = 0.
Changes: F.
Keeps: A.

10451.synopsis:
Empties the file buffer: next_pos = data_buf0 and databuflen = 0.
Entry: none.
Changes: none (memory only).

10466.synopsis:
Opens Imp/Export's window with OS_Pout: defines window 1 (SOH '7' '#', 92 columns by 8 rows
from the left of the screen), then selects and clears it, turns the cursor on and sends SOH
'S'.
Entry: none.

10489.synopsis:
Prints a message with a bell (PrntBell_impexp), on a new line if the cursor is not in column
0. A = 0 prints the last OZ error (OS_Erc, GN_Esp, read with GN_Rbe); 1 to 7 print
Imp/Export's own message from ErrorTable.
Entry: A = message number (ERR_xxx or MSG_xxx).
Exit: Fc = 1.
Changes: AF, BC, HL; DE for messages 1 to 7.

10544.synopsis:
Table of 7 words: the address of Imp/Export's message for each message number 1 to 7
(Error_1 to Error_7), read by PrntError at number - 1.

10640.synopsis:
Imp/Export's bell: writes BEL (7) with OS_Out.
Entry: none.

10645.synopsis:
Called after GN_Sip was left (suspended): moves the cursor back over the C characters of the
input line with backspaces, and returns A = 1 so that the next GN_Sip edits the text already
in the buffer. The flags are kept.
Entry: C = cursor position on the line (from GN_Sip).
Exit: A = 1; F unchanged.
Changes: A, B.

10663.synopsis:
Imp/Export's upper-case conversion: a letter in A (IsAlpha_impexp) has bit 5 cleared; any
other character is returned as it is.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: A = character, upper case if a letter.
Changes: AF.

10684.synopsis:
Starts the X/Y-modem part of Imp/Export (from the X)modem and Y)modem commands): installs
error_handler with OS_Erh and calls app_main_xymodem. When that returns, falls into kill:
closes the file (file_close), gives the serial port back (hw_close_com) and leaves
Imp/Export with OS_Bye. Does not return.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace; state_prg bit ymodem = protocol chosen.

10735.synopsis:
The X/Y-modem main loop. Clears the window, takes over the UART (hw_open_com), and if the
mailbox "NAME" (OS_Sr SR_RPD) holds a file name, sends that file first (send_file). Then
shows the menu (main_menu): protocol, /Checksum or /CRC, -1K, E)nd batch for Ymodem, and the
commands, and reads a key with OS_In: X or Y selects the protocol, C toggles CRC, K toggles
1K blocks (each saved with save_xymodem_cfg); E sends the end of a batch (send_end_batch); R
receives (Ymodem: receive_ymodem; Xmodem: asks a name with get_filename, then receive_file);
S asks a name, expands it (GN_Fex) and sends every file that matches it (GN_Opw, GN_Wfn,
send_file) until one is escaped. Timer interrupts are off while receiving (di_tick) and back
on at the menu (ei_tick). ESC is ignored; B does nothing.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: returns to xymodem_init on Shift+Enter (key code 209).

11093.synopsis:
Asks for a file name: prints "Filename? " on a new line and reads up to 51 characters into
fname_buf with GN_Sip, then checks it with GN_Prs. A suspended input is read again keeping
its text; any other input error or an invalid name asks again.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: Fc = 0; fname_buf = file name; DE = fname_buf.
Error: Fc = 1 if the input ended with ESC (after a new line).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

11137.synopsis:
Resets the expected file size before a receive, for a sender that gives none: filesize =
$FFFFFFFF, blocks = $7FFF, bytes = 0, and clears date_rx in state_rx.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace.
Changes: DE.

11167.synopsis:
Receives a batch of files with Ymodem; its second half, from receive_file, also receives one
Xmodem file.
1. Takes CRC or checksum mode from state_prg into state_rx, expects block 0 and sends NAK or
'C' (CRC) to start (send_NAKs). Each wait has at most 10 tries (update_retries), with the
input purged before every NAK.
2. A block is SOH (128 bytes) or STX (1024 bytes), the block number and its complement, the
data and a checksum or a CRC-16 (update_crc). A bad block is answered with NAK; a repeat of
the previous block too; any other number ends with Out of sync. CAN CAN cancels; EOT ends
the file.
3. Block 0 is the Ymodem header: an empty name ends the batch. Else the name, the size
(FP_VAL) and the octal modification time (seconds since 1970) are read, the time is turned
into a Z88 date and time with the FPP, and the file is opened (open_file) from block 1.
4. Data blocks are written with OS_Mv, the last one cut to the file size, then ACKed with a
spinner character.
5. At EOT the file is closed; Xmodem returns, Ymodem sets the file's update date and time
(OS_Dor) if the header had one, and goes back for the next file. An error sends CANs
(cancel), prints its message and closes the file (quit_to_main).
Entry: IY = WorkSpace; state_prg = protocol options.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX and the alternate registers.

11831.synopsis:
Drains the serial input: reads bytes with hw_rxbt (A = 1) until none arrives within the
timeout (or a key is pressed).
Exit: Fc = 1.
Changes: AF, AF', BC'.

11839.synopsis:
Cancels a transfer: purges the input (purge) and sends CAN eight times.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 if a byte cannot be sent (hw_txbt).
Changes: AF, B, AF', BC'.

11853.synopsis:
Sets the retry counter: retries = 11 (10 tries, it is decremented before each).
Changes: A.

11859.synopsis:
Adds the byte in A to the CRC-16 in DE (the Xmodem CRC, polynomial $1021, most significant
bit first).
Entry: A = byte; DE = CRC so far.
Exit: DE = new CRC.
Changes: AF, DE, AF'.
Keeps: BC, HL.

11927.synopsis:
Sends the file named in fname_buf with Xmodem or Ymodem.
1. Opens its DOR (GN_Opf, OP_DOR) to get the explicit name; anything but a RAM device
(":RAM") is skipped. Because data_buf0 follows fname_buf, the Ymodem header's name is the
explicit name without its ':'.
2. Adds to the header the size (DOR dt_ext, written with GN_Pdn), a space and the update
time (dt_upd) as 11 octal digits of seconds since 1970, worked out with the FPP; pads with
zeros.
3. Counts the blocks (calc_blocks_and_bytes), picks 1K blocks if chosen and opens the file
(open_file).
4. Ymodem sends the header as block 0 when the receiver asks with NAK, 'C' or 'G', then
waits for that again; Xmodem starts at block 1. NAK selects checksum, 'C' CRC, 'G' Ymodem-G
(no ACK waited for).
5. Each block is read with OS_Mv (the last padded with zeros), sent with SOH or STX, its
number, the complement, the data and the checksum or CRC; NAK resends it, ACK goes on, CAN
CAN cancels; a spinner shows progress (indicate).
6. At end of file EOT is sent up to 10 times until ACKed. An error prints its message and
closes the file (quit_to_main).
Entry: IY = WorkSpace; fname_buf = file name; state_prg = protocol options.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX and the alternate registers.

12750.synopsis:
Ends a Ymodem batch: sends an empty header block, SOH, block 0, $FF and 130 zero bytes (the
data and a zero CRC), then purges the input.
Exit: Fc = 1 (from purge).
Error: Fc = 1 if a byte cannot be sent.
Changes: AF, BC, HL, AF', BC'.

12864.synopsis:
Shows the send spinner: for a block number of 1, 3, 5 or 7 modulo 8 prints '|', '/', '-' or
'\', for an even one a backspace.
Entry: A = block number.
Changes: AF.

12907.synopsis:
Loads the X/Y-modem options into state_prg from ubImpExpSelProtocol: the crc, block1k and
ymodem bits; the other bits are cleared.
Exit: A = state_prg.
Changes: AF.

12920.synopsis:
Keeps the X/Y-modem options in the system variable ubImpExpSelProtocol: the crc, block1k and
ymodem bits of state_prg.
Changes: AF.

12929.synopsis:
Closes the transfer's file with GN_Cl if the file_open bit of state_prg is set, and clears
the bit.
Entry: IY = WorkSpace; IX = the file's handle (left there by open_file).

12942.synopsis:
Opens a file for a transfer with GN_Opf. The explicit name goes to fname_buf, or to
fname_buf1 when a Ymodem header carried a date (date_rx). Sets file_open, prints the
explicit name on a new line followed by cursor_off, and points next_pos after the name.
Entry: A = open mode (OP_In or OP_Out); HL = file name; IY = WorkSpace.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = file handle.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from GN_Opf.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

13008.synopsis:
Disables the RTC (timer) interrupts: clears BB_INTTIME in the BL_INT softcopy and writes it
to the port, so receiving at high speed is not interrupted.
Changes: AF, BC.

13018.synopsis:
Enables the RTC (timer) interrupts again: sets BB_INTTIME in the BL_INT softcopy and writes
it to the port.
Changes: AF, BC.

13051.synopsis:
Receives a byte from the UART directly, with a timeout. Polls BL_UIT 256 times first, then
until the RTC seconds counter (BL_TIM1) reaches the start plus A (get_timeout_sec). A key
pressed stops it (BL_KBD read with B' = the target second, so the row with ESC is always
among the rows read).
Entry: A = timeout, 1 to 59 (the wait is A - 1 to A seconds).
Exit: Fc = 0; A = byte from BL_RXD.
Error: Fc = 1; Fz = 1 on timeout, Fz = 0 if a key was pressed.
Changes: AF, AF', BC'.

13101.synopsis:
Sends a byte through the UART directly: waits for the transmit register to empty (BL_UIT
TDRE) for up to about 31 seconds, then writes it to BL_TXD. A key pressed stops it.
Entry: A = byte to send.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = byte.
Error: Fc = 1, A lost; Fz = 1 on timeout, Fz = 0 if a key was pressed.
Changes: F, AF', BC'; A on error.

13170.synopsis:
Reads the RTC seconds counter (BL_TIM1), reading again until two reads agree.
Exit: A = seconds, 0 to 59.
Changes: AF, C.

The mailbox name "NAME", null-terminated: app_main reads a file name to send from it (OS_Sr

"Xmodem" in bold (SOH 'B' on and off), null-terminated: the protocol shown in the menu and

13196.synopsis:
"Ymodem" in bold (SOH 'B' on and off), null-terminated: the protocol shown in the menu and

13207.synopsis: "/Checksum", null-terminated: shown in the menu when CRC is off.

13217.synopsis: "/CRC", null-terminated: shown in the menu when CRC is on.

13222.synopsis: "-1K", null-terminated: shown after the protocol when 1K blocks are on.

13242.synopsis: ": E)nd batch", null-terminated: the menu's extra command with Ymodem.

13255.synopsis:
": R)eceive file or S)end file? " and SOH "2+C" (cursor on), null-terminated: the end of the
X/Y-modem menu.

13304.synopsis: CR, LF, "Canceled", null-terminated: shown when the other side cancels with CAN CAN.

13315.synopsis: CR, LF, "Timeout", null-terminated: shown when a byte is not sent or received in time.

13325.synopsis: CR, LF, "End of retries", null-terminated: shown when a block fails 10 times.

13342.synopsis:
CR, LF, "Out of sync", null-terminated: shown when a block number is neither the expected
one nor the previous one.

13356.synopsis:
CR, LF, "Bad block number", null-terminated: shown when a repeated block's complement does
not match.

13375.synopsis: CR, LF, "No ack on EOT", null-terminated: shown when EOT is not acknowledged after 10 tries.

13391.synopsis:
A backspace and SOH "2C" $FD, null-terminated: printed after a received file to remove the
progress spinner (the source's comment, "CR & LF & 0", is out of date).

13397.synopsis: CR, LF, "Dor won't open", null-terminated: shown when send_file cannot open the file's DOR.

13414.synopsis: CR, LF, "Could not open file", null-terminated: shown when open_file fails.

13436.synopsis:
CR, LF, "End of batch", null-terminated. Nothing uses it (its use is commented out in the
source).

13451.synopsis: CR, LF, "Escape", null-terminated: shown when a transfer is stopped by a key.

13460.synopsis:
Two spaces and SOH "2-C" (cursor off), null-terminated: printed by open_file after the file
name.

0.synopsis:
The System Token Table: the token base shared by the MTH of most built-in applications and
popdowns, whose application DORs (dorappl in mth/appdors.asm) point at it. Layout: byte 0,
the recursive token boundary ($80); byte 1, the number of tokens ($80, so tokens $80-$FF);
then $81 words, each an offset from SysTokenBase: the start of tokens $80 to $FF in order
and, last, the end of the table (end_tokens). A token's length is the next offset minus its
own; the token texts follow the offsets, from token80 on. OS_Wrt reads it (WriteToken in
os/token.asm): a byte $80-$FF is looked up in the active application's token base (set by
OS_Wtb). With bit 7 of the boundary set, as here, every byte of a token goes back through
OS_Wrt, so tokens nest; with bit 7 clear, only tokens from $80 + boundary upwards do. A $7F
byte in a token prints CR, LF.

to show that word in tiny characters.

1050.synopsis:
Index's MTH commands: the command block that IndexDOR points to, read by the kernel's MTH
code (GetAppCommands, os/mth0.asm) for the menus, the help and the command keys. Topics:
Commands (15 commands, 2 of them hidden: HARD and NQ) and Info (2 entries, "Description" and
"Card insertion", each with a help page). Layout: CMD_MARK (0); one mthcmd record per
command (length, command code, key sequence and 0, tokenised name, help page offset high
byte first when CMDF_HELP is set, CMDF_* attributes, length again); TPC_SEP (1) between
topics; CMD_MARK.

1295.synopsis:

new line, ended by 0. The DOR points to it; the help page offsets of the topics and commands
count from here.

1309.synopsis: Index's help page for the Info topic: empty, a single 0.

1310.synopsis:
Index's help page for the Info entry "Description": what the popdown does: launching,
reviving or killing suspended activities, installing or removing applications, and system
information.

1414.synopsis:
Index's help page for the Info entry "Card insertion": cards are inserted and removed only
from the Index, a ROM card in use stays in, and a FAIL message needs a reset.

1576.synopsis: Index's help page for the Commands topic: empty, a single 0.

1577.synopsis:
Index's help page for the Card Display command (<>CARD): the resources of the inserted
cards, the free space of the selected RAM device and its graphic map of used and free
memory.

1762.synopsis:
Index's help page for the Install Application command (<>INS): enter the name of a .app file
(it can be marked in the Filer); the ap0... files must be in the same directory.

1884.synopsis:
Index's help page for the Remove Application command (<>RMV): the application's suspended
activities must be killed first; an installation of several applications is removed by
selecting the first one.

1995.synopsis:
Index's help page for the Update OZ command (<>UPD): updates OZ in slot 0 or 1 from the
update package files on the RAM device.

2114.synopsis:

kernel's MTH code (GetAppCommands, os/mth0.asm) for the menus, the help and the command
keys. Topics: Info (10 entries, each with a help page: the function groups, operators and
wildcards), Blocks (13), Cursor (22, 2 hidden), Edit (25, 2 hidden), Files (7), Layout (17),
Options (1) and Print (13). Layout: CMD_MARK (0); one mthcmd record per command (length,
command code, key sequence and 0, tokenised name, help page offset high byte first when
CMDF_HELP is set, CMDF_* attributes, length again); TPC_SEP (1) between topics; CMD_MARK.

3461.synopsis:

7726.synopsis:
Index's application DOR, the first in the ROM's chain: the front DOR at $3FC0 (romhdr.asm)
links to it. Built by dorappl (def/macros.def), the layout every application DOR here
shares:
1. Three 3-byte pointers (offset, bank): parent, brother (the next application DOR) and son;
only the brother is set.
2. Type Dm_Rom ($83) and the length of the rest.
3. Dt_Inf ($40) record: 2 reserved bytes, key letter, continuous RAM pages, environment
estimate, unsafe and safe stack workspace (words), entry address (word), the banks bound
into S0-S3 on entry, type (AT_xxx) and type 2 (AT2_xxx).
4. Dt_Hlp ($48) record: 3-byte pointers to the MTH topics, commands, help page and token
base (SysTokenBase); an absent one points at the DOR's own zero parent pointer.
5. Dt_Nam ($4E) record: the name, zero-terminated; then $FF ends the DOR. Index: key 'I',
AT_Good|AT_Popd|AT_Ones (a popdown, one instance), entry IDX_ENT with IDX_BNK in S3; MTH
IndexTopics, IndexCommands, IndexHelp; next DiaryDOR.

Error text "Flash VPP low", zero-terminated. ErrStr_tbl points here for RC_VPL; GN_Esp
returns it in BHL (bank MTH_BNK).

9670.synopsis:
Error text "UV Eprom not fully cleared, erase again", zero-terminated. ErrStr_tbl points
here for RC_EPNE; GN_Esp returns it in BHL (bank MTH_BNK).

9710.synopsis:
Error text "Flash/UV Eprom Write error", zero-terminated. ErrStr_tbl points here for RC_BWR;
GN_Esp returns it in BHL (bank MTH_BNK).

9737.synopsis:
Error text "Flash Erase error", zero-terminated. ErrStr_tbl points here for RC_BER; GN_Esp
returns it in BHL (bank MTH_BNK).

9755.synopsis:
Error text "Flash chip unknown", zero-terminated. ErrStr_tbl points here for RC_NFE; GN_Esp
returns it in BHL (bank MTH_BNK).

9774.synopsis:
Error text "Flash chip contains OZ", zero-terminated. ErrStr_tbl points here for RC_NOZ;
GN_Esp returns it in BHL (bank MTH_BNK).

9797.synopsis:
Error text "Battery Low", zero-terminated. ErrStr_tbl points here for RC_BTL; GN_Esp returns
it in BHL (bank MTH_BNK).

5.synopsis:
EazyLink's entry point, reached through the JP at $8000. Checks that the Index gave it its
contiguous RAM (IX+2, the end page + 1, must be $20+EAZ_BAD) and that it runs on the OZ it
was built for (OS_Nq NQ_Voz); otherwise it leaves through OS_Bye (A = RC_ROOM or 0). Then it
enables Escape detection, clears MenuBarPosn and UserToggles (line feed conversion and
translations off), calls Appl_Main and jumps to KillPopdown.
Entry: IX = the application's information block.
Exit: does not return (OS_Bye).

44.synopsis:
EazyLink's error handler, called with the code of a failed serial port or keyboard read
(from PollInput, the keyboard scan and the byte I/O's timeout check). RC_esc is acknowledged
(OS_Esc SC_ACK) and, like RC_quit, ends EazyLink: it falls into KillPopdown. Every other
code (RC_susp included) returns unchanged.
Entry: A = error code; Fc = 1.
Exit: A and F unchanged (codes other than RC_esc and RC_quit).
Changes: none.

63.synopsis:
Entry inside Errhandler: ends EazyLink. Closes any open transfer file (Close_file) and the
serial port dump files (Close_serportdump_filehandles), restores the Panel's original serial
port settings, purges the keyboard buffer, sets the Escape state (OS_Esc SC_SET) and quits
with OS_Bye, A = 0 (no error message), returning to the Index.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Exit: does not return.

81.synopsis:
EazyLink's main program. Opens the log window ("3") and the command window ("2"), resets
both translation tables to identity and loads the translations, zeroes the I/O handles,
switches automatic translation and CRLF conversion off (ESC_T_cmd2, ESC_C_cmd2), saves the
Panel's serial settings and installs EazyLink's own (Init_PanelSets), points IX at the
workspace ($2000) and clears its runtime flags. It writes 'Running', shows the baud rate and
version, draws the menu bar and loops in Fetch_synch for ever.
Entry: none.
Exit: does not return.

145.synopsis:
Text the command window shows (GN_Sop): select window "2", the SD_DTS character, then the
five menu lines in tiny type ("2+T" ... "2-T"): toggle translation mode, toggle linefeed
mode, use ISO translations, load translations, quit EazyLink. Null-terminated.

277.synopsis:
Draws the menu bar in the command window: selects window "2" without a cursor, moves to
column 0, row MenuBarPosn and applies reverse video to 26 characters ($1A).
Entry: MenuBarPosn = row of the bar (0-4).
Keeps: AF, HL.

311.synopsis:
VDU string 1, "3@", 0: the start of a cursor move; DisplMenuBar and RemoveMenuBar follow it
with the column and the row, each + 32.

315.synopsis:
VDU string selecting the command window: 1, "2H2" (window "2"), 1, "2-C" (cursor off),
null-terminated. Used by DisplMenuBar and RemoveMenuBar.

324.synopsis:
VDU string that draws the menu bar at the cursor: 1, "2+R" (reverse on), then 1, "2A",
32+$1A (apply the attributes to 26 characters), null-terminated.

333.synopsis:
Removes the menu bar from the command window: selects window "2" without a cursor, moves to
column 0, row MenuBarPosn and applies normal video (MenuBarOff) to 26 characters.
Entry: MenuBarPosn = row of the bar (0-4).
Keeps: AF, HL.

367.synopsis:
VDU string that removes the menu bar at the cursor: 1, "2-R" (reverse off), then 1, "2A",
32+$1A (apply to 26 characters), null-terminated.

376.synopsis:
Waits for a byte from the serial port while it runs the menu. Each key from PollInput is
handled here: Cursor Down and Up move the menu bar (wrapping between rows 0 and 4), ENTER
runs the command under the bar (through Command_lookup), and the codes
EazyLink_CC_dbgOn/dbgOff ($80/$81) switch serial port logging on and off. When a serial byte
arrives, PollInput returns straight to Poll's caller.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Exit: A = byte received from the serial port.

459.synopsis:
Polls the serial port and the keyboard. Resets PopDownTimeout to $FFFF (about ten minutes),
then loops: OS_Si Si_Gbt with a 1/10 second timeout; on a timeout it gives
CheckHandshakeMode the chance to switch the handshake mode, passes the error to Errhandler
and scans the keyboard (OS_Tin, 1 cs), whose timeouts count PopDownTimeout down to ShutDown.
A menu key returns to Poll; a serial byte is dumped to the log file when logging is on, then
PollInput discards its own and Poll's return addresses and jumps to Poll's caller with the
byte.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0, A = key code (IN_ENT, IN_DWN, IN_UP, $80 or $81) to Poll; or A =
serial byte, returned to Poll's caller (Fetch_synch).

595.synopsis:
Switches the Z88 off (OS_Off) when the keyboard has been idle for the pop-down timeout
(about ten minutes), then returns.
Entry: none.

612.synopsis:
Table of 6 words: the routine for each menu row, indexed by MenuBarPosn: toggle translation,
toggle line feed conversion, ISO translations, load translations, KillPopdown, and
disp_running. Read by ActivateCommand, which jumps to the entry.

624.synopsis:
Menu command: toggles bit 1 of UserToggles and switches automatic file translation on
(ESC_T_cmd1) or off (ESC_T_cmd2) to match; then writes 'Running' (falls through to
disp_running).
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: HL.

645.synopsis:
Menu command: toggles bit 0 of UserToggles and switches automatic CRLF conversion on
(ESC_C_cmd1) or off (ESC_C_cmd2) to match; then writes 'Running' (jumps to disp_running).
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: HL.

666.synopsis:
Menu command: installs the standard ISO/IBM translation tables (Use_StdTranslations), then
writes 'Running' (jumps to disp_running).

671.synopsis:
Menu command: loads the translation tables again from the external "translate.dat" file
(LoadTranslations), then falls into disp_running.

674.synopsis:
Writes the 'Running' message (message1) to the log window through Write_message.
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, HL.

680.synopsis:
EazyLink's main loop, which never returns. Waits for a byte through Poll. $01 starts the
EazyLink synch (extended_synch): when Check_synch confirms it, the handshake counter is
cleared, the synch is acknowledged (Send_synch) and Extended_ESC_commands runs one command.
$05 starts the PCLINK II synch (pclink_synch): after Check_synch it also signals Xon/Xoff
handshaking (SignalSerportMode), acknowledges, shows the flashing 'PCLINK II' text and runs
one PCLINK II command (removing the text when that fails). Other bytes, bad synchs and
failed acknowledgements are ignored.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Exit: does not return.

760.synopsis:
Runs one command of the EazyLink protocol after a synch: fetches the ESC command
(FetchBytes) and looks its letter up in EscCommands, jumping to the matching routine of the
subroutines table, which returns to the caller. A plain byte instead of ESC <letter> is a
protocol error (Msg_Protocol_error); an unknown letter returns.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Error: Fc = 1 when the serial port failed or timed out.

819.synopsis:
VDU string that greys the command window: 1, "2H2" (window "2"), 1, "2G+", null-terminated.
Written by GreyCommandWindow.

828.synopsis:
Switches the serial port to Xon/Xoff (software) handshaking: records SerportXonXoffMode in
CurrentSerportMode, clears SignalSerportMode, writes 'Using Xon/Xoff' and sets the Panel to
Xon/Xoff yes (SetPanel_SoftwareHandshaking, which installs the settings).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, HL.

853.synopsis:
Switches the serial port to RTS/CTS (hardware) handshaking: records SerportHardwareMode in
CurrentSerportMode, clears SignalSerportMode, writes 'Using RTS/CTS' and sets the Panel to
Xon/Xoff no (SetPanel_HardwareHandshaking, which installs the settings).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, HL.

959.synopsis:
Inline OS_Pout string of DisplayPclinkIIText: selects window "7", moves to column 0, row 7
and writes 'PCLINK II' flashing ("2+F", grey off with "2-G"), then flash off.
Null-terminated.

995.synopsis:
Inline OS_Pout string of RemovePclinkIIText: selects window "7", moves to column 0, row 7
and clears to the end of the line (1, "2C", 253). Null-terminated.

1277.synopsis:
Text "00/00/0000 00:00:00", null-terminated: the dummy create and update date stamp that
ESC_U_cmd sends for a file in a file area (":EPR.x"), which keeps no dates.

1464.synopsis: Text ", " (comma and space), null-terminated, placed after ESC_U_cmd2.

2211.synopsis:
Command ESC "c" (and the menu): switches automatic CRLF conversion on. Writes 'Auto CRLF ON'
to the log window and sets BB_LnfdConv in the runtime flags.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2222.synopsis:
Command ESC "C" (and the menu, and start-up): switches automatic CRLF conversion off. Writes
'Auto CRLF OFF' to the log window and clears BB_LnfdConv in the runtime flags.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2233.synopsis:
Command ESC "t" (and the menu): switches automatic character translation on. Writes 'Auto
Translation ON' and sets BB_CharTrans and its copy BB_CharTransCpy.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2248.synopsis:
Command ESC "T" (and the menu, and start-up): switches automatic character translation off.
Writes 'Auto Translation OFF' and clears BB_CharTrans and BB_CharTransCpy.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2263.synopsis:
Starts serial port logging (the <>D key code): creates the dump files
(Create_serportdump_files) and writes 'Serial port logging enabled' to the log window.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2281.synopsis:
Stops serial port logging (the <>Z key code): closes the dump files
(Close_serportdump_filehandles) and writes 'Serial port logging disabled'.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2299.synopsis:
Closes the serial port dump files: GN_Cl on serfile_in_handle and serfile_out_handle when
non-zero, then zeroes both handles and clears BB_SerportLog in the runtime flags.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, HL, IX.

2347.synopsis:
Creates the serial port dump files: closes open ones first, then creates "/rs232rcv.log" and
"/rs232snd.log" in the default RAM device (CreateFilename), moves their handles from
file_handle to serfile_in_handle and serfile_out_handle, and sets BB_SerportLog. When a file
cannot be created, both are closed (but BB_SerportLog is still set on the way out).
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF, BC, HL, IX.

2422.synopsis:
Switches character translation on for one transfer and remembers the user's setting:
BB_CharTransCpy gets the current BB_CharTrans, then BB_CharTrans is set. Restore_Traflag
undoes it.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF (works in AF', exchanged back).

2445.synopsis:
Restores the translation flag saved by Set_TraFlag: BB_CharTrans is set again when
BB_CharTransCpy is set, and cleared otherwise.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Keeps: AF (works in AF', exchanged back).

2464.synopsis:
Saves the Panel's serial port settings (Fetch_PanelSets) and installs EazyLink's own: 9600
baud transmit and receive, no parity, RTS/CTS handshaking (Define_PanelSettings); then falls
into EzyLnkSerPortTmt.
Entry: none.

2470.synopsis:
Entry inside Init_PanelSets: sets the OS_Si block I/O timeout to EazyLink_DefaultTimeout
(3000 cs, 30 seconds) through OS_Si SI_TMO.
Entry: none.

2478.synopsis:
Copies the Panel's serial port settings to the workspace so KillPopdown can restore them:
transmit and receive baud rates (each as a length byte and a word, Cpy_PA_Txb and
Cpy_PA_Rxb), Xon/Xoff (Cpy_PA_Xon) and parity (Cpy_PA_Par), read through OS_Nq.
Entry: none.
Error: an OS_Nq failure is reported through System_error (GN_Err) and returned, Fc = 1.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.

2565.synopsis:
Sets the Panel's Xon/Xoff parameter to No (hardware handshaking, OS_Sp PA_Xon), then falls
into InstallPanelSets.
Entry: none.

2577.synopsis:
Sets the Panel's Xon/Xoff parameter to Yes (software handshaking, OS_Sp PA_Xon), then falls
into InstallPanelSets.
Entry: none.

2587.synopsis:
Installs the Panel's serial port parameters (OS_Sp PA_Gfi with A = 0), which applies them to
the serial port.
Entry: none.

2705.synopsis:
Shows the system error message for an error code (GN_Err).
Entry: A = error code.
Keeps: AF.

2711.synopsis:
Writes a message as a new line in the log window: selects window "3" (vdulog), writes the
string (GN_Sop) and a new line (GN_Nln).
Entry: HL = null-terminated message.
Keeps: AF, HL.

2715.synopsis:
Inline OS_Pout string of Write_message: 1, "2H3", null-terminated, which selects the log
window "3".

2729.synopsis:
Saves the current machine time (GN_Gmt) in timestamp (3 bytes, centiseconds), the start of a
transfer for Disp_Elapsedtime.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

2751.synopsis:
Writes the time passed since Get_Time: reads the machine time (GN_Gmt), stores the
difference in timestamp, writes " in " and the elapsed time (GN_Ptm to the standard output
handle, from OS_Nq NQ_OHN), then a new line.
Entry: timestamp = the start time from Get_Time.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.
Keeps: AF, IX.

2785.synopsis: Inline OS_Pout string of Disp_Elapsedtime: " in ", null-terminated.

2818.synopsis:
Writes 'Protocol error: Unknown ESC command.' to the log window (Write_message).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.

2823.synopsis:
Writes 'File aborted.' to the log window (Write_message).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.

2828.synopsis:
Writes 'No Room.' to the log window (Write_message).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.

2833.synopsis:
Writes '- command aborted...' to the log window (Write_message).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.

2838.synopsis:
Writes 'File received' to the log window, followed by the transfer time (Disp_Elapsedtime).
Entry: timestamp = the start time from Get_Time.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.
Keeps: AF.

2857.synopsis:
Writes 'File sent' to the log window, followed by the transfer time (Disp_Elapsedtime).
Entry: timestamp = the start time from Get_Time.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.
Keeps: AF.

2876.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the command window: window "2" with bars, banner and bottom line
(2 | 192), at X 0, Y 0, 26 columns ($1A) by 8 rows, banner "Commands".

2883.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the log window: window "3" with bars and banner (3 | 128), at X
28 ($1C), Y 0, 62 columns ($3E) by 8 rows, banner "EazyLink".

2934.synopsis:
Copies the 7-byte wildcard ":RAM.*" with its terminator to filename_buffer.
Entry: none.
Exit: HL = filename_buffer; DE = filename_buffer+7; BC = 0.

3018.synopsis:
PCLINK II command ESC "N": sends the names of the files that match a path. Fetches the path
with acknowledgements (Fetch_pathname_ackn, translation on for it), then sends each matching
file name as ESC "N" <name> and ends with ESC "Z". A failure writes 'command aborted'; the
translation flag is restored in any case.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3057.synopsis:
PCLINK II command ESC "G": sends a Z88 file to the PC. Writes 'Send file', fetches the name
(Fetch_pathname_ackn), opens the file and sends it byte by byte with acknowledgements: a CR
goes as CR LF when CRLF conversion is on, a control code below 32 as ESC "B" <hex>. Ends
with ESC "Z" and the 'File sent' time; a failure writes 'command aborted' and closes the
file.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3172.synopsis:
PCLINK II command ESC "Q": answers ESC "Y" and ends EazyLink (KillPopdown). When the answer
cannot be sent, writes 'command aborted' and returns.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3235.synopsis:
Receives a path name with the PCLINK II byte-by-byte acknowledgement (Getbyte_ackn) into
filename_buffer, up to ESC and the byte after it ('Z' or 'F'). Appends '*' and a null,
keeping the position of the '*' in buffer.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; filename_buffer = the path + "*"; (buffer) = address of the '*'.
Error: Fc = 1 from Getbyte_ackn (serial port error or timeout).
Changes: AF, HL.

3264.synopsis:
PCLINK II command ESC "S": receives files from the PC. Writes 'Receive files', then for each
ESC "N" <name> creates the file (directories included) and writes the bytes that follow
until ESC "E": ESC "B" <hex> gives a raw byte and a LF is dropped when CRLF conversion is
on. ESC "Z" ends the batch. A protocol error aborts the file; a full RAM answers $01 to the
PC.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3466.synopsis:
EazyLink command ESC "q": answers ESC "Y" and ends EazyLink (KillPopdown). When the answer
cannot be sent, writes 'command aborted' and returns.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3569.synopsis:
EazyLink command ESC "n": sends the names of the files that match a path, each as ESC "N"
<name>, ending with ESC "Z". A path in a file card (":EPR.x") lists the entries of that
slot's file area instead (OS_Epr EP_Name). Translation is on while the path is fetched; a
failure writes 'command aborted'.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3662.synopsis:
EazyLink command ESC "b": receives a batch of files from the PC (ImpExp protocol). Each ESC
"N" <name> is followed by the file's data: a RAM file is created and filled
(ReceiveRamFile); an ":EPR.x" name is saved in the slot's file area when it can be written
(FileEprSaveFile, the older entry of the same name is deleted). On an error the rest of the
file is read and ignored up to ESC "E". ESC "Z" ends the batch.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3815.synopsis:
EazyLink command ESC "s": sends the files that match a path to the PC (ImpExp protocol): for
each file ESC "N" <name>, ESC "F", the data and ESC "E" (Transfer_ RamfileImage), with the
'File sent' time; ESC "Z" ends the batch. An ":EPR.x" path sends the one matching entry of
the slot's file area (FileEprSendFile).
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

3975.synopsis:
Sends one RAM file's contents to the PC: ESC "F", the file's blocks (SendFileBuffer) and ESC
"E" as end-of-file marker.
Entry: HL = file name; DE = buffer for its expanded name (GN_Opf).
Error: Fc = 1 when sending failed or the file could not be opened (reported through
System_error).

4014.synopsis:
EazyLink command ESC "k": backs up files to the PC (ImpExp protocol). Writes 'Backup Files',
fetches the path and sends the matching files (SearchFilesystem); then writes 'Scanning
directories...', collects the directories of all RAM devices in a file (Get_Directories),
sends that file and ends with ESC "Z".
Entry: IX = start_workspace.

4113.synopsis:
Receives an ESC-terminated path name (the protocol's 'Z', 'F' or 'N' byte ends it) into
filename_buffer, at most 256 bytes, through FetchBlock; the name is null-terminated.
Entry: IX = start_workspace.
Exit: Fz = 1, A = ESC terminator byte; BC = length; HL = filename_buffer.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error or timeout).
Changes: AF, BC.

4169.synopsis:
Builds the device name ":EPR.x" in filename_buffer, where x is the slot digit in A, and
null-terminates it. Send_Epr_devices sends the result for each slot with a file area.
Entry: A = slot digit ('0' to '3').
Exit: DE = filename_buffer; A = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

4527.synopsis:
Writes the bytes the last ReceiveBuffer put into the I/O buffer to the file entry in the
flash card, then decides how the reception goes on.
1. When (IY+IObufCtr) is not 0, blows that many bytes from (IY+IObuffer) with OS_Fep
FEP_Wrbl at the image pointer (IY+FeImgPtr), through segment 1, and stores the advanced
pointer back.
2. If blowing fails, marks the new entry deleted (MarkDeleted) and blows the size received
so far (BlowFileEntrySize).
3. Otherwise adds the block to the file size (AddBlck2FileSize). If the receive status had
Fc = 1, shows "File aborted." and takes the same error path as step 2.
Entry: AF = the status ReceiveBuffer returned (Fc = 1 serial port error, Fz = 1 end of file
or timeout); IY = save workspace; IX = EazyLink runtime variables.
Exit: Fc = 0; Fz = 1 at end of file, Fz = 0 when more file data is to come.
Error: Fc = 1 (write or serial port error; the entry is marked deleted).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.
Keeps: IX.

4599.synopsis:
Adds the size of the current I/O buffer, (IY+IObufCtr), to the 24-bit file size at
(IY+FileSize).
Entry: IY = save workspace.
Changes: F, BC, HL.

4864.synopsis:
Stores the received byte in the I/O buffer and counts it, then tells whether the buffer is
full.
Entry: A = byte; HL = next free position in the buffer; IY = save workspace.
Exit: HL = HL + 1; (IY+IObufCtr) incremented; Fc = 0, Fz = 1 when the count equals
(IY+IObufSize), the buffer is full.
Changes: F, DE, HL.

4885.synopsis:
Empties the flash save routine's I/O buffer: HL points at its start and the byte count
(IY+IObufCtr) is reset to 0.
Entry: IY = save workspace.
Exit: HL = (IY+IObuffer).
Changes: HL.

5068.synopsis:
Sends every file that matches a wildcard name to the remote computer for the ImpExp backup.
Opens a wildcard handler with A = 0 (files before directories) and runs filenames_loop when
it succeeds.
Entry: HL = wildcard filename; IX = EazyLink runtime variables.
Exit: Fc = 0 when all names are processed.
Error: Fc = 1 (no wildcard handler, or a transmission error).
Keeps: IX.

5081.synopsis:
The loop of SearchFilesystem. Fetches the next name from the wildcard handler; for each file
whose creation and update date stamps are equal (compare_dates), sends its name
(Transfer_filename) and contents (Transfer_RamfileImage), then opens it for update and
closes it, which gives it a new update date stamp. Directories and other files are skipped.
Exit: Fc = 0 when there are no more names (the wildcard handler is left open).
Error: Fc = 1 on a transmission error, after Clse_wcard_hndlr has released the handler.

5258.synopsis:
Writes a line to DIRECTORIES.CLI for every directory below the current one, recursively.
1. Moves to the first entry with OS_Dor DR_SON; returns Fc = 0 when there is none.
2. Pushes its name on the path (push_dir_name). For a directory, writes its path
(prt_dir_path), calls itself for its contents and reopens it (fetch_cur_dir).
3. Moves to each sibling with DR_SIB, replacing the last path name (upd_dir_name), and
handles directories the same way.
4. When there are no more siblings, removes the name from the path (pop_dir_name).
Entry: IX = DOR handle of the directory; file_buffer holds its path; (directory_ptr) = top
of the directory name stack.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (a directory DOR could not be reopened).

5315.synopsis:
Appends the CLI line of the directory whose path is in file_buffer to DIRECTORIES.CLI. Frees
the current DOR handle, opens the file for update, moves to its end ((file_ptr)), writes
cli_cmd3, the path and cli_cmd5, and closes it. Then adds the length written to (file_ptr)
and reopens the directory's DOR (fetch_cur_dir).
Entry: IX = DOR handle; file_buffer = path; (file_ptr) = current length of the file.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = DOR handle of the directory in file_buffer.
Error: Fc = 1 when the DOR cannot be reopened (a write error is reported by System_error,
not in Fc).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5400.synopsis:
Opens the DOR of the path held in file_buffer (OP_DOR through open_file).
Entry: file_buffer = path.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = DOR handle.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_xxx).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

5411.synopsis:
Appends the name of the current DOR to the path in file_buffer and pushes it on the
directory name stack. Puts a '/' before the free position the stack's top points at, reads
the name there (DT_NAM, up to 17 bytes) and pushes a pointer past its terminator.
Entry: IX = DOR handle; (directory_ptr) = top of the stack (in ScratchBuffer).
Exit: (directory_ptr) and IY = new top of the stack.
Changes: BC, DE, HL, IY.
Keeps: AF.

5455.synopsis:
Pops the last name off the directory name stack: clears the top entry, moves (directory_ptr)
down and null-terminates the path in file_buffer where that name began.
Entry: (directory_ptr) = top of the stack.
Exit: (directory_ptr) and IY = new top of the stack.
Changes: HL, IY.
Keeps: AF.

5488.synopsis:
Replaces the last name of the path with the name of the current DOR: pop_dir_name, then
push_dir_name.
Entry: IX = DOR handle.
Changes: BC, DE, HL, IY.
Keeps: AF.

5586.synopsis:
Reads the creation and update date stamps of the file named in filename_buffer into
creation_date and update_date (rw_date, 6 bytes each) and compares them.
Entry: filename_buffer = filename.
Exit: A = $FF when the stamps are equal, A = 0 when they differ.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL, IX.

5634.synopsis:
Opens a file or resource with GN_Opf, for a filename in local memory and an explicit name
buffer of 128 bytes.
Entry: A = open mode (OP_xxx); HL = filename; DE = buffer for the explicit filename.
Exit: Fc = 0; IX = handle; DE = end of the explicit name; B = segments, C = characters in
the name.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_xxx).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, IX.

5641.synopsis:
The name of the CLI file the backup writes the RAM devices' directories to,
":RAM.-/DIRECTORIES.CLI", null-terminated.

5664.synopsis: Length-prefixed text written first to DIRECTORIES.CLI: 3, then "#F" and CR.

5668.synopsis: Length-prefixed text written before each directory path in DIRECTORIES.CLI: 5, then "|CD|D".

5674.synopsis:
Length-prefixed text written after each directory path in DIRECTORIES.CLI: 3, then "~E" and
CR.

5689.synopsis:
Sends a synch sequence to the remote computer: the start byte twice, then the end byte.
Entry: H = start byte; L = end byte.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (ESC pressed or timeout).
Changes: AF, B.

5701.synopsis:
Receives a byte from the serial port (RxByte) and, when character translation is on
(BB_CharTrans), translates it; falls into TrnslteIncoming.
Entry: IX = EazyLink runtime variables.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = byte.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_xxx).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

5710.synopsis:
Translates a byte received from the remote computer through the table at TraTableOut.
Entry: A = byte.
Exit: A = translated byte.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

5719.synopsis:
Translates a byte to send to the remote computer through the table at TraTableIn.
Entry: A = byte.
Exit: A = translated byte.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

5736.synopsis:
Receives a byte from the serial port with OS_Si SI_GBT and a 30 second timeout. When serial
port logging is on (BB_SerportLog), copies the byte to the input log file. A failure goes to
Check_timeout.
Entry: IX = EazyLink runtime variables.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = byte.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Time on timeout).
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

5767.synopsis:
Sends a byte to the serial port with OS_Si SI_PBT and a 30 second timeout. When serial port
logging is on (BB_SerportLog), copies the byte to the output log file. A failure goes to
Check_timeout.
Entry: A = byte; IX = EazyLink runtime variables.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Time on timeout).
Keeps: BC, HL.

5787.synopsis:
Handles a failed serial port transfer: ErrHandler deals with ESC, suspend and quit, and on a
timeout (RC_Time) "Waiting..." is written to the log window.
Entry: A = error code (RC_xxx).
Exit: Fc = 1; A = error code.
Changes: F, HL.

5797.synopsis:
Writes "Waiting..." (message2) to the log window with Write_message.
Exit: HL = message2.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

5955.synopsis:
Converts a value 0 to 15 to its ASCII hex digit, '0' to '9' or 'A' to 'F'. This is the
serial byte module's own copy, used by Send_ESC_byte_ackn.
Entry: A = value (0 to 15).
Exit: A = ASCII hex digit.
Changes: AF.

5965.synopsis:
Sends ESC 'N' to the remote computer (Send_ESC_Rspnse).
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

5974.synopsis:
Sends ESC 'Y' to the remote computer (Send_ESC_Rspnse).
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

5983.synopsis:
Sends ESC 'Z' to the remote computer (Send_ESC_Rspnse).
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

5992.synopsis:
Sends ESC 'E' to the remote computer (Send_ESC_Rspnse).
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

6001.synopsis:
Sends ESC 'F' to the remote computer (Send_ESC_Rspnse).
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

6010.synopsis:
Sends CR and LF to the remote computer (Send_ESC_Rspnse).
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

6019.synopsis:
Sends an ESC byte in its encoded form, the four bytes ESC "B1B" (ESC_1B), untranslated.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

6033.synopsis:
Sends the 2-byte sequence at HL untranslated (SendStringRaw, OS_Si SI_PX), copying it to the
output log file when serial port logging is on.
Entry: HL = sequence.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error; A keeps its value).
Changes: F.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, HL.

6261.synopsis:
Sends the run of buffer bytes before a byte that needs special handling. SendFileBuffer
calls it before it sends an escape, CRLF or ESC B HH sequence, and falls into it after the
last byte to send the rest. Nothing is sent when the run is empty.
Entry: DE = start of the run; HL = position of the byte that ends it; Fc = 0.
Exit: Fc = 0; DE = HL + 1, the start of the next run.
Error: Fc = 1 (serial port error).
Changes: F, DE.
Keeps: A, BC, HL.

6345.synopsis:
Entry inside FetchBytes, after ESC 'B': receives the two ASCII hex digits of an encoded byte
(RxByte) and combines them.
Exit: A = byte; Fc = 0, Fz = 1 (a normal byte).
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (serial port error or timeout).
Changes: AF, B.

6615.synopsis:
Converts an ASCII hex digit to its value in the high nibble (ConvAsciHexNbble, times 16).
Entry: A = '0' to '9' or 'A' to 'F'.
Exit: A = value * 16.
Changes: AF.

6623.synopsis:
Converts an ASCII hex digit to its value: digits above '9' are taken as 'A' to 'F' (upper
case only).
Entry: A = '0' to '9' or 'A' to 'F'.
Exit: A = 0 to 15.
Changes: AF.

6732.synopsis:
Installs the built-in translation tables: copies the 512 bytes at IBM_TraTableIn over
TraTableIn and TraTableOut, and writes "Using ISO translations" to the log window.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.
Keeps: AF.

6752.synopsis:
Installs one translation pair read from the translation file: TraTableIn(D) = E and
TraTableOut(E) = D.
Entry: D = Z88 byte; E = byte on the remote computer.
Changes: F.
Keeps: BC, HL.

6771.synopsis:
Reads the next byte of the open file ((file_handle)) with OS_Gb, unless the file is at its
end (OS_Frm FA_EOF).
Entry: (file_handle) = open file.
Exit: Fz = 0, A = byte; Fz = 1 at end of file.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: DE, IX.

6829.synopsis:
Releases the wildcard handler held in (wildcard_handle) with GN_Wcl.
Keeps: AF, IX.

6843.synopsis:
Abandons the file being received: closes it (Close_file) and deletes the file named in
filename_buffer with GN_Del.
Keeps: AF, BC, HL.

6861.synopsis:
Puts a byte into the file buffer and counts it ((buffer), (buflen)). When the buffer holds
1280 bytes it is written to the file with Flush_buffer.
Entry: A = byte.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 when a full buffer could not be written.
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: A, BC.

6893.synopsis:
Writes the (buflen) bytes of file_buffer to the open file ((file_handle)) with OS_Mv, when
there are any, then falls into Reset_buffer_ptrs, which empties the buffer.
Exit: Fc = 0; (buffer) = file_buffer; (buflen) = 0.
Error: Fc = 1 from OS_Mv (A keeps its value, not an error code).
Changes: F, HL (HL = the AF value on entry).
Keeps: A, BC, DE, IX.

6939.synopsis:
Reads up to 1280 bytes of the open file ((file_handle)) into file_buffer with OS_Mv and
stores the number read in (buflen). Nothing is read at end of file.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 0; (buflen) = bytes read.
Error: Fc = 1 (OS_Frm error); Fz = 1 at end of file; an OS_Mv error is not reported.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.
Keeps: IX.

6975.synopsis:
Opens a file with GN_Opf (explicit name buffer of 128 bytes) and keeps its handle in
(file_handle).
Entry: A = open mode (OP_xxx); HL = filename; DE = buffer for the explicit filename.
Exit: Fc = 0; (file_handle) = handle; DE = end of the explicit name; B = segments, C =
characters in the name.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_xxx).
Changes: AF, BC, DE.
Keeps: HL, IX.

6992.synopsis:
Reads the size of the open file ((file_handle)) with OS_Frm FA_EXT and stores it as a 32-bit
value at (File_ptr), low word first.
Exit: (File_ptr) = file size; DEBC = file size.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.
Keeps: IX.

7016.synopsis:
Closes the open file with GN_Cl and clears (file_handle). Does nothing when (file_handle) is
0, so it can be called after an error.
Keeps: AF, HL, IX.

7210.synopsis:
Converts a value 0 to 15 to its ASCII hex digit, '0' to '9' or 'A' to 'F'. This is the
CRC-32 module's copy, the one other modules call (Send_ESC_B).
Entry: A = value (0 to 15).
Exit: A = ASCII hex digit.
Changes: AF.

7227.synopsis:
The name of the translation file LoadTranslations reads, ":*//Translate.dat",
null-terminated.

7245.synopsis: The wildcard name of the RAM devices, ":RAM.*", null-terminated.

7252.synopsis:
The text ":EPR." without a terminator: EprDev_name copies its 5 bytes and appends the slot
digit.

7257.synopsis:
The name of the serial port input log file, "/rs232rcv.log", null-terminated (created in the
default RAM device).

7271.synopsis: The name of the serial port output log file, "/rs232snd.log", null-terminated.

7285.synopsis:
The message "Serial port logging ", led by the sequence 1, "2H3" that selects window 3,
null-terminated. msg_srdmpfl_enbl or msg_srdmpf_dsble follows it on screen.

7327.synopsis:
Two bytes: the start (5) and end (6) bytes of the PCLINK II synch sequence, read by
Fetch_synch.

7329.synopsis:
Two bytes: the start (1) and end (2) bytes of the EazyLink extended protocol synch sequence,
read by Fetch_synch.

7331.synopsis: The title "EazyLink", null-terminated, of the log window (LogWinDef).

7340.synopsis: The title "Commands", null-terminated, of the command window (CmdWinDef).

7357.synopsis: The message "Waiting...", null-terminated, shown on a serial port timeout.

7452.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Auto CRLF OFF", written to the log window by ESC_C_cmd2 when the
client switches off automatic CRLF conversion (ESC "C").

7466.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Receive Files", written to the log window by ImpExp_Receive (ESC
"b").

7480.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "Send Files", written to the log window by ImpExp_Send (ESC "s").

7491.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Backup Files", written to the log window by ImpExp_Backup (ESC
"k").

7504.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Sending ", printed before each file name while ImpExp_Send sends a
batch of RAM files or a file area entry.

7513.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Scanning directories...", written by ImpExp_Backup before it
collects the directories of all RAM devices.

7537.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Using file translations", written by LoadTranslations after it has
installed the byte pairs of the translation file.

7561.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Using ISO translations", written by Use_StdTranslations after it
has copied the built-in IBM tables into the translation tables.

7584.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Update Translation Table", written by ESC_Z_cmd before it reloads
the translation file.

7609.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "Delete file/dir ", written by ESC_R_cmd before the name it deletes.

7626.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "Create dir ", written by ESC_Y_cmd before the directory it creates.

7638.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "Rename file ", written by ESC_W_cmd before the file it renames.

7651.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Set Z88 Clock", written by ESC_p_cmd (ESC "p") when the client sets
the system clock.

7665.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "Using Xon/Xoff", written by UseSoftwareHandshaking.

7680.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "Using RTS/CTS", written by UseHardwareHandshaking.

7694.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "File received", printed in the log window by Msg_file_received,
followed by the elapsed time.

7708.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Change to 38.400bps", written by ESC_L_cmd before it switches the
serial port to 38400 baud.

7728.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "File sent", printed in the log window by Msg_file_sent, followed by
the elapsed time.

7738.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "Escape pressed...."; no EazyLink code loads its address.

7757.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "File open error.", written by Msg_File_open_error.

7774.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "- command aborted...", written by Msg_Command_aborted.

7795.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "Protocol error: Unknown ESC command.", written by
Msg_Protocol_error.

7832.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "File aborted.", written by Msg_file_aborted.

7846.synopsis: Zero-terminated message "No Room.", written by Msg_No_Room.

7855.synopsis:
Zero-terminated message "File Card Write Error.", written when a received file cannot be
written to a file card.

7878.synopsis:
Zero-terminated protocol response ESC "Z", sent by Send_ESC_Z: the end of a list of names or
files.

7881.synopsis: Zero-terminated protocol response ESC "F", sent by Send_ESC_F.

7884.synopsis: Zero-terminated protocol response ESC "E", sent by Send_ESC_E.

7887.synopsis: Zero-terminated protocol response ESC "N", sent by Send_ESC_N before a name.

7890.synopsis:
Zero-terminated protocol response ESC "Y", sent by Send_ESC_Y as the acknowledgement of a
command (ESC_A_cmd1 answers the PCLINK II 'Hello' with it).

7893.synopsis:
Zero-terminated protocol response ESC "B"; blockio.asm imports it, but no instruction loads
its address.

7896.synopsis:
Zero-terminated protocol response ESC ESC; blockio.asm imports it, but no instruction loads
its address.

7899.synopsis:
The 4 bytes ESC "B1B" (zero-terminated): the escaped form of an ESC byte in the data stream,
sent by Send_ESC.

7904.synopsis: Zero-terminated CR, LF pair, sent by Send_CRLF.

7907.synopsis:
Zero-terminated ESC "N" ".": the current directory entry that ESC_D_cmd2 and the PCLINK II
directory command send first in a directory list.

7911.synopsis:
Zero-terminated ESC "N" "..": the parent directory entry sent after Current_dir when the
path is below the root.

7916.synopsis:
Word 9600: the default transmit and receive baud rate that Define_PanelSettings installs
with OS_Sp (PA_Txb, PA_Rxb).

7918.synopsis:
Word 38400: the transmit and receive baud rate that ESC_L_cmd installs with OS_Sp when the
client asks for light speed (ESC "L").

7920.synopsis:
Byte 'N': the Panel value given to OS_Sp for parity none (PA_Par) and for Xon/Xoff off
(PA_Xon).

7921.synopsis:
Byte 'Y': the Panel value given to OS_Sp for Xon/Xoff on (PA_Xon) by
SetPanel_SoftwareHandshaking.

7960.synopsis:
Table of words: the handler address of each ESC command, in the order of the command letters
in EscCommands. EscCommand finds the letter's index, doubles it, reads the word here and
jumps to it.

8292.synopsis:
Table of 256 bytes: the default outgoing (IBM to Z88 ISO) translation, indexed by byte
value. It follows IBM_TraTableIn, and Use_StdTranslations copies both (512 bytes) into
TraTableIn and TraTableOut.

8565.synopsis:
Entry inside SetBlinkScreen: sets the LCD-on bit (BB_COMLCDON) in A, the COM register value
being built.
Entry: A = COM value.
Exit: A = COM value with the LCD on.
Changes: A.

8568.synopsis:
Switches the LCD on: calls SetBlinkScreen with Fz = 1, which sets BB_COMLCDON in the
BLSC_COM soft copy and writes it to the Blink COM register.
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

8735.synopsis:
Entry inside FileEprTransferBlockSize: the remaining file image fits in the current bank, so
the block is the whole remainder.
Entry: DE' = remaining file size (at most 16K).
Exit: HL' = block size (the file size); DE' = 0.
Changes: DE', HL'.

8742.synopsis:
Entry inside FileEprTransferBlockSize: the remaining file image crosses the bank boundary,
so the block is only the space left in this bank.
Entry: DE = space left in the bank; CDE' = remaining file size; Fc = 0.
Exit: HL' = block size (the bank space); CDE' = file size less the bank space.
Changes: BC', DE', HL'.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

8957.synopsis:
Creates one directory: opens the path at IY with GN_Opf in OP_DIR mode and frees the DOR
handle it returns. A directory that exists (RC_EXIS) or is in use (RC_USE) counts as
success.
Entry: IY = pathname, terminated after the level to create; C = buffer length.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, DE, IX.
Keeps: BC, HL.

9107.synopsis:
Scans backwards from HL for the directory separator '/'.
Entry: HL = position inside a pathname, after a '/'.
Exit: HL = the separator.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

9308.synopsis:
The Filer's main loop: reads a key with OS_In and acts on it. RC_Quit and RC_Esc leave
through ExitFiler, RC_Draw redraws with InitDisplay. A zero byte is followed by an extended
code: ENTER, the four arrows, $20 (ShEnter), $32 (ChDirDown), $31 (ChDirUp) and $21-$30
(DoCmd with A = 0-15); other keys are ignored.

9451.synopsis:
Zero-terminated mailbox name "NAME": ExitFiler writes the first selected file name to this
mailbox with OS_Sr (SR_WPD).

9456.synopsis:
Tests whether IX holds a handle.
Entry: IX = handle or 0.
Exit: Fz = 1 when IX = 0; DE = IX.
Changes: AF, DE.

10226.synopsis:
Closes the source resource if one is open: frees it with OS_Dor (DR_FRE) when bit 4 of
f_CmdFlags marks a DOR, otherwise closes it with OS_Cl, and writes IX back to
f_SourceHandle.
Entry: f_SourceHandle = handle or 0.
Changes: AF, DE, IX.

10255.synopsis:
Closes the temporary file with OS_Cl if f_TmpFileHandle holds a handle, and writes IX back
to f_TmpFileHandle.
Entry: f_TmpFileHandle = handle or 0.
Changes: AF, DE, IX.

10271.synopsis:
Closes the destination file with OS_Cl if f_DestHandle holds a handle, and writes IX back to
f_DestHandle.
Entry: f_DestHandle = handle or 0.
Exit: Fz = 0 when a file was closed; Fz = 1 when there was none.
Changes: AF, DE, IX.

10310.synopsis:
Frees the DOR handle in IX with OS_Dor (DR_FRE), if IX is not 0.
Entry: IX = DOR handle or 0.
Changes: AF, DE.

10319.synopsis:
Opens f_SourceName with OpenFile (GN_Opf): as a DOR (OP_DOR) when bit 4 of f_CmdFlags is
set, otherwise for reading (OP_IN). Stores IX in f_SourceHandle and A in f_SourceType, also
after an error.
Entry: f_SourceName = name; f_CmdFlags.
Exit: Fc = 0, IX = handle; A = DOR type.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

10350.synopsis:
Lets the user edit a file name and checks it: shows the cursor, edits the buffer with GN_Sip
at the given position (redrawing after RC_Susp), parses the result with GN_Prs, and shows a
bad name with GN_Err. Ends through ToggleCrsr, which hides the cursor again.
Entry: DE = buffer, holding the text to edit; B = column, C = row.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = key that ended the input; C = GN_Prs flags.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

10987.synopsis:
Draws the whole Filer screen.
1. Reads the filename match string (GetMatchString); clears f_NumDirEntries.
2. Opens the command window with GN_Win and sets up the directory window.
3. Prints the title: "NM" when the match string is not "*", "DIRECTORY " and the current
directory, expanded with GN_Fex and compressed with GN_Fcm.
4. If IX is 0, opens the current directory's DOR into f_CurrentDirHandle, freeing it again
when it is not a device or a directory.
5. Draws the directory window (DrawDirWindow) when there is a directory, then the command
window, and the selector bar (ApplyReverse).
Entry: IX = current directory DOR handle, or 0.

11182.synopsis:
Zero-terminated ".", the current directory. The byte before it (ParentDir_txt) makes "..".
InitDisplay expands it to show the current path.

11184.synopsis:
Draws the command window: selects and clears window 1, then prints up to 7 command names
from f_SelectedCmd onwards, one a line, stopping at the last command.
Entry: f_SelectedCmd.

11213.synopsis:
Draws the directory window: selects and clears window 2, then prints up to 7 lines of 3
matching entries, starting with entry f_TopDirEntry (SkipBCMatches). When the top entry lies
past the end, it is reset to 0 and the window drawn again. Sets f_NumDirEntries to the
number shown.
Entry: IX = directory DOR handle.
Keeps: IX.

11289.synopsis:
Prints one line of up to 3 directory entries, starting with the current match: a bullet
arrow for a selected entry, the name padded to 16 characters (directories between PrntDir
toggles), and a space. FindMatch moves on to the next entry.
Entry: IX = DOR of a matching entry, its name in f_StrBuffer.
Exit: B = number of entries printed; Fc = 0 when 3 were printed.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code when the entries ran out (B < 3).

11351.synopsis:
Sends the VDU sequence 1, "B", which toggles bold; Print3Matches prints a directory name
between two of them.
Entry: none.

11377.synopsis:
Moves to match number BC of a directory: duplicates the directory DOR, takes its first child
with OS_Dor (DR_SON) and calls FindMatch BC + 1 times.
Entry: IX = directory DOR handle (0 gives RC_Eof); BC = matches to skip.
Exit: Fc = 0, IX = DOR of the match, its name in f_StrBuffer.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (RC_Eof when the entries ran out).
Keeps: BC.

11431.synopsis:
Calls FreeDOR (frees the DOR handle in IX if there is one), keeping AF.
Entry: IX = DOR handle or 0.
Changes: DE.
Keeps: AF.

11437.synopsis:
Finds the next directory entry whose name matches f_MatchString: steps to the next sibling
with OS_Dor (DR_SIB), unless bit 1 of f_Flags2 says to test the current DOR first, reads its
name record into f_StrBuffer and matches it with GN_Wsm. Stores the minor type in
f_SourceType.
Entry: IX = DOR handle; f_Flags2 bit 1.
Exit: Fc = 0, IX = DOR of the match, its name in f_StrBuffer.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (no more entries).
Keeps: BC.

11485.synopsis:
Reads the current filename match string (OS_Nq, NQ_Fnm) and copies it to f_MatchString with
CopyExtended.
Entry: none.

11526.synopsis:
Draws the selector bar: switches reverse on, applies it over the selector's field with
RemoveHighlight, and switches reverse off.
Entry: f_ActiveWd; f_SelectorPos.

11535.synopsis:
Applies the current attributes over the selector's field: 24 characters on row f_SelectorPos
of the command window, or the 18 characters of entry f_SelectorPos in the directory window.
Without reverse set, this removes the highlight.
Entry: f_ActiveWd (0 = command window); f_SelectorPos.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

11565.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to directory entry A: row A / 3, column 18 * (A mod 3).
Entry: A = entry number.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

11656.synopsis:
Selects the entry under the selector: stores the path first when the list is empty
(GetPath), reads the entry's name from the screen, allocates a 22 byte node from f_MemPool,
copies the name into it, queues it on the selected list, draws the bullet arrow, counts it
in f_NumSelected and redraws the bar. An error is shown with GN_Err (RC_Room when 255 are
selected).
Entry: f_SelectorPos.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Keeps: IX.

11861.synopsis:
Empties the selected-file list: frees every node on f_SelectedList through FreeSelNode and
sets f_NumSelected to 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: f_SelectedList null; f_NumSelected = 0; A = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL; S1 binding.
Keeps: IX, IY.

11998.synopsis:
Reads the three-byte link at IY into CDE (bank in C).
Entry: IY = a link (offset low, offset high, bank).
Exit: C = bank; DE = offset.
Changes: C, DE.

12134.synopsis:
Reads the name of the directory entry under the selector from the screen. Moves to entry
f_SelectorPos (CrsrToPosA), one column right, reads 16 characters with OS_Nq NQ_Rds into
f_StrBuffer, then removes the spaces and zero-terminates it.
Entry: f_SelectorPos = entry number in the directory window.
Exit: f_StrBuffer = the entry's name, zero-terminated; DE = its terminator; A = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

12175.synopsis:
Prints the right bullet arrow character (VDU 1,$F5) with OS_Pout.
Entry: none.

12181.synopsis:
Clears the current window from the cursor to the end of the line (VDU 1,"2C",$FD).
Entry: none.

12189.synopsis:
Prints the prompt "Name :" at column 13, row 1 of the current window.
Entry: none.

12204.synopsis:
Prints the prompt "New name :" at column 9, row 3 of the current window.
Entry: none.

12240.synopsis:
Selects window 1, the Filer's commands window (VDU 1,"2I1").
Entry: none.

12248.synopsis:
Selects window 2, the Filer's directory window (VDU 1,"2I2").
Entry: none.

12256.synopsis:
Selects window 3, the window a command works in (VDU 1,"2I3").
Entry: none.

12264.synopsis:
Sets normal justification in the current window (VDU 1,"2JN").
Entry: none.

12272.synopsis:
Sets centre justification in the current window (VDU 1,"2JC").
Entry: none.

12280.synopsis:
Sends VDU 1,"2.]", which the screen driver passes to DC_Gen: it stops the output of the
current CLI going to the printer (sets CLIF_B_DISABLEPRT). PrntDotOpen undoes it.
Entry: none.

12288.synopsis:
Sends VDU 1,"2.[", which the screen driver passes to DC_Gen: it lets the output of the
current CLI go to the printer again (clears CLIF_B_DISABLEPRT).
Entry: none.

12296.synopsis:
Toggles the cursor of the current window (VDU 1,"C").
Entry: none.

12302.synopsis:
Toggles the tiny font and the capitals attribute (VDU 1,"T",1,"L").
Entry: none.

12310.synopsis:
Toggles underline (VDU 1,"U"), then falls into PrntReverse to toggle reverse video.
Entry: none.

12321.synopsis:
Prints " IN SLOT n", n being the default File Card slot; DoCmd adds it to the title of a
command whose block ends in 'S'.
Entry: f_filecardslot = slot (0-3).
Changes: AF.

12341.synopsis:
Moves the cursor of the current window to column B, row C (VDU 1,"3@",32+B,32+C).
Entry: B = column; C = row.
Keeps: AF.

12369.synopsis:
GN_Win block of the commands window, read by InitDisplay: byte $91 (@10010000 with window ID
1), position word $0000, size word $0818, then the address of the banner text (cmds_banner).

12385.synopsis: "Yes", zero-terminated: the answer GetYesNo shows for yes.

12389.synopsis: "No ", zero-terminated and padded to the width of "Yes": the answer GetYesNo shows for no.

12393.synopsis:
" to ", zero-terminated: printed between the source and destination names of a command
(DoCmd, TreeCopy).

12398.synopsis:
Table of 16 words: the command block of each Filer command, in the order of the MTH command
codes $21-$30: Catalogue files, Catalogue File Card, Save to File Card, Fetch from File
Card, Copy, Rename, Erase, View, Select Directory, Select Device, Select File Card, Execute,
Create Directory, Create File Card, Tree copy and Name match. GetCmdData indexes it. A block
is a flags byte, the handler's address and the name. Flags: bit 0 ask for a destination
name; 1 display each file (with Confirm each file); 2 the handler does its own input, so
DoCmd prompts for nothing; 3 ignore the selected files; 4 open the source as a DOR, not a
file; 5 page wait; 6 beep when done; 7 empty the selected list when done. DoCmd calls the
handler for each source file in turn; it returns Fc = 1, A = error code to stop, and with
flag 3 set it is called once.

12443.synopsis:
Command block of the "Copy " command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $83 (ask
destination, display each file, empty the selected list), the handler's address (Copy), then
the name "Copy " for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12446.synopsis:
The name text of the Copy command block, "Copy ", zero-terminated; TreeCopy also prints it
before each file it copies.

12452.synopsis:
Command block of the "Erase " command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $92 (display
each file, source as a DOR, empty the selected list), the handler's address (Erase), then
the name "Erase " for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12462.synopsis:
Command block of the "Catalogue files" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $A4
(own input, page wait, empty the selected list), the handler's address (CatalogueFiles),
then the name "Catalogue files" for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12481.synopsis:
Command block of the "Save to File Card" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte
$C2 (display each file, beep when done, empty the selected list), the handler's address
(Save), then the name "Save to File Card" for the title bar, zero-terminated, followed by
'S', which makes DoCmd append " IN SLOT n" (PrFcSlotNo) to the title.

12503.synopsis:
Command block of the "Fetch from File Card" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte
$0D (ask destination, own input, ignore the selected files), the handler's address (Fetch),
then the name "Fetch from File Card" for the title bar, zero-terminated, followed by 'S',
which makes DoCmd append " IN SLOT n" (PrFcSlotNo) to the title.

12528.synopsis:
Command block of the "Execute " command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $08 (ignore
the selected files), the handler's address (Execute), then the name "Execute " for the title
bar, zero-terminated.

12540.synopsis:
Command block of the "Select Directory" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $0C
