(own input, ignore the selected files), the handler's address (SelectDir), then the name
"Select Directory" for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12560.synopsis:
Command block of the "Name match" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $0C (own
input, ignore the selected files), the handler's address (NameMatch), then the name "Name
match" for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12574.synopsis:
Command block of the "Rename " command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $90 (source
as a DOR, empty the selected list), the handler's address (Rename), then the name "Rename "
for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12585.synopsis:
Command block of the "View" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $80 (empty the
selected list), the handler's address (View), then the name "View" for the title bar,
zero-terminated.

12593.synopsis:
Command block of the "Select Device" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $0C
(own input, ignore the selected files), the handler's address (SelectDevice), then the name
"Select Device" for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12610.synopsis:
Command block of the "Select File Card" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $2C
(own input, ignore the selected files, page wait), the handler's address (SelectFileCard),
then the name "Select File Card" for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12630.synopsis:
Command block of the "Create File Card" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $2C
(own input, ignore the selected files, page wait), the handler's address (CreateFileCard),
then the name "Create File Card" for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12650.synopsis:
Command block of the "Create Directory" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte $0C
(own input, ignore the selected files), the handler's address (CreateDir), then the name
"Create Directory" for the title bar, zero-terminated.

12670.synopsis:
Command block of the "Catalogue File Card" command, one of the CmdTable entries: flags byte
$2C (own input, ignore the selected files, page wait), the handler's address
(CatalogueEPROM), then the name "Catalogue File Card" for the title bar, zero-terminated,
followed by 'S', which makes DoCmd append " IN SLOT n" (PrFcSlotNo) to the title.

12762.synopsis:
The Select Device command (CmdTable): asks for a device name, showing the current one, and
makes it the current device.
1. Copies the current device into f_SourceName (GetDev) and edits it (InputSrcName).
2. Parses it with GN_Pfs. If that fails with A = 9 (RC_Eof; the source says an extension and
"/." were used), sets the device to the text anyway (OS_Sp, SP_Dev) and asks again.
3. Accepts only a name with the device and extension flags and no others, whose DOR (GN_Opf,
OP_DOR) is a device (Dm_Dev); then sets it with OS_Sp SP_Dev, empties f_SourceName and calls
ChgDir. Anything else is RC_Ivf. An error is shown with GN_Err; after RC_Susp the name is
asked again. Leaves through ToggleCrsr.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; A = RC_Esc when ESC was pressed, else the error already shown.

12872.synopsis:
Lets the user choose a File Card slot. SelectFileCard falls into it with its own prompt;
CreateFileCard calls it with another. Prints the prompt and the help line, then shows the
slot number (f_filecardslot) under the cursor and reads keys (GetKey): 0-3 choose that slot
when it holds a flash chip (checkflash) or no RAM card (checkram); <>J (LF) moves to the
next such slot, wrapping from 3 to 0; ENTER accepts.
Entry: HL = prompt text, zero-terminated; f_filecardslot = slot shown first.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = IN_ENT; f_filecardslot = the chosen slot.
Error: Fc = 1; A = RC_Esc when ESC was pressed.

12963.synopsis:
Asks whether slot A holds a flash chip (OS_Fep, FEP_CDID).
Entry: A = slot.
Exit: Fc = 0 when a flash chip was identified, Fc = 1 when not; A = slot.
Keeps: A, BC.

12973.synopsis:
Asks whether slot A holds RAM (OS_Nq, Nq_Mfp); the error code is ignored.
Entry: A = slot.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the slot has RAM, Fc = 1 when not; A = E = slot.
Keeps: A, BC, D.

12985.synopsis:
The Select File Card prompt, "Select slot for default File Card", zero-terminated;
SelectFileCard passes it to SelectSlotPrompt.

13097.synopsis:
Reads a key with OS_In for SelectSlotPrompt; a zero byte (the prefix of an extended key) is
skipped.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = key code. Another OS_In error than RC_Esc also comes back with Fc = 0 and
A = the error code.
Error: Fc = 1; A = RC_Esc.

13227.synopsis:
The Create File Card prompt, "Select slot to create or re-format File Card",
zero-terminated; CreateFileCard passes it to SelectSlotPrompt.

13272.synopsis:
The Erase command's handler (CmdTable), called by DoCmd for each source file: frees the
source DOR (CloseSource) and deletes the file named in f_SourceName with GN_Del.
Entry: f_SourceName = expanded file name; f_SourceHandle = its DOR handle (or 0).
Exit: Fc = 0; f_SourceHandle = IX after GN_Del.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code from GN_Del.

13363.synopsis:
The View command's handler (CmdTable): closes the source handle, checks that f_SourceName is
a file (ValidateFileType), opens it for reading and shows it as a hex and ASCII dump
(ViewFile), then closes it.
Entry: f_SourceName = expanded file name.
Exit: the file closed again (CloseSource).
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code (RC_Ftm when it is not a file).

13390.synopsis:
The Save to File Card command's handler (CmdTable), called for each source file: closes the
source handle, checks that f_SourceName is a file (ValidateFileType) and writes it into the
file area of the default slot with OS_Epr EP_NewFile.
Entry: f_SourceName = expanded file name; f_filecardslot = slot.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code (RC_Ftm when it is not a file, else from OS_Epr).

13914.synopsis:
Asks for the name of an existing directory or device, for TreeCopy. Edits the buffer
(InputLine), expands it in place (ExpandFname) and opens its DOR (OpenFile, OP_DOR); the
type must be Dm_Dev or Dn_Dir, else RC_Ftm. An error other than RC_Esc is shown with GN_Err,
and after RC_Susp the input starts again.
Entry: DE = name buffer (NBUFSIZE); B = column, C = row of the input.
Exit: Fc = 0; buffer = the expanded name.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code (RC_Esc not shown).
Keeps: BC, DE.

13966.synopsis:
Finds the end of a file name: moves HL to its first byte below $21.
Entry: HL = name.
Exit: HL = the terminator; A = it; Fc = 1.
Changes: AF, HL.

13973.synopsis:
The Create Directory command (CmdTable): asks for a name in an empty input line and creates
the directory by opening it with OP_DIR (OpenFile), then frees the handle (FreeDOR). An
error other than RC_Esc is shown with GN_Err; after RC_Susp the name is asked again. Leaves
through ToggleCrsr.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code (RC_Esc when ESC was pressed).

14016.synopsis:
The Catalogue files command (CmdTable): lists files with their dates and sizes.
1. With no files selected, asks for a name (an empty one becomes "*"), expands it and opens
a wildcard handler (GN_Opw, forward scan, full path).
2. Takes each match (GN_Wfn), or each selected file (GetNextSelected), counts its segments
(GN_Prs) and indents it by one space per segment after the first.
3. Opens its DOR: a file is printed by CatFile, anything else by its name; then a new line
with page wait (PntLF_pagewait).
4. Closes the wildcard handler at the end (RC_Eof) or on an error; an error other than
RC_Esc is shown with GN_Err, and after RC_Susp the name is asked again.
Entry: f_NumSelected, f_SelectedList.
Exit: Fc = 0 when the list ended.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code (RC_Esc when ESC was pressed).

14240.synopsis:
Prints one line of the catalogue for a file: its name (N record, PrntStr16), its creation
and update dates (C and U records, GN_Sdo) and its size (X record, GN_Pdn), separated by
spaces. The records are read into a 17-byte buffer on the stack (ReadSrcRecord); without an
X record the size is left out.
Entry: f_SourceHandle = the file's DOR handle.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

14408.synopsis:
The Select Directory command (CmdTable): asks for a directory, showing the current one
(GetDir), then checks it and makes it current (falls into ChgDir). In ChgDir: an empty name
goes straight to setting it; otherwise the name's DOR (OpenFile, OP_DOR) must be a directory
or device, else RC_Ftm. An error is shown with GN_Err; after RC_Susp the name is asked
again. Then VerifiedChDir sets it.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code (RC_Esc when ESC was pressed).

14488.synopsis:
Entry inside ChgDir (SelectDir), also called by ChDir: sets the current directory and, when
files are selected, records it in the selected list.
1. Parses f_SourceName with GN_Pfs and ignores the flags (the source asks what this does and
calls it a probable bug); GN_Pfs leaves HL at the end of the first segment.
2. Sets the current directory from the text at HL (OS_Sp, SP_Dir); ChgDir's empty name
enters here at this step.
3. With files selected, walks to the last node of f_SelectedList; a path node there (type 1)
is freed (FreeSelNode). Then adds the current path as a new node (GetPath).
Entry: f_SourceName = expanded directory name.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IY.

14545.synopsis:
The Name match command (CmdTable): edits the current name match string (OS_Nq, NQ_Fnm) and
sets the new one (OS_Sp, SP_Fnm). The text must parse as one name segment (GN_Pfs) without
directory or device parts (flags $7C), else RC_Ivf. An error other than RC_Esc is shown with
GN_Err; after RC_Susp the input starts again. Leaves through ToggleCrsr.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code (RC_Esc when ESC was pressed).

14625.synopsis:
Waits for a key at the end of a page of output when that is allowed: clears the line count
(f_OutLnCnt) and, when the output is not teed (the NQ_Tot handle is 0) and the command
enables page wait (f_CmdFlags bit 5), calls OS_Sr SR_PWT, repeating it after RC_Susp.
Entry: f_CmdFlags.
Exit: Fc = 0; f_OutLnCnt = 0.
Error: Fc = 1; A = error code from SR_PWT (RC_Esc when ESC was pressed).
Changes: AF, BC.
Keeps: HL, IX.

14766.synopsis:
Removes the first node of the selected list and frees it (GetLinkBHL, FreeSelNode). It sits
inside GetNextSelected's code, which calls it and branches around it.
Entry: f_SelectedList not empty.
Exit: IY = f_SelectedList.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IY; S1 binding.

14828.synopsis:
Prints the prompts "Source :" at column 11, row 1 and "Destination :" at column 6, row 3,
then falls into ResetSrcDestName.
Entry: none.
Exit: f_SourceName and f_DestName empty; A = 0.

14862.synopsis:
Empties f_SourceName and f_DestName by zeroing their first bytes.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = 0.
Changes: A.

14870.synopsis:
Tests whether the three-byte link at IY is null.
Entry: IY = a link.
Exit: Fz = 1 when it is null; A = OR of its bytes.
Changes: AF.

14880.synopsis:
Reads the three-byte link at IY into BHL (bank in B).
Entry: IY = a link (offset low, offset high, bank).
Exit: B = bank; HL = offset.
Changes: B, HL.

14944.synopsis:
Copies the name of the current device (OS_Nq, NQ_Dev) into f_SourceName (CopyExtended).
Entry: none.
Exit: f_SourceName = device name with its terminator (a byte below $21); DE = the
terminator; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

14954.synopsis:
Copies the name of the current directory (OS_Nq, NQ_Dir) into f_SourceName; falls into
CopyExtended.
Entry: none.
Exit: f_SourceName = directory name with its terminator (a byte below $21); DE = the
terminator; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

15062.synopsis:
The key loop of the View command's dump (ViewFile): sets up the windows and shows the first
128 bytes (ResetCurPos, InitView), then moves the cursor on each key (VFGetKey, which works
out the CRC-32 while no key is pressed). Keys: code $20 (the source says TAB) switches
between the hex and ASCII cursor; left and right move a byte; up and down a line of 16
bytes, scrolling at the edges; SHIFT up and down ($31, $32) 128 bytes; DIAMOND up and down
go to the start and the end of the file.
Entry: f_SourceHandle open on the file; vf_fptr, vf_fsize set (ViewFile).
Exit: Fc = 1; A = RC_Esc when ESC was pressed.

15715.synopsis:
Converts an ASCII hex digit to its value: a code below '@' has 48 subtracted, any other 55.
It does not check the digit. Nothing in the Filer calls it.
Entry: A = '0'-'9' or 'A'-'F'.
Exit: A = 0-15.
Changes: AF.

15810.synopsis: The 16 hex digit characters "0123456789ABCDEF", indexed by CalcHexNibble.

16000.synopsis:
Draws the View command's screen: defines window 2 for the dump (column 1, 73 by 8) and
window 3 for the information panel (column 76, 16 by 8), prints the "VIEW FILE" banner, the
CRC-32 caption, a divider and the key help (start/end, page, cursor, hex/ASCII, quit), then
selects and clears window 2. Called by InitView.
Entry: none.

116.synopsis:
FlashStore's main command loop. It draws the command and file windows and the right-hand
window (file card statistics when the bar is in the menu window, browse help when it is in
the file window), pushes its own address as the return address of every command, and then
reads keys until ESC leaves the application.
1. Shows the active bar (DisplBar), reads a key (rdch) and removes the bar again; a read
error retries.
2. Polls the current slot's file card watermark (PollFileCardWatermark); when the file area
disappeared (Fc = 1) or changed (Fz = 1) it redraws the command and file windows and the
statistics.
3. Dispatches the key: ESC jumps to suicide; the command shortcuts (catalogue, save, fetch,
backup, restore, format, select card, erase, default RAM, file view, file area copy) jump to
their commands; the cursor keys move the menu bar (rows 1 to 7, wrapping) or the file bar;
left and right switch between the menu and file windows; ENTER (or 'F') runs the menu bar's
command or fetches the selected file; DEL or 'D' marks a file deleted, 'C' copies, 'V' views
a file and 'M' views bank memory. Other keys are ignored.
Entry: (MenuBarPosn), (barMode), (curslot) set up by the initialisation.
Exit: never returns to its caller while running; ESC leaves through suicide.

580.synopsis:
Reads the bar mode: whether the cursor bar is in the menu window or in the file window.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = (barMode); Fz = 1 when the bar is in the menu window, Fz = 0 (A = $FF) when it is
in the file window; Fc = 0.
Changes: AF.

609.synopsis:
Toggles the cursor bar in the active window: the 17-character menu bar on row (MenuBarPosn)
of the command window, or the 53-character file bar on row (FileBarPosn) of the file window.
The bar is drawn by XOR, so the main loop calls it once to show it and once to remove it.
Entry: (barMode), (MenuBarPosn), (FileBarPosn).
Changes: BC, HL.
Keeps: AF.

615.synopsis:
Entry inside DisplBar, the menu window case: selects window 1 (SelectMenuWindow), places the
cursor at column 1 of row (MenuBarPosn) with VduCursor and toggles the menu bar (MenuBar).
It ends with POP AF, so it is entered only from DisplBar with AF pushed.
Entry: AF on the stack; (MenuBarPosn) = row of the menu bar.
Changes: BC, HL.
Keeps: AF.

661.synopsis:
VDU sequence (1,"2H1"): selects window 1, the command window, for the menu bar. Sent by
DisplMenuBar.

666.synopsis:
VDU sequence: selects window 2, the file window, and switches its cursor and vertical
scrolling off (1,"2H2", 1,"2-C", 1,"2-S"). Sent by DisplBar for the file bar.

679.synopsis:
VDU sequence that draws the menu bar: reverse video on, the attribute applied by XOR over 17
characters from the cursor (1,"2E",32+17), reverse video off. Sending it twice removes the
bar again.

692.synopsis:
VDU sequence that draws the file bar: reverse video on, the attribute applied by XOR over 53
characters from the cursor (1,"2E",32+53), reverse video off.

705.synopsis:
Draws the command window and its menu, like dispcw, and keeps AF.
Entry: (curslot) = current slot.
Keeps: AF.

711.synopsis:
Draws the command window (window 1, 17 x 8 at the left, banner "COMMANDS") with GN_Win from
CmdWindowDef and writes the seven menu entries (menu_msg). When the card in the current slot
has no write or erase support (SlotWriteSupport returns Fc = 1), it greys out SAVE TO CARD
and BACKUP FROM RAM (grey_wrercmds).
Entry: (curslot) = current slot.
Changes: AF, C (other registers through SlotWriteSupport not traced).

801.synopsis:
Clears the whole application window area: redefines window 1 as the full 94 x 8 area and
clears it (winbackground).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.

808.synopsis:
Writes a null-terminated string and a newline (GN_Sop, GN_Nln).
Entry: HL = local pointer to the string.
Keeps: AF.

817.synopsis:
Greys the whole screen area by defining window 8 over it and switching grey on there
(grey_msg); used before a pop-up window is drawn.
Entry: none.
Keeps: HL.

826.synopsis:
Removes the grey from the whole screen area (ungrey_msg), the reverse of greyscr.
Entry: none.
Keeps: HL.

835.synopsis:
Clears window 2, the main window on the right of the command window (clsvdu).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

844.synopsis:
Reads a key with OS_In. An extended key (a 0 code first) is read as its second code, and an
escape condition is returned as the ESC key.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = key code (IN_ESC when ESC was pressed).
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from OS_In (for example RC_SUSP after pre-emption).
Changes: AF.

863.synopsis:
Waits for a key with OS_Sr SR_PWT (page wait), repeating the wait when it returns RC_SUSP.
An extended key (a 0 code first) is read as its second code with OS_In.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = key code.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code from OS_Sr.
Changes: AF.

881.synopsis:
Asks a yes/no question. It runs the routine at HL, which displays the question, then shows
the current answer (the message at DE) and reads keys: 'Y' selects Yes, any other key No,
ENTER accepts the answer shown and ESC aborts. Keys in the input buffer are purged first and
pre-emption is ignored.
Entry: HL = routine that displays the question (it returns into yesno); DE = default answer,
yes_msg or no_msg.
Exit: Fc = 0; Fz = 1 for Yes, Fz = 0 for No or ESC.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

959.synopsis:
Switches the VDU to centre justification (centerjustify).
Entry: none.
Keeps: HL.

968.synopsis:
Switches the VDU back to normal (left) justification (leftjustify).
Entry: none.
Keeps: HL.

986.synopsis:
VDU text of the command window's menu: selects window 1, grey off, tiny font on, then the
seven entries at rows 0 to 6 (TOGGLE FILE VIEW, SELECT CARD, SAVE TO CARD, FETCH FROM CARD,
BACKUP FROM RAM, RESTORE TO RAM, DEFAULT RAM), each placed with 1,"3@",x,y; cursor off.
Written by dispcw.

1139.synopsis:
VDU sequence that greys out the SAVE TO CARD (row 2) and BACKUP FROM RAM (row 4) entries of
the command window over 17 characters each, then switches grey off. Sent by dispcw when the
card in the current slot cannot be written.

1170.synopsis:
VDU sequence: defines window 8 at (0,0), 94 x 8 (1,"6#8"), selects it and greys it
(1,"2G+"). Sent by greyscr.

1187.synopsis:
VDU sequence: defines window 8 at (0,0), 94 x 8, selects it and removes the grey (1,"2G-").
Sent by ungreyscr.

1204.synopsis: VDU sequence sent by cls: clears window 2 (1,"2C2"), then 1,'S' and a form feed (12).

1212.synopsis:
VDU sequence sent by ClearWindowArea: defines window 1 at (0,0), 94 x 8 (1,"7#1") and clears
it (1,"2C1").

1226.synopsis:
VDU sequence that starts a window bar under the banner: tiny, underline and reverse on,
centre justification and the cursor at (0,0). Sent by wbar before the caption.

1242.synopsis:
VDU sequence that ends a window bar: cursor at (0,0), the attributes applied over 53
characters (1,"2A",85), tiny, underline and reverse off, normal justification. Sent by wbar
after the caption.

1262.synopsis: Message "Last file failed.", null-terminated; shown by the fetch and copy commands.

1280.synopsis:
The "Yes" answer of yesno: CR, cursor on, " Yes" and three backspaces, null-terminated.
yesno compares DE with this address to tell Yes from No.

1293.synopsis: The "No" answer of yesno: CR, cursor on, " No " and three backspaces, null-terminated.

1306.synopsis:
VDU text of the resume prompt: selects window 2, centre justification, flash and tiny on,
"PRESS SPACE OR ENTER TO RESUME" with the key symbols, attributes and cursor off, normal
justification and CR LF. Written by ResSpace.

1356.synopsis: VDU sequence (1,"3-SC"): no vertical scrolling and no blinking cursor in the window.

1382.synopsis: VDU sequence (1,"2JC"): centre justification. Sent by VduEnblCntrJstfy.

1387.synopsis: VDU sequence (1,"2JN"): normal (left) justification. Sent by VduEnblNrmlJstfy.

1397.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the command window: window 1 with bars, shelf brackets and banner
(1 | 128), at (0,0), 17 wide and 8 high, banner "COMMANDS". Used by dispcw.

1404.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the main window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and banner (2
| 128), at (19,0), 53 wide and 8 high; the banner pointer is 0, so the caller gives it in
DE. Used by DispMainWindow.

1916.synopsis:
Entry inside DisplayCard (also called by FileEpromStatistics): appends the card size, A x 16
followed by 'K', to the VDU cache at (vdubufptr).
Entry: A = size of the card in 16K banks; (vdubufptr) = end of the VDU cache.
Exit: (vdubufptr) advanced past the text.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL.

1938.synopsis:
Appends the free space of the current slot's file area, in K followed by 'K', to the VDU
cache at (vdubufptr). The free bytes come from OS_Epr EP_FreSp; the value written is the
quotient of the bytes / 1024 (GN_D24) plus one.
Entry: (curslot) = slot; (vdubufptr) = end of the VDU cache.
Exit: (vdubufptr) advanced past the text.
Changes: AF, DE.
Keeps: BC, HL.

1972.synopsis:
Lets the user choose a slot in the card selection window: the flashing bar under the current
card box moves with cursor left and right (wrapping between 0 and 3), keys 0 to 3 select a
slot directly, ENTER accepts the slot under the bar and ESC aborts. Other keys are ignored.
Entry: (curslot) = slot of the bar at the start.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1, (curslot) = selected slot (0 to 3).
Error: Fc = 1 when ESC was pressed.
Changes: AF, HL.

2070.synopsis:
Shows the flashing reverse menu bar under the current slot's card box: HL = MenuBarOn and
jumps into the card selection's DisplMenuBar ($C7F8).
Entry: (curslot) = slot.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF, BC.

2075.synopsis:
Removes the menu bar under the current slot's card box: HL = MenuBarOff and jumps into the
card selection's DisplMenuBar ($C7F8).
Entry: (curslot) = slot.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF, BC.

2374.synopsis:
Appends a 16-bit number in decimal to the VDU cache at (vdubufptr): converts it to text in
buf1 (IntAscii) and copies it with CacheVduString.
Entry: DE = number.
Exit: (vdubufptr) advanced past the digits; HL = end of the digits in buf1.
Changes: BC, HL.
Keeps: AF, DE.

2480.synopsis: Message "No Flash Cards found in slots 1-3." between bold toggles (1,"B"), null-terminated.

2519.synopsis: VDU prefix of a cursor move (1,"3@"); CacheVduCursor follows it with X+32 and Y+32.

2523.synopsis:
VDU text of a card box's top line: the top left corner (1,"2*C"), 12 horizontal lines
(1,"2*E") and the top right corner (1,"2*F"), null-terminated. Drawn by DrawCardBox.

2580.synopsis:
VDU text of a card box's middle line: the left T-section (1,"2*K"), 12 horizontal lines and
the right T-section (1,"2*N"), null-terminated.

2637.synopsis:
VDU text of a card box's bottom line: the bottom left corner (1,"2*I"), 12 horizontal lines
and the bottom right corner (1,"2*L"), null-terminated.

2694.synopsis: VDU text of a card box's side: one vertical line (1,"2*J"), null-terminated.

2699.synopsis:
VDU text of the AMD logo: defines user characters J, K, L and M (each 1,138,'=',char and 8
pixel rows) and displays each after its definition (1,"2?",char); null-terminated.

2764.synopsis:
VDU text of the Intel logo: defines user characters N, O, P and Q (8 pixel rows each) and
displays each after its definition; null-terminated.

2829.synopsis:
VDU text of the padlock symbol: defines user character Z (8 pixel rows) and displays it
between two spaces; null-terminated.

2930.synopsis: Card label "EPROM " in tiny font, null-terminated.

2941.synopsis: Card label "FLASH " in tiny font, null-terminated.

2952.synopsis: Card label "RAM " in tiny font, null-terminated.

2961.synopsis: Text " FREE " in tiny font, null-terminated.

2989.synopsis: Text "NO FILE AREA" in tiny font, null-terminated.

3015.synopsis: Text "EMPTY SLOT" in tiny font, then tiny off; null-terminated.

3034.synopsis: VDU sequence: no vertical scrolling and no cursor (1,"3-SC"), then tiny font on.

3044.synopsis:
The card selection's SelectMenuWindow: selects window 2 and switches its cursor off
(1,"2H2", 1,"2-C"). Sent by its DisplMenuBar before the bar is placed.

3053.synopsis:
VDU sequence that shows the card selection bar: flash and reverse on (1,"4+F+R") and the
attributes applied over 3 characters (1,"2A",32+3). Sent by ShowMenuBar.

3064.synopsis:
VDU sequence that removes the card selection bar: flash and reverse off (1,"4-F-R") and the
attributes applied over 3 characters. Sent by RemoveMenuBar.

3075.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the card selection window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and
banner (2 | 128), at (16,0), 56 wide and 8 high; the banner pointer is 0, so the caller
gives it in DE.

3082.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the help window on the right: window 3 with left and right bars
only (3 | 64), at (75,0), 18 wide and 8 high. Used by DispHelpText.

3229.synopsis:
Asks OZ whether slot A holds a RAM device (OS_Nq Nq_Mfp).
Entry: A = slot number.
Exit: Fc = 0, a RAM device: A = total banks of the RAM card; DE = free pages (256 bytes).
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_ONF when the slot has no RAM device.
Changes: AF, DE.
Keeps: BC, HL.

3304.synopsis:
Text ":RAM.", null-terminated: the device name prefix that GetDefaultRamDevice copies before
the slot number.

3310.synopsis: Message CR LF " Select RAM device." CR LF, null-terminated.

3334.synopsis:
Message shown under the RAM device prompt: " Use keys 0-3 or <diamond>J to toggle. ENTER to
select.", with VDU symbol codes, null-terminated. Shown by DefaultRamCommand, the backup
command and the copy command before SelectRamDevice.

3406.synopsis:
Body of FileEpromStatistics: fills the file statistics window for the current slot.
1. Builds the window banner "SLOT n" at buf1 from slot_bnr; slot 1 is set left, slot 3
right, the others centred.
2. Asks OS_Epr (EP_Req) for a file area in the slot; without one it goes to no_filearea.
3. Counts the files (FilesAvailable), reads the free space (EP_FreSp) into (free) and the
active and deleted space (EP_TotSp) into (active), (deleted) and their sum (total).
4. Opens the window (InitWindow) and shows the card type (the flash chip's text, or the UV
EPROM size), the file area size (DisplayEpromSize), the free and used bytes, the counts of
saved and deleted files, and the free space bar (DispFreeSpaceBar).
Entry: (curslot) = slot.
Exit: (file), (fdel), (free), (active), (deleted), (total) updated.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

3453.synopsis:
Entry inside dispstats, taken when the slot has no file area or its free space cannot be
read: opens the file statistics window (InitWindow) and shows "No File Area" (nofepr_msg).
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, HL.

3680.synopsis:
Shows the size of the current slot's file area at (1,1) of the statistics window, in tiny
text: the size in K followed by "K FILE AREA". It keeps the size in 16K banks at
(bytesperline), where FillFreeSpaceBar picks it up.
Entry: (curslot) = slot; the slot holds a file area.
Exit: (bytesperline) = size of the file area in 16K banks.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

3756.synopsis:
Shows the number in DE in decimal at the cursor (IntAscii, GN_Sop).
Entry: DE = number.
Changes: BC, HL.

3899.synopsis:
Draws the deleted and the active space of the file area into the free space bar's UDG
characters. It divides the file area's size by 106 to get the bytes one vertical line of the
bar stands for, draws the deleted space as stippled lines from line 1, then the active space
as filled lines after them (DispBarLine).
Entry: (bytesperline) = size of the file area in 16K banks; (deleted), (active) = 24-bit
byte counts; (FreeSpaceBar) = base of the bar's UDGs, bound into segment 1.
Exit: (bytesperline) = bytes per bar line.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4021.synopsis:
ORs the pixel mask in C into the UDG byte at (HL): one pixel of a vertical bar line.
Entry: C = pixel mask; HL = UDG byte.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4060.synopsis:
Text "FILE AREA" followed by the VDU code that turns tiny text off, null-terminated.
DisplayEpromSize shows it after the size.

4074.synopsis:
Banner text for the file statistics window: the VDU code for centred text followed by "SLOT
". dispstats copies its first 9 bytes to buf1, changes the justify letter for slots 1 and 3
and adds the slot digit.

4084.synopsis: Text "FREE", null-terminated: follows the free space in the statistics window.

4089.synopsis: Text "USED", null-terminated: follows the used space in the statistics window.

4094.synopsis: Text " FILES SAVED", null-terminated: follows the count of active files.

4107.synopsis: Text " FILES DELETED", null-terminated: follows the count of deleted files.

4122.synopsis:
Message for a slot without a file area: two new lines, then "No File Area" centred and
flashing; it ends by restoring normal justification and turning flashing and the cursor off.
Shown by no_filearea.

4234.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the file statistics window (InitWindow): window 3 with bars,
brackets and a banner (byte $83), at X = $4A, Y = 0, 18 wide and 8 high; the banner pointer
is 0, so the banner is the dynamic one passed in DE (buf1).

4262.synopsis:
Entry inside DispFilesWindow: clears the file area window and lists up to 7 file entries
(DisplayFile), starting with the window's top entry at (WindowFilePtr). Reached by
MoveToFirstFile and at the end of the page up and page down moves.
Entry: (WindowFilePtr) = top file entry of the window.
Exit: Fc = 0 when 7 lines were shown; Fc = 1 when the end of the list was reached ("END"
shown).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL; (linecnt).

4300.synopsis:
Sends norm_sq (tiny and grey text off) to the window: the attributes for an active file
entry.
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

4305.synopsis:
Sends tiny_sq to the window: tiny, grey text, a grey "DEL" mark, then grey off; the
attributes for a deleted file entry.
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

4310.synopsis:
Sends the VDU code for right-justified text to the window.
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

4315.synopsis:
Sends the VDU code for normal, left-justified text to the window; falls into the shared
output code (dispsq).
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.
Keeps: AF.

4324.synopsis:
Shows the browse keys help (browsehelp) in the right-hand help window (DispHelpText): shown
while the cursor is in the file window.
Entry: none.
Keeps: HL.

4568.synopsis:
Loop inside MoveFileBarPageUp, also called by MoveToLastFile: moves the file cursor up C
entries through the file entry cache, making each new entry the window's top entry too, then
redraws the window (DispFiles). It stops early at the top of the list.
Entry: C = entries to move up; DE = current entry in the cache (from CacheFileEntries);
(CursorFilePtr) = current entry.
Exit: C = entries left of the C asked for (source comment); (CursorFilePtr), (WindowFilePtr)
updated.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

4769.synopsis:
Reads the random ID of the current slot's file area header (at $3FF8 of the header bank) and
the file area's size: the two make the card's watermark. Part of PollFileCardWatermark.
Entry: (curslot) = slot.
Exit: Fc = 0: DEBC = random ID; A = size of the file area in 16K banks.
Error: Fc = 1, no file area in the slot.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, BC', DE', HL' (it swaps the register sets).

4789.synopsis:
Clears the 5-byte watermark (random ID and size of the last seen file area) to zero. It
leaves the flags alone, so PollFileCardWatermark's Fc = 1 survives it.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = 0; HL = 0; (watermark) = 0.
Keeps: F, BC, DE.

5152.synopsis:
Called by CacheFileEntries for each cached entry when it caches only up to the current
entry: compares BHL with the entry at (IX+0..2) (flentry). When they match, it drops its
return address and leaves CacheFileEntries with Fc = 0 and the cache ending at this entry;
otherwise it returns.
Entry: BHL = file entry; IX = flentry, the entry to stop at.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL (when not equal).

5178.synopsis:
Stores the 3-byte file entry pointer BHL at (DE) in the order L, H, B, and advances DE.
Entry: BHL = file entry; DE = cache slot.
Exit: DE = DE + 3.
Keeps: AF, BC, HL.

5205.synopsis:
Entry inside GetPrevCachedFilePtr: reads the cached file entry at (DE) into BHL. An all-zero
entry marks either end of the cached list.
Entry: DE = cache slot.
Exit: Fc = 0: BHL = file entry.
Error: Fc = 1, BHL = 0: beyond the end of the list.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE.

5385.synopsis:
Start of the file area window's banner, "FILE AREA - CURSOR SELECTS " (no terminator):
FileAreaBannerText copies it and appends allfiles_banner or savedfiles_banner.

5412.synopsis:
End marker of filearea_banner, used to compute its length, and the start of allfiles_banner,
"SAVED & DELETED FILES" (no terminator), the banner ending while deleted files are shown.

5433.synopsis:
End marker of allfiles_banner, and the start of savedfiles_banner, "ONLY SAVED FILES" (no
terminator), the banner ending while only active files are shown.

5449.synopsis:
End marker of savedfiles_banner, and the start of norm_sq: the VDU code turning tiny and
grey text off, null-terminated, sent by NormalAttrText.

5455.synopsis:
VDU string sent by TinyAttrText before a deleted file entry: tiny and grey on, "DEL", grey
off; null-terminated.

5468.synopsis:
Marker shown after the last file entry: grey off, then " END " in tiny, underlined, reverse
text; null-terminated. Shown by DisplayFile.

5490.synopsis:
VDU code 1, SD_UP (stdio.def: scroll upwards), null-terminated; MoveFileBarUp sends it
before drawing a new top line.

5493.synopsis:
VDU code 1, SD_DWN (stdio.def: scroll downwards), null-terminated; MoveFileBarDown sends it
before drawing a new bottom line.

5630.synopsis:
Writes the catalogue line for one file entry to the listing file: an "F " (active) or "d "
(deleted) mark, the file name padded with spaces, the size right-justified, and a CR; the
54-byte line goes out through WriteLine (OS_Mv).
Entry: Fz = 0 active, Fz = 1 deleted (from EP_Stat); BHL = file entry; name at buffer+2; IX
= file handle.
Changes: AF, DE; (flen).
Keeps: BC, HL.

5707.synopsis:
Puts the mark "F " (active file) at buffer for CatalogueFile; falls into the shared store
(dispsq). The flags are left alone.
Entry: none.
Exit: DE = buffer + 1.
Changes: A, DE.

5711.synopsis:
Puts the mark "d " (deleted file) at buffer for CatalogueFile. The flags are left alone.
Entry: none.
Exit: DE = buffer + 1.
Changes: A, DE.

5728.synopsis:
Copies the default listing file name, "/filearea.pdd" and its terminator, to (DE), after the
RAM device name that GetDefaultRamDevice wrote.
Entry: DE = destination.
Exit: DE = past the terminator; BC = 0.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

5737.synopsis:
Base banner of the catalogue command's window, "CATALOGUE FILES [" and a terminator, passed
to FileAreaBannerText with its length (catlg_banner_end - catlg_banner).

5755.synopsis:
End marker of catlg_banner, and the start of catlg_msg: " List Catalogue to PipeDream file."
after a new line, null-terminated.

5792.synopsis:
Prompt " Filename: " with the cursor turned on, null-terminated: the catalogue command's
file name prompt.

5808.synopsis: Message " Catalogue written to file.", null-terminated.

5836.synopsis:
Default name of the catalogue file, "/filearea.pdd", null-terminated; copied by
GetDefaultListingFilename.

5850.synopsis:
PipeDream document header written at the start of a catalogue file (20 bytes): "%OP%BON",
CR, "%CO:A,60,60%", a single 60-character column without borders.

6115.synopsis:
After a file was saved, refreshes the file statistics window (FileEpromStatistics) when Fc =
0, then selects window 2 again (filewindow).
Entry: Fc = 0 to refresh the statistics.
Keeps: AF, HL.

6129.synopsis:
Checks that the current slot can take new files: the card must support writing
(SlotWriteSupport) and hold a file area (OS_Epr EP_Req). On failure it shows the error
(DispIntelSlotErr or disp_no_filearea_msg).
Entry: (curslot) = slot.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1: file area found and writable.
Error: Fc = 1 or Fz = 0, the message was shown.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL.

6147.synopsis:
Ends the save, restore and copy commands: shows "n file saved." ("files" unless n is 1)
centred, waits for SPACE (ResSpace) and resets the file bar to the first file
(InitFirstFileBar).
Entry: (savedfiles) = count.
Keeps: AF, HL.

6204.synopsis:
Adds 1 to the count of saved files at (savedfiles).
Entry: none.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

6484.synopsis:
Wildcard "//*" and its terminator: the backup command appends it to the chosen RAM device
name, making ":RAM.n//*" (every file on the device).

6488.synopsis:
VDU code selecting window 2, null-terminated: sent by UpdateFileAreaStats to return to the
main window.

6493.synopsis: Banner "SAVE FILES TO FILE CARD AREA", null-terminated: the save command's window.

6522.synopsis:
Message " (Wildcards allowed)." after a new line, null-terminated: shown by the save
command.

6546.synopsis:
Prompt " Filename: " with the cursor turned on, null-terminated: used by the save, fetch and
delete commands.

6562.synopsis:
Prompt " Overwrite all files?" between new lines, null-terminated: asked by the save,
restore and copy commands.

6588.synopsis: Text ".", null-terminated; nothing in the FlashStore source refers to it.

6590.synopsis:
Banner "SAVING TO FILE CARD AREA ...", null-terminated; nothing in the FlashStore source
refers to it.

6619.synopsis:
Text " file", null-terminated: DispFilesSaved shows it after the count, adding "s" for any
count but 1.

6625.synopsis: Text " saved." and CR, LF, null-terminated: ends DispFilesSaved's message.

6635.synopsis:
Message "File not saved properly - will be re-saved." and CR, LF, null-terminated: shown
when saving a file to the card fails with a write error.

6681.synopsis: Prompt " File already exists in File Card. Overwrite?" after a CR, null-terminated.

6922.synopsis:
Step inside the fetch dialog (QuickFetchFile, FindFileToFetch) once the user has entered the
destination name at buffer: asks before overwriting an existing file (PromptOverWrFile),
expands the name (GN_Fex), creates the RAM file, fetches the file entry into it (OS_Epr
EP_Fetch) and closes it. On an error it deletes the new file and reports the error (GN_Err);
falls into DispCompletedMsg on success.
Entry: name at buffer; (fbnk), (fadr) = file entry.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

7009.synopsis:
Shows "Completed." centred and waits for SPACE (DispErrMsg); ends the fetch and copy
commands.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1.
Changes: AF, HL.

7231.synopsis:
Shows the 16-bit number in HL in decimal at the cursor (IntAscii, GN_Sop).
Entry: HL = number.
Changes: BC, HL.

7280.synopsis:
Converts a value of 0-15 in A to its hexadecimal digit, "0"-"9" or "A"-"F". Used by
Int32Hex.
Entry: A = 0-15.
Exit: A = ASCII digit.
Changes: AF.

7318.synopsis:
Warning "WARNING: File is marked as deleted" in flashing reverse text, null-terminated:
shown before fetching a deleted file entry.

7366.synopsis:
Message " Enter filename (* and ? wildcards may be used)." after a new line,
null-terminated: shown by the fetch and delete commands.

7417.synopsis:
Text " :RAM.", null-terminated: DisplayFreeRamDevs shows it before each RAM device's slot
digit.

7424.synopsis:
Text "Saved to " with the cursor turned on, null-terminated: shown before the name of the
fetched RAM file.

7438.synopsis: Message "Completed." and CR, LF, null-terminated: shown by DispCompletedMsg.

7451.synopsis:
Prompt " Save to: " in bold after a CR, null-terminated: the fetch command's destination
name prompt.

7467.synopsis:
Message "File not found in File Area.", null-terminated: shown when the fetch command finds
no such file entry.

7496.synopsis: Text " bytes ", null-terminated: DispInt returns it as the unit for values below 1K.

7504.synopsis: Text "File size = ", null-terminated: shown by DisplayFileSize.

7517.synopsis: Text "CRC-32 = ", null-terminated; nothing in the FlashStore source refers to it.

7527.synopsis:
Text " = ", null-terminated: DisplayFreeRamDevs shows it between a RAM device's name and its
free space.

7531.synopsis:
String: "free", CR LF, 0. DispFreeRamDevs prints it after the free space of each RAM device
in the Fetch command's list.

8484.synopsis:
Converts an upper-case ASCII hex digit ('0'-'9', 'A'-'F') into its value 0-15.
ViewBankMmryCmd uses it on the two digits of the bank number the user typed.
Entry: A = ASCII hex digit.
Exit: A = digit value.
Changes: AF.

8579.synopsis:
Table of 16 ASCII characters "0123456789ABCDEF": the hex digit for each value 0-15, indexed
by CalcHexNibble.

9049.synopsis:
String: CR LF, " Enter memory bank number to view (hexadecimal).", 0. The prompt of
ViewBankMmryCmd.

9100.synopsis:
String: cursor on (1,"2+C") and " Memory Bank: ", 0. The input label ViewBankMmryCmd prints
before the bank number is typed.

9119.synopsis: String: "VIEW FILE", 0. The banner MemDump shows when ViewFileEntryCmd views a file entry.

9129.synopsis:
String: "VIEW MEMORY", 0. The banner of ViewBankMmryCmd's window and of its memory dump
view.

9265.synopsis:
Shows the file entry's name in bold (DispBoldFilename, through the buffer) and asks "Mark
file as deleted?" with No as the default (yesno).
Entry: BHL = file entry.
Exit: Fz = 1, the user answered Yes; Fz = 0, No or ESC; BHL = file entry.
Changes: AF, DE.

9319.synopsis:
Entry inside FindToMarkDltd, also called by QuickDeleteFile after a Yes: marks the file
entry as deleted with OS_Epr EP_Delete and reports "File marked as deleted." through
DispErrMsg (waits for SPACE). On failure it reports "Error. File was not marked as deleted."
and then also "File not found." (falls into delfile_notfound).
Entry: BHL = file entry.
Exit: Fc = 0; Fc = 1, A = RC_ESC when ESC answered the message.

9378.synopsis:
String: "File not found.", 0. Shown by delfile_notfound when the name the user typed is not
in the file area.

9394.synopsis:
String: CR LF, " Found", 0. Printed by FindToMarkDltd before the file's name when the file
was found.

9403.synopsis:
String: "Error. File was not marked as deleted.", 0. Shown by delfile_failed when OS_Epr
EP_Delete fails.

9442.synopsis:
String: centre justify on (1,"2JC"), "File marked as deleted.", justify normal (1,"2JN"), 0.
Shown by exec_delete on success.

9474.synopsis:
String: " Mark file as deleted?", CR LF, 0. The question disp_mrkdl_prmpt prints for
ConfirmDelete.

9499.synopsis:
String: bold toggle (1,"B") and a space, 0. Printed by DispBoldFilename before the file
name.

9503.synopsis: String: bold toggle (1,"B"), CR LF, 0. Printed by DispBoldFilename after the file name.

9557.synopsis:
Exit of RstrFlsCmd when the file area holds no active files (FilesAvailable gives Fz = 1):
shows "NO FILES AVAILABLE IN FILE AREA" through DispErrMsg, which waits for SPACE, and
returns from the command.
Exit: as DispErrMsg (Fc = 1, A = RC_ESC when ESC was pressed).
Changes: HL.

9877.synopsis:
Prints " file already exists. Overwrite?" (after a CR) with GN_Sop. Catalogue, copy, fetch
and restore pass it to PromptOverWrite or PromptOverWrFile as the routine that shows the
overwrite question.
Entry: none.
Changes: HL.

9909.synopsis: String: CR LF, " Enter Device/path.", 0. The prompt of RstrFlsCmd for the destination.

9931.synopsis: String: cursor on (1,"2+C") and " Device: ", 0. The input label for the restore destination.

9945.synopsis:
String: "Saving...", CR LF, 0. Printed while a file is restored to RAM, and also used by the
save files command.

9957.synopsis:
String: CR LF, "Wildcards not allowed.", 0. Shown by RstrFlsCmd when the destination path
contains wildcards.

9982.synopsis:
String: CR LF, "Invalid Path", 0. Shown by RstrFlsCmd when GN_Fex cannot expand the
destination path.

9997.synopsis: String: CR, " file already exists. Overwrite?", CR LF, 0. Printed by disp_exis_msg.

10053.synopsis:
Inside CopyFileAreaCmd, reached when FilesAvailable gives Fz = 1 (no active files): shows
"NO FILES AVAILABLE IN FILE AREA" through DispErrMsg, which waits for SPACE, and returns
from the command.
Exit: as DispErrMsg (Fc = 1, A = RC_ESC when ESC was pressed).
Changes: HL.

10158.synopsis:
Checks that files can be written to the destination slot (dstslot) with SlotWriteSupport.
When they cannot, it makes the destination the current slot for a moment, shows the Intel
Flash or EPROM slot message (DispIntelSlotErr, waits for SPACE) and puts the current slot
(curslot) back.
Entry: (dstslot) = destination slot.
Exit: Fc = 0, the destination supports writing.
Error: Fc = 1; A = the current slot number.
Changes: AF, BC.

10498.synopsis:
Compares a slot number with the current slot (curslot), for the destination slot selection
of SelDstntnSlot.
Entry: A = slot number.
Exit: Fz = 1 when it is the current slot; A = E = slot number.
Changes: F, E.

10535.synopsis:
Checks with OS_Epr EP_Req whether the slot holds a file area (a File Card), for the
destination slot selection.
Entry: A = slot number.
Exit: Fz = 1, a file area header was found; Fz = 0, none.
Changes: AF, D, HL.
Keeps: BC, E.

10555.synopsis:
Prints " Copying files from Slot x" with the current slot (curslot) and falls into
DispToSlotStatus, which adds " to Slot y".
Entry: (curslot), (dstslot).

10588.synopsis:
Prints " to Slot y" with the destination slot (dstslot) through disp16bitInt. Ends
DispCopyStatus, and CopyToSlotPrompt calls it for the single file copy question.
Entry: (dstslot) = destination slot.

10646.synopsis: String: "COPY SELECTED FILE TO ANOTHER FILE CARD", 0. The banner of QuickCopyFileCmd.

10686.synopsis:
String: CR LF, " Select File Card.", CR LF, 0. Printed by SelDstntnSlot before the
destination slot is chosen.

10709.synopsis: String: " Copying ", 0. The start of DispCopyStatus's line.

10719.synopsis: String: " Copy", 0. Printed by QuickCopyFileCmd before the destination question.

10725.synopsis:
String: "Only current file card is available.", 0. Shown by single_filearea when there is no
other file card to copy to.

10762.synopsis: String: " Slot ", 0. Printed before a slot number in the copy messages.

10838.synopsis:
Formats the file area in the current slot (curslot), after asking:
1. Clears the greyed screen, updates the statistics (FileEpromSttstcs) and opens the "FORMAT
FILE AREA ON FLASH CARD" window.
2. Looks for a file area with OS_Epr EP_Req. With one, it warns "Re-format File Area in slot
n (All data is lost)."; without one, it says there is no file area for the card's
applications (NoAppFileAreaMsg) or that the Flash Card is empty.
3. Asks "Format (create new) file area in slot n?" (default No) and returns on No.
4. Formats with OS_Fep FEP_FFMT, then resets the file area information (PollFileArea).
5. Shows " File Area formatted." and waits for SPACE; on an error it shows "File Area not
formatted properly!" and resets the watermark (ResetWatermark).
Entry: (curslot) = slot to format.
Exit: Fc = 0, Fz = 1, formatted; Fz = 0, the user answered No or ESC.

11203.synopsis: String: "File Area not formatted properly!", CR LF, 0. Shown by formaterr.

11239.synopsis: String: "FORMAT FILE AREA ON FLASH CARD", 0. The banner of the format command's window.

11270.synopsis:
String: CR LF, flash on (1,"F"), " Formatting File Area ... ", flash off, 0. Printed while
OS_Fep formats the file area.

11303.synopsis: String: CR LF, " File Area formatted.", CR LF, 0. Shown after a successful format.

11329.synopsis:
Table of 2 words for DispSlotErrorMsg: the addresses of reformat1_msg and reformat2_msg,
printed on either side of the slot number.

11333.synopsis:
String: CR LF, bold on (1,"B"), "Re-format File Area in slot ", 0. The first half of the
re-format warning (reformat_msgs).

11366.synopsis:
String: " (All data is lost).", bold off (1,"B"), 0. The second half of the re-format
warning (reformat_msgs).

11389.synopsis:
Table of 2 words for DispSlotErrorMsg: the addresses of filefmt_ask1_msg and
filefmt_ask2_msg, printed on either side of the slot number.

11393.synopsis:
String: cursor on (1,"2+C"), CR, "Format (create new) file area in slot ", 0. The first half
of the format question (filefmt_msgs).

11437.synopsis: String: "? ", 0. The second half of the format question (filefmt_msgs).

11813.synopsis:
Entry inside openfile, taken when GN_Opf fails with RC_ONF (object not found): expands the
filename with GN_Fex, creates the missing directories of its path (createpath) and jumps
back to openfile to create the file again.
Entry: HL = filename (local pointer, B = 0); DE = scratch buffer; C = its size.
Exit: as openfile (Fc = 0, IX = handle of the file opened for output).
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_IVF when the name has wildcards or no file name; Fc = 1, A = error
code of GN_Fex or of a directory that could not be made.

11839.synopsis:
Entry inside createpath, the loop that scans backwards from HL for a '/' separator. At the
separator (found_separator) it ends the path there with a 0, creates the parent levels first
(createpath again while B > 0), makes this level with mkdir and puts the '/' back.
Entry: A = '/'; HL = position to scan back from; B = path levels to create; IY = name.
Exit: Fc = 0, the directory path exists.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Changes: AF, DE, HL.

11860.synopsis:
Creates one directory with GN_Opf OP_DIR, the name being the 0-terminated path at IY, and
frees the returned DOR handle with OS_Dor DR_FRE. A directory that already exists (RC_USE or
RC_EXIS) counts as success.
Entry: IY = directory path name.
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.
Keeps: BC, HL.

11931.synopsis:
Reads the address word at HL, for DispSlotErrorMsg's two-string tables.
Entry: HL = pointer to a word.
Exit: HL = the word; DE = pointer past the word.
Changes: DE, HL.

11937.synopsis:
Shows, bold and centred, "No File Area available on Card in slot n." with the current slot
(DispSlotErrorMsg).
Entry: (curslot) = slot number.
Changes: HL.

11943.synopsis:
Shows, bold and centred, "Flash Card is empty in slot n." with the current slot
(DispSlotErrorMsg).
Entry: (curslot) = slot number.
Changes: HL.

11949.synopsis:
Shows, centred, "File Area not detected in slot n." with the current slot, greys the command
window (DispCmdWindow) and jumps to FileEpromSttstcs to update the file area statistics
window. The commands jump here when the current slot has no file area.
Entry: (curslot) = slot number.

11961.synopsis:
Tells the user there are no files to show, without waiting for a key (DispErrMsgNoWait): "NO
FILES AVAILABLE IN FILE AREA" when the file area has neither active nor deleted files (file)
+ (fdel) = 0, otherwise "NO FILES AVAILABLE IN CURRENT FILE VIEW". The commands jump here
when FilesAvailable gives Fz = 1.
Entry: (file) = active files; (fdel) = deleted files.
Exit: Fz = 1 when the file area holds no files at all.
Changes: DE, HL.

12052.synopsis:
String: CR LF, bold on (1,"B"), "No File Area available on Card in slot ", 0. The first half
of NoAppFileAreaMsg's message (no_appflarea_msgs).

12096.synopsis: String: ".", bold off (1,"B"), 0. The second half of NoAppFileAreaMsg's message.

12100.synopsis:
Table of 2 words for DispSlotErrorMsg: the addresses of empty_flcrd1_msg and
empty_flcrd2_msg, used by dsp_emp_flcr_msg.

12104.synopsis:
String: CR LF, bold on (1,"B"), "Flash Card is empty in slot ", 0. The first half of
dsp_emp_flcr_msg's message.

12137.synopsis: String: ".", bold off (1,"B"), 0. The second half of dsp_emp_flcr_msg's message.

12141.synopsis:
Table of 2 words for DispSlotErrorMsg: the addresses of intlslt_err1_msg and
intlslt_err2_msg, used by DispIntelSlotErr for an Intel Flash Card outside slot 3.

12145.synopsis:
String: CR LF, bold on (1,"B"), "Intel Flash Card found in slot ", 0. The first half of the
Intel Flash slot message (intelslot_msgs).

12181.synopsis:
String: ".", bold off, CR LF, "You can only format file area, save files or", CR LF, "delete
files in slot 3.", CR LF, 0. The second half of the Intel Flash slot message.

12258.synopsis:
Table of 2 words for DispSlotErrorMsg: the addresses of eprmslt_err1_msg and
eprmslt_err2_msg, used by DispIntelSlotErr for an EPROM outside slot 3.

12262.synopsis:
String: CR LF, bold on (1,"B"), "EPROM found in slot ", 0. The first half of the EPROM slot
message (epromslot_msgs).

12287.synopsis:
String: ".", bold off, CR LF, "You can only save files to Eprom in slot 3.", CR LF,
"Further, files or EPROMs cannot be erased in the Z88.", CR LF, 0. The second half of the
EPROM slot message.

12393.synopsis:
Table of 2 words for DispSlotErrorMsg: the addresses of nofilearea1_msg and nofilearea2_msg,
used by disp_no_fra_msg.

12397.synopsis:
String: CR LF, bold on (1,"B"), "File Area not detected in slot ", 0. The first half of
disp_no_fra_msg's message (nofilearea_msgs).

12433.synopsis:
String: ".", CR LF, 0. The second half of disp_no_fra_msg's message. It has no bold toggle,
so the bold switched on by nofilearea1_msg is not switched off here.

12437.synopsis:
String: tiny on (1,"2+T"), "NO FILES AVAILABLE IN FILE AREA", tiny off (1,"2-T"), CR LF, 0.
Shown by no_files and by both no_active_files exits.

12479.synopsis:
String: tiny on (1,"2+T"), "NO FILES AVAILABLE IN CURRENT FILE VIEW", tiny off (1,"2-T"), CR
LF, 0. Shown by no_files when the file area has files but none in the current view.

523.synopsis:
Opens the file named at HL for output: sets the mode to OP_OUT and continues in OpenRead's
common part (skip leading spaces, open with GN_Opf).
Entry: HL = filename (local pointer).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from GN_Opf).
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.
Keeps: BC.

527.synopsis:
Opens the file named at HL for input. Skips leading spaces, then calls GN_Opf with B = 0
(local name), DE = 3 so no explicit name is kept, and C = $FF. OpenWrite enters the same
code with OP_OUT.
Entry: HL = filename (local pointer).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0; HL = first non-space of the name.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from GN_Opf).
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.
Keeps: BC.

551.synopsis:
CLI script ".T>:PRT", CR, ".S", 0: tees the CLI's output to the printer, then ends its
input. DC_Alt starts it with DC_Icl ([]+P) when no CLI is running.

562.synopsis:
CLI script ".T<:RAM.-/K.sgn", CR, ".S", 0: tees keyboard input into the file K.sgn, then
ends its input. DC_Alt starts it with DC_Icl ([]+K) when no CLI is running.

565.synopsis:
Entry inside RedirInKsgn_cli: the filename ":RAM.-/K.sgn", ended by CR. DC_Alt opens it with
OpenWrite to rebind a running CLI's input tee ([]+K).

581.synopsis:
CLI script ".T>:RAM.-/S.sgn", CR, ".S", 0: tees the screen output into the file S.sgn, then
ends its input. DC_Alt starts it with DC_Icl ([]+S) when no CLI is running.

584.synopsis:
Entry inside RedirOutSsgn_cli: the filename ":RAM.-/S.sgn", ended by CR. DC_Alt opens it
with OpenWrite to rebind a running CLI's output tee ([]+S).

889.synopsis:
Forgets the application waiting to be run: clears pIdxRunProcIX and the bank byte of
eIdxRunProc.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = 0.
Changes: AF.

1291.synopsis:
A single zero byte, an empty string. DC_Dq for the default directory returns BHL =
DC_BNK:zero_byte when the Filer process has no associated directory.

1952.synopsis:
Reads the 3-byte link at IY into CDE.
Entry: IY = list node (link at +0..+2: low, high, bank).
Exit: C = bank; DE = address.
Changes: C, DE.

1962.synopsis:
Reads the 3-byte link at IY into BHL.
Entry: IY = list node or list head (link at +0..+2: low, high, bank).
Exit: B = bank; HL = address.
Changes: B, HL.

1972.synopsis:
Fills B bytes from HL with zero.
Entry: HL = start; B = count (0 means 256).
Exit: HL = byte after the block; B = 0; A = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

1978.synopsis:
Returns an error to the caller of a DC call: stores A in the OS frame's A and sets Fc in its
F.
Entry: IY = OS frame; A = error code.
Exit: frame A = error code; frame Fc = 1.
Changes: none.

1986.synopsis:
Loads the caller's HL from the OS frame.
Entry: IY = OS frame.
Exit: HL = caller's HL.
Changes: HL.

1993.synopsis:
Reads a process block's stacked environment, dynamic ID and handle; falls into
GetProcHandle.
Entry: IY = process block (bound).
Exit: BHL = prc_stkProcEnv; C = prc_dynid; DE = prc_hndl.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

2005.synopsis:
Reads a process block's application handle.
Entry: IY = process block (bound).
Exit: DE = prc_hndl.
Changes: DE.

2012.synopsis:
Stores IX as a process block's application handle.
Entry: IY = process block (bound); IX = handle.
Exit: prc_hndl = IX; DE = IX.
Changes: DE.

2200.synopsis:
Tests whether IX is the :INP handle (phnd_Ihn).
Entry: IX = handle.
Exit: Fz = 1 when IX = phnd_Ihn; HL = IX - phnd_Ihn.
Changes: F, BC, HL.

2300.synopsis:
Rebinds one stream of a CLI with RebindStream, then frees the CLI with FreeCli when none of
its six streams is left open.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound in S1); BC = offset of the stream word (cli_instream ...); A =
its CLIS_xxx flag; IX = new handle (0 closes the stream).
Exit: as RebindStream, or as FreeCli when the CLI was freed.

2792.synopsis:
Loads the timeout stored in the CLI block (the BC that DC_In was given).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: BC = cli_argB:cli_argC.
Changes: BC.

2799.synopsis:
Frees every CLI: calls FreeCli until it reports that no CLI is left.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = RC_Eof (from the last FreeCli); no CLI remains.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, IY.

2950.synopsis:
Points HL at the CLI's prefix sequence buffer, used with OS_Isq and OS_Wsq.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: HL = IY + cli_PrefixBuffer.
Changes: BC, HL.

3119.synopsis:
Writes a byte to a stream with OS_Pbt, using the CLI's stored timeout.
Entry: A = byte; IX = handle; IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from OS_Pbt).
Keeps: BC.

3127.synopsis:
Frees the most recently invoked CLI, the head of eIdxCliList.
1. Binds the CLI block into S1 and closes its six streams (RebindStream with IX = 0).
2. Unlinks it from the list and releases the block with OS_Mfr (pIdxMemHandle).
3. Decrements the CLI use count (OS_Cli, CL_DEC).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc and A as OS_Cli returns them; the CLI's bank stays bound in S1.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Eof when no CLI is running.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, IY (IY = eIdxCliList).

3224.synopsis:
Writes CDE as the 3-byte link at IY.
Entry: IY = list node or list head; C = bank; DE = address.
Exit: (IY+0..2) = E, D, C.
Changes: none.

3503.synopsis:
Reads CLI input up to and including the next CR, then clears CLIF_B_NOTBOL (at the start of
a line again).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: Fc = 0; A = CR.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from ReadCliChar).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

3516.synopsis:
Reads the rest of the CLI line as a filename and opens it for input (GetRedirectName,
OpenRead).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

3523.synopsis:
Reads the rest of the CLI line as a filename and opens it for output (GetRedirectName,
OpenWrite).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

3530.synopsis:
Fills the CLI line buffer up to the end of the line (sets CLIF_B_FILLALL, FillCLIBuffer),
then falls into GetLineBuffer to point HL at it.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: HL = cli_LineBuffer in the CLI block; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from FillCLIBuffer).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3538.synopsis:
Points HL at the CLI's line buffer.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: HL = IY + cli_LineBuffer; Fc = 0.
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: DE.

3644.synopsis:
Takes the next character of CLI input: tops up the line buffer with FillCLIBuffer, removes
the first byte and moves the rest down.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: A = C = character; Fc = 0; Fz = 1 when the character is 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from FillCLIBuffer).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE, IX.

3685.synopsis:
Reads the CLI's input stream into the free end of its line buffer with OS_Gbt and the stored
timeout. It reads one byte, or, when CLIF_B_FILLALL is set (it is then cleared), up to a CR
or until the buffer is full. Bytes below $20 other than CR are dropped.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: Fc = 0 (also when the read failed but the buffer holds bytes).
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code when the read failed and the buffer is empty.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX (IX = input stream).

3764.synopsis:
Reads the head of the CLI list, the most recently invoked CLI.
Entry: none.
Exit: BHL = CLI block; Fz = 1 when no CLI is running; A = B or H or L.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: IY.

4081.synopsis:
Filename ":EPR.?/Boot.cli", 0: a Boot.cli in any file area. Index tries it after RamBootCLI
when it is started the first time.

4097.synopsis:
Filename ":RAM.?/Boot.cli", 0: a Boot.cli in any RAM device. Index tries it first when it is
started the first time.

4113.synopsis:
Opens the named file for input (GN_Opf, with a 256-byte explicit name buffer on the stack)
and starts a new CLI that reads it (DC_Icl with BHL = 0, IX = the file). When DC_Icl fails
the file is closed again.
Entry: HL = filename (local pointer).
Exit: Fc = 0 when the CLI was started; when DC_Icl failed, Fc as OS_Cl returns it.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code when the file cannot be opened.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, AF'.

4233.synopsis:
Index's entry after its first run (and after the boot scripts were tried).
1. When an application is marked to start at boot (pIdxAutoRunAppl), clears the mark and
enters it.
2. Otherwise reads the "NAME" mailbox (OS_Sr, SR_RPD) into App_Buff1; when it holds a name,
goes to AskInstall.
3. Otherwise falls into IndexRedraw.
Entry: none.

4273.synopsis:
Redraws Index and falls into MainLoop. When an application ended with an error (IDXF2_ERROR
in ubIdxFlags2), goes to ShowExitError instead. The commands jump here after changing the
display.
Entry: none.

4284.synopsis:
Index's command loop: reads a key with OS_In (marking IDXF1_B_INSIDEOZ while waiting) and
calls MayInitIndex before and after. On an error, RC_Quit exits Index with OS_Bye, RC_Draw
goes to IndexRedraw, anything else reads again. A key goes to main_2.
Entry: none.

4311.synopsis:
Entry inside MainLoop: dispatches a key. '0'-'3' go to cmd_ramcrd_sel, 'Y'/'N'/'y'/'n' to
cmd_insrmv_sel, other plain keys are ignored. A 0 is followed by a command code; codes 1-15
jump through the table at main_3, others are ignored.
Entry: A = key from OS_In.

4384.synopsis:
Table of 15 words: Index's command handlers for command codes 1-15: right, left, up, down,
enter, escape, kill, card, 0 (the purge command, removed), info, install, remove, nq,
update, hard reset. Code 9 would jump to address 0.

4417.synopsis:
Clears IDXF1_B_INSIDEOZ. When IDXF1_B_INIT is set, clears it and rebuilds Index: resets the
selection (InitIndex), rescans the application keys (InitKeys) and redraws (DrawWindow).
Entry: HL = ubIdxPubFlags.
Keeps: AF.

5318.synopsis:
GN_Win block of the APPLICATIONS window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel
banner; X = 0, Y = 0, width 18, height 8; banner text at appl_banner.

5338.synopsis:
GN_Win block of the SUSPENDED ACTIVITIES window: window 3 with bars, shelf brackets and an
8-pixel banner; X = 20, Y = 0, width 56, height 8; banner text at proc_banner.

5366.synopsis:
Selects and clears the application window and lists up to 6 applications from
ubIdxTopApplication on, leaving out Index, each with its key (PrintApp). Stores the count in
ubIdxNApplDisplayed.
Entry: none.

5425.synopsis:
Selects and clears the process window and lists up to 6 suspended processes from
ubIdxTopProcess on (PrintProcess). When the top process no longer exists, restarts from 0
(and resets ubIdxSelectorPos when the process window is active). Stores the count in
ubIdxNProcDisplayed and prints "NONE" when there is none.
Entry: none.

5563.synopsis:
Draws the selection bar: toggles reverse on, applies it over the selected line
(RemoveHighlight) and toggles reverse off again.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC.

5572.synopsis:
Moves to column 0 of the selected line (ubIdxSelectorPos) and applies the current attributes
over it with ApplyA: 50 characters in the application window, 83 in the process window
(ubIdxActiveWindow). With no attribute on, this removes the bar.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC.

5771.synopsis:
Compares the low byte of an application handle with a key table entry.
Entry: IX = application handle; HL = key table entry.
Exit: Fz = 1 when IXL = (HL); A = IXL.
Changes: AF.

5881.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column B, row C of the current window (1, "3@", X, Y).
Entry: B = column; C = row.
Changes: AF.

5898.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column A of the current line (1, "2X", X).
Entry: A = column.
Changes: AF.

5911.synopsis:
Toggles the tiny font (1, "T").
Entry: none.

5931.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to the top left of the current window and clears to the end of the window
(1, "2C", $FE), clearing all of it.
Entry: none.

5944.synopsis:
Selects and initialises window 2, the application window (1, "2I2").
Entry: none.

5952.synopsis:
Selects and initialises window 3, the process window (1, "2I3").
Entry: none.

5960.synopsis:
Scrolls the current window up (1, $FF).
Entry: none.

5966.synopsis:
Applies the toggled display attributes to A characters from the cursor (1, "2A", A).
Entry: A = number of characters.
Keeps: A.

5977.synopsis:
Index command "card" (code 8). Fills CardData, 3 bytes per slot 0-3 (RAM banks, file area
banks, ROM banks): RAM from OS_Nq NQ_Mfp, an application card's size from its header byte at
$3FFC of the top bank (NQ_Slt says BU_ROM), the file area from OS_Epr EP_Req. Then it makes
the card window active (ubIdxActiveWindow = 2) and goes to IndexRedraw.
Entry: none.

6203.synopsis:
GN_Win block of the CARDS window: window 4 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel banner,
drawn as a pop-up on a grey screen; X = 9, Y = 0, width 46, height 8; banner text at
cards_banner.

6216.synopsis:
Prints the rows of the card window for slots 3 down to 0 (GetCardData, DisplayCard).
Entry: CardData filled by cmd_card.
Exit: D = $FF; IY = slot 0's bytes in CardData.

6232.synopsis:
Prints one slot's row of the card window: moves to column 0, row slot + 1, and prints the
ROM size at column 15, the file area at 25 and the RAM at 35 (PrintCardSize).
Entry: D = slot; IY = the slot's 3 bytes in CardData (RAM, file area, ROM banks).
Keeps: DE.

6266.synopsis:
Prints a size in 16K banks as kilobytes at a column: C * 16 in a 4-character field followed
by 'K' (GN_Pdn to the standard output), or " -" when C = 0.
Entry: A = column; C = size in 16K banks.
Keeps: DE.

6331.synopsis:
Clears the current line and prints "Are you sure ? " with the answer in ubIdxYesNo ("Yes" or
"No"), then moves the cursor back onto the answer and switches the cursor on.
Entry: ubIdxYesNo = 'Y'/'y' for yes, anything else for no.
Changes: AF.

6392.synopsis:
Writes the centred "PRESS ESC TO RESUME" line in tiny font (ESC as its key symbol) with
OS_Pout, then turns centring off again. Used by the info, install, remove and update windows
before they wait for ESC.
Entry: none (writes to the current window).

6537.synopsis:
Shows the FreeRAM details of a RAM card: the size column (DispCardSizeClmn), a cleared and
redrawn page map (DispFreeRamMap), the card size and then jumps to the free space text
(bytes and percentage).
Entry: slotno, cardsize and freespace set by GetFreeSpace.

6551.synopsis:
Shows FreeRAM for a slot without a RAM card: clears window 2 and the page map, then selects
and clears window 3 and writes "(None)" there.
Entry: A = error code from GetFreeSpace.
Keeps: AF.

6578.synopsis:
Writes the card size as "(<n>K)" in window 3, where n = cardsize * 16.
Entry: cardsize = size of the card in 16K banks.

6729.synopsis:
Asks OS_Nq NQ_Mfp for the RAM in the slot held in slotno and stores the card size in banks
in cardsize and the free space in bytes (free pages * 256) in freespace.
Entry: slotno = slot number (0-3).
Exit: Fc = 0; cardsize, freespace (32-bit, low word first) set.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Onf when the slot holds no RAM device.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.

6757.synopsis:
Draws the FreeRAM page map: one pixel for each used 256-byte page of the RAM card, each 16K
bank being an 8x8 pixel character block, eight blocks to a row (128K).
1. Binds the card's bottom bank, which holds the allocation table (slot 0: $21), into
segment 1, and the HIRES0 map area (GetMapAddress) into segment 2.
2. For a card below 8 banks it computes a pixel factor by rotating 8 right once per bank
above one; otherwise one pixel per page.
3. Reads the table from $4100 (2 bytes per page, non-zero = used) and plots each used page
(plot_usedpage) while moving the pixel position (update_pixelptr) per pixel.
4. Restores the segment 2 and segment 1 bindings.
Entry: slotno, cardsize.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, AF', BC', DE', HL'.

6851.synopsis:
Plots one pixel of the page map: ORs the column bit D' into the byte at HL' + BC' (the
current row of the current 8x8 block). Works in the alternate set.
Entry: HL' = block base; BC' = row (0-7); D' = column bit; map bound in segment 2.
Changes: none (AF and HL' are kept).

6862.synopsis:
Moves the page map's pixel position one row down in the current 8x8 block; after the eighth
row it calls new_column. Works in the alternate set.
Entry: HL', BC', D', E' = the map position (see DispFreeRamMap).
Changes: F, C', D', E', HL'.

6871.synopsis:
Moves the page map's pixel position to the next pixel column (column bit rotated right);
when the bit leaves the block it calls next_matrix. Then starts again at row 0. Runs with
the alternate set swapped in by update_pixelptr.
Entry: C = 8; D = column bit; HL = block base; E = blocks left in the row.
Exit: C = 0; D = next column bit.

6879.synopsis:
Moves the page map's position to the next 8x8 block: HL += BC (8 bytes on); counts the
blocks of the row in E and reloads it with 8 when a row of eight blocks is done. Runs with
the alternate set swapped in.
Entry: HL = block base; BC = 8; E = blocks left in the row.
Exit: HL = next block; E = blocks left (8 after a full row).

6885.synopsis:
Clears window 2 and writes the size labels beside the page map, right justified: one line
per 128K row with the running card size in K ("128K", "256K", ...), or the card size alone
for a card below 128K.
Entry: cardsize = size of the card in 16K banks.

6940.synopsis:
Inline OS_Pout text inside DispCardSizeClmn: "K ", CR, LF, null, written after each size
label; the code continues after it with the jump back to the label loop.

7010.synopsis:
Selects and clears window 2 with OS_Pout (1,"2C2"). Shared by FreeRAM and the Index's ESC
handling.
Entry: none.

7025.synopsis: The FreeRAM window's banner text: "FREE RAM", null-terminated, named by FreeRamWindowDef.

7034.synopsis:
Index command <>INFO (entry in the command table): shows the SYSTEM INFORMATION window.
1. Gets the :OUT handle (NQ_Ohn) for the number output, opens the window (InfoWdBlock) and
writes the captions OZ, BUILD, MACHINE, TYPE, FREE MEMORY, BATTERY, FREE HANDLES.
2. OZ version and slot (disp_ver); "Z88"; type "expanded" or "unexpanded" from OS_Frm
FA_EOF; battery "good" or "low" from NQ_Btl.
3. Revision (disp_rev) and the build's date and time, assembled in as constants, through
GN_Dei, GN_Pdt and GN_Ptm.
4. Free memory in K (OS_Frm FA_EXT divided by 1024) and free handles (OS_Frm FA_PTR).
5. Sets the active window to 3 (info window, closed by ESC) and jumps to MainLoop.
Entry: none. Does not return: jumps to MainLoop (IX is kept).

7545.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the info windows (SYSTEM INFORMATION and the <>NQ windows):
window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel banner on a greyed screen, at X = 9, Y =
0, 64 wide and 8 high; banner pointer 0, so the banner comes in DE.

7552.synopsis: Banner text of the info window: "SYSTEM INFORMATION", null-terminated.

7571.synopsis:
Writes "rev. " and the OZ revision as 8 hex digits: OS_Nq NQ_Roz returns it in DEBC, written
D, E, B, C with OS_Hout.
Entry: none.

7597.synopsis:
Writes the OZ version as "<major>.<minor>" from the low byte of OS_Frm FA_PTR (high nibble
major, low nibble minor), then " in slot 1" when OS_Ploz says OZ is not running from slot 0.
Entry: none.

7643.synopsis:
The text "unexpanded", null-terminated. cmd_info writes it for an unexpanded Z88 and writes
from 2 bytes on ("expanded") for an expanded one.

7654.synopsis: The text "good", null-terminated: cmd_info's battery state.

7659.synopsis: The text "low", null-terminated: cmd_info's battery state when NQ_Btl reports low.

7663.synopsis:
Index command <>INS (entry in the command table): opens the INSTALL APPLICATION window and
asks for the .APP filename with GN_Sip into App_Buff1 (up to 128 characters). On ENTER it
goes to AskInstall; otherwise it sets the active window to 0 and redraws the Index
(IndexRedraw).
Entry: none. Does not return.

7709.synopsis:
Sets the active window to 4 (install), redraws the install window and shows "Install
<filename>", then asks "Are you sure ?" with Yes as the default (AreYousure) and jumps to
MainLoop; ENTER there runs DoInstall.
Entry: App_Buff1 = filename. Does not return.

7751.synopsis:
Opens the INSTALL APPLICATION window (GN_Win with InstallWdBlock) and defines window 2 as
its text area (58 x 6 at column 13, row 2), selected and cleared.
Entry: none.

7775.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the install window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an
8-pixel banner on a greyed screen, at X = 9, Y = 0, 64 wide and 8 high; banner
InstallBanner.

7782.synopsis: Banner text of the install window: "INSTALL APPLICATION", null-terminated.

7802.synopsis:
Installs an application from RAM files: the .APP header and the .AP0 to .AP6 bank files
named by App_Buff1. Run by ENTER after AskInstall.
1. Unless the answer was 'y', sets window 0 and redraws the Index. Otherwise draws the
install window and saves SP in App_Stack for the error exit.
2. Copies 40 bytes of the .APP file to App_Tag (ci_copyfile) and checks the tag (APF_TAG),
at most 8 banks and no patches; RC_Ftm otherwise.
3. Opens a memory handle (OS_Mop) and allocates an installation handle (OS_Fn FN_AH,
HND_INST) that keeps the memory handle.
4. For each bank entry: works out the pages needed, finds a bank (OS_Fma, even when its
App_Even bit is set), allocates the area (OS_Axm) and loads the .AP<n> file into it
(ci_copyfile); bank, offset page and length go to the Fma table (Fma_AP0, 4 bytes each).
5. Takes the application DOR (App_DOR, or the son pointer at $3FC6 of relative bank 63 when
it is 0), stores it in the installation handle and chains it after the last DOR under the
:APP.- front DOR ($4060 in bank $21).
6. Walks the new DOR chain and translates each DOR's bank numbers (segments, topics,
commands, help, tokens, brother) with ci_TranslateBank, counting the applications.
7. Restores SP, polls the keys again (InitKeys), writes "Installation completed." and waits
for ESC (PressEsc), then jumps to MainLoop.
Error: frees the installation handle, memory and file, stores the error code in
ubIdxErrorCode, sets IDXF2_B_ERROR and redraws the Index. Does not return.

8382.synopsis:
Frees the installation handle: clears App_InstHnd and calls OS_Fn FN_FH with B = HND_INST.
Entry: IX = installation handle.

8395.synopsis:
Closes the install's (or update's) memory handle: clears App_MemHnd and calls OS_Mcl, which
frees the memory allocated through it.
Entry: IX = memory handle.

8404.synopsis:
Closes the install's open file: clears App_FileHnd and calls GN_Cl.
Entry: IX = file handle.
Exit: IX = 0.
Changes: AF, HL, IX.

8414.synopsis:
Tests IX for a null handle.
Entry: IX = handle.
Exit: Fz = 1 when IX = 0, Fz = 0 otherwise.
Changes: AF.

8422.synopsis:
Loads one file of the application being installed into memory: puts the extension character
in A into the third place of App_Buff1's 3-letter extension (which must start with 'A'),
opens the file (GN_Opf), binds bank B into segment 1, reads DE bytes to the offset HL
(OS_Mv) and closes the file.
Entry: A = 'P' or '0'-'7'; B = bank; HL = offset in the bank; DE = length; App_Buff1 =
filename.
Exit: file copied; bank B left bound in segment 1; App_FileHnd = 0.
Error: does not return; jumps to the install's error exit (RC_Ftm for a bad extension).
Changes: AF, DE, HL.
Keeps: BC, IX.

8522.synopsis:
Translates a bank number of an application's DOR from its relative form ($F8-$FF for bank 7
to bank 0 of the application) to the bank allocated for it, read from the first byte of its
4-byte entry in the Fma table (Fma_AP0). Bank 0 is left as it is.
Entry: A = relative bank number.
Exit: A = absolute bank number.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

8544.synopsis:
Index command <>REM (entry in the command table): starts removing the selected application.
Gets its static handle (GetAppByNum) and keeps it in App_RmvHnd; an application that is not
installed (handle below $80) gives RC_Fail, one that runs (DC_Pol with A = $80) gives
RC_Use, both shown through the Index's error flag (IDXF2_B_ERROR) and a redraw. Otherwise
sets the active window to 5, shows "Remove <name>" and asks "Are you sure ?" with No as the
default, then jumps to MainLoop; ENTER there runs DoRemove.
Entry: ubIdxTopApplication + ubIdxSelectorPos = the selected application. Does not return.

8636.synopsis:
Removes an installed application. Run by ENTER after the remove question.
1. Unless the answer was 'y', sets window 0 and redraws the Index.
2. Finds the installation handle whose DOR matches the application's (OS_Nq NQ_Ain, OS_Fn
FN_GH/FN_NH with HND_INST); RC_Fail when none does.
3. When the handle installed several applications, checks with OS_Poll and DC_Pol that none
of them runs (RC_Use otherwise).
4. Lowers the static handle of the processes of later applications by the number removed
(OS_Uash on each stacked process environment).
5. Unchains the DORs from the :APP.- front DOR ($4060 in bank $21), linking the son or the
preceding brother to the DOR after the removed group (GetSmallestBrother).
6. Closes the memory handle (OS_Mcl), frees the installation handle, polls the keys again
(InitKeys), writes "Removal completed." and waits for ESC; then MainLoop.
Error: stores the error code in ubIdxErrorCode, sets IDXF2_B_ERROR, sets window 0 and
redraws the Index. Does not return.

8856.synopsis:
Reads the brother pointer of a DOR: binds the DOR's bank into segment 1, reads its
DOR_BROTHER field and restores segment 1.
Entry: BHL = DOR.
Exit: BHL = brother DOR (0 when there is none).
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE, IY.

8890.synopsis:
Follows the brother chain from a DOR as many times as the installation handle has
applications (ihnd_AppNbOf), giving the DOR that comes after the installed group.
Entry: BHL = first DOR of the group; IX = installation handle.
Exit: BHL = DOR after the group.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE, IY.

9056.synopsis:
Opens the remove window (GN_Win with RemoveWdBlock) and defines window 2 as its text area
(58 x 6 at column 13, row 2), selected and cleared.
Entry: none.

9080.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the remove window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an
8-pixel banner on a greyed screen, at X = 9, Y = 0, 64 wide and 8 high; banner RemoveBanner.
